chapters.title: Unit 1: The Last Sermon of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW)

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Why was Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) called Sadiq and Amin?
    Ans: As a grown-up man, Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) was so honourable and trustworthy that people would call him Al-Sadiq and Al-Amin. Al-Sadiq means the truthful one and Al-Amin means the trustworthy one, because he always spoke the truth and people could fully trust him.
  • Q: Q2. Why is Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) called Rehmatul-lil-Aalamin?
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) is called Rehmatul-lil-Aalamin, a mercy for all the worlds, because his teaching was not for one tribe or nation only. His words in the Last Sermon were directed to the entire humanity, and he taught everyone to be kind and just to all, so his message is a mercy and guidance for the whole of mankind.
  • Q: Q3. What was the impact of Hazrat Muhammad's (peace be upon him) personality on people?
    Ans: His personality had a deep impact on people. Because he was honourable and trustworthy, people called him Al-Sadiq and Al-Amin and listened to him with full attention. At the Last Sermon, when he asked the assembled people, "Have I fulfilled my mission?", the hundreds of pilgrims replied together, "In truth you have," which shows how completely people believed in him and accepted his message.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions:

  • Q: Q1. Describe a few character traits of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him).
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) was honourable and trustworthy, so people called him Al-Sadiq and Al-Amin. He was firm and steadfast: he spared no effort in preaching the true religion Islam and suffered great hardships, but nothing could move him from his chosen path. He was also kind and just to everyone, as his Last Sermon teaches kindness to wives, servants and all people.
  • Q: Q2. As a Muslim how should we treat our servants?
    Ans: In the Last Sermon, Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that we should feed and clothe our slaves and servants with such food as we eat ourselves and with such clothes as we wear ourselves. If they commit a fault which we find hard to forgive, we should let them go away and not treat them harshly. In short, we must be kind and just to them.
  • Q: Q3. When did Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) perform his last Hajj? Where did he give his last Hajj sermon?
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) performed his last Hajj and delivered his last sermon (Khutbah) on the ninth of ZulHijjah, the 12th and last month of the Islamic year, 10 years after Hijrah, the migration from Makkah to Madinah. He gave the sermon in the Uranah Valley of Mount Arafat.
  • Q: Q4. What makes a man superior to others?
    Ans: According to the Last Sermon, there is no preference for the Arab over the non-Arab or the non-Arab over the Arab, and a white has no superiority over black nor does a black have any superiority over white. Only the goodness and piety of a man makes him superior to others.
  • Q: Q5. What does the last sermon of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) teach us?
    Ans: The Last Sermon teaches us that the lives and property of all people are a sacred trust and that everyone will appear before Allah and give an account of all his actions. It teaches us to beware of Satan, to treat wives with kindness and affection, to be faithful and not commit sins, and never to take usury (interest), which Allah has forbidden. It teaches that every Muslim is truly a brother to every other Muslim and that no one is superior because of race or colour, but only because of goodness and piety. It also teaches us to worship Allah, say the five prayers daily, fast during Ramadan, give Zakat and perform Hajj if we can afford it, and to follow the Qur'an and the Sunnah so that we never go astray.
  • Q: Q6. As a Muslim how should we treat women?
    Ans: In the Last Sermon, Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "You have rights over your wives and your wives have rights over you. Treat them with kindness and affection." So, as Muslims, we must treat women, especially our wives, with kindness and affection, respect their rights, and be faithful to each other and not commit sins.

Comprehension — B. Choose the correct option.

  • Q: Q1. What is the basis of superiority in the eyes of Allah?
    Options: earning wealth / fair/white skin / good parentage / goodness and piety
    Ans: goodness and piety
  • Q: Q2. "There is no preference for Arab over the non-Arab". Here the word "preference" means
    Options: liking for / disliking for / precedent / hatred for
    Ans: liking for
  • Q: Q3. Allah revealed to him the true religion, Islam. In this sentence "him" refers to
    Options: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) / Hazrat Jibrail / Arabs / Muslims
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)
  • Q: Q4. "Have I fulfilled my mission?" What mission the Rasool (peace be upon him) is referring to?
    Options: Preaching of Islam / Journey from Makkah to Madina / Conquering of Makkah / Battle of Badar
    Ans: Preaching of Islam
  • Q: Q5. The phrase "lend me an attentive ear" means
    Options: put your hands on ears / give me your ears / listen to me attentively / consider it carefully
    Ans: listen to me attentively
  • Q: Q6. The last sermon of the Rasool (peace be upon him) is for the entire
    Options: Muslims / Arabs / humanity / Quraish
    Ans: humanity

Comprehension — C. State whether the following statements are true or false.

  • Q: Be faithful to each other and do not commit sins.
    Ans: True
  • Q: After death of Hazrat Muhammad's (peace be upon him) parents, his uncle Abu Jahl looked after him.
    Ans: False
  • Q: Feed and clothe your slaves with such food and clothing as you choose for yourself.
    Ans: True
  • Q: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) taught love, kindness and compassion to his people.
    Ans: True
  • Q: Allah has allowed you to take usury (interest).
    Ans: False

mcqs.q: What is the basis of superiority in the eyes of Allah?
mcqs.why: The Last Sermon teaches that no Arab, non-Arab, white or black is superior by race or colour; only goodness and piety makes a man superior to others.

mcqs.q: In 'There is no preference for Arab over the non-Arab', the word 'preference' means:
mcqs.why: In this sentence 'preference' means a liking for or favouring one over another, and the sermon says no such preference exists between Arab and non-Arab.

mcqs.q: In 'Allah revealed to him the true religion, Islam', 'him' refers to:
mcqs.why: Allah revealed the true religion Islam to Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him), so the pronoun 'him' in the sentence refers to him.

mcqs.q: In 'Have I fulfilled my mission?', what mission is the Rasool (peace be upon him) referring to?
mcqs.why: His mission was preaching Islam; he spared no effort in preaching the true religion and at the sermon asked if he had fulfilled that mission.

mcqs.q: The phrase 'lend me an attentive ear' means:
mcqs.why: The phrase 'lend me an attentive ear' is an idiom meaning listen to me attentively and carefully, as he asked the assembled people to do.

mcqs.q: The last sermon of the Rasool (peace be upon him) is for the entire:
mcqs.why: His teaching was not for one tribe or nation only; his words in the Last Sermon were directed to the entire humanity.

mcqs.q: Why was Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) called Al-Sadiq and Al-Amin?
options: He always spoke the truth and people could fully trust him
mcqs.why: As a grown-up man he was so honourable and trustworthy that people called him Al-Sadiq, the truthful one, and Al-Amin, the trustworthy one.

mcqs.q: When and where did Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) deliver his last sermon?
options: On the ninth of ZulHijjah, 10 years after Hijrah, in the Uranah Valley of Mount Arafat
On the first of Ramadan in Madinah
On the ninth of Muharram in Makkah
At the time of Hijrah in the Uranah Valley
mcqs.why: He performed his last Hajj and delivered the sermon on the ninth of ZulHijjah, the 12th month, 10 years after Hijrah, in the Uranah Valley of Mount Arafat.

mcqs.q: How should we treat our servants according to the Last Sermon?
options: Give them less food than we eat
Let them wear old clothes only
Feed and clothe them with such food as we eat and such clothes as we wear ourselves
Treat them harshly for a fault
mcqs.why: The sermon says to feed and clothe slaves and servants with such food as we eat ourselves and such clothes as we wear ourselves, and to be kind and just.

mcqs.q: What does the Last Sermon say about usury (interest)?
options: It is allowed in small amounts
It is allowed for traders only
mcqs.why: The Last Sermon teaches never to take usury (interest), which Allah has forbidden, so the statement that Allah has allowed usury is false.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — A. Find the meaning of the following words from the dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviation used.

  • Q: Q1. traced
    Ans: Meaning: followed back to the origin or source; found out the line or history of something, as in the lesson, "His family is traced back to Hazrat Ismail." Part of speech: verb (v.).
  • Q: Q2. dearly
    Ans: Meaning: very much; with great love and affection, as in the lesson, "He loved his young nephew dearly." Part of speech: adverb (adv.).
  • Q: Q3. retire
    Ans: Meaning: to go away to a quiet or private place, as in the lesson, "he would retire to Mount Hira for prayers and meditation." Part of speech: verb (v.).
  • Q: Q4. intense
    Ans: Meaning: very strong, great or extreme in degree; felt very strongly. Part of speech: adjective (adj.).
  • Q: Q5. conveying
    Ans: Meaning: carrying, taking or communicating something, such as a message, to others, as in the Last Sermon, "understand words which I convey to you." Part of speech: verb (v.).
  • Q: Q6. assembled
    Ans: Meaning: gathered together in one place, as in the lesson, "addressing the assembled people." Part of speech: verb (v.).

Vocabulary — B. Consult a thesaurus and find out the synonyms of the following words.

  • Q: Q1. vast
    Ans: Synonyms: huge, immense, very large. In the lesson it is used in "the vast expanse of the desert of Arabia," meaning a very large open area.
  • Q: Q2. spare
    Ans: Synonyms: to save, to hold back, to avoid using. In the lesson, "spared no effort" means he held back nothing and made every possible effort.
  • Q: Q3. effort
    Ans: Synonyms: attempt, struggle, hard work. It means the energy and hard work a person puts in to do something.
  • Q: Q4. great
    Ans: Synonyms: large, huge, much. In the lesson, "He suffered great hardships" means he suffered very large and heavy hardships.
  • Q: Q5. hardship
    Ans: Synonyms: difficulty, suffering, trouble. It means a difficult condition in which a person has to suffer.
  • Q: Q6. grew
    Ans: Synonyms: became larger, increased, developed. It is the past form of "grow."
  • Q: Q7. interest
    Ans: Synonyms: usury. In the Last Sermon, interest means the extra money taken on a loan, which Allah has forbidden.

Grammar — A. Choose the correct option for the following statements.

  • Q: Q1. Quaid-e-Azam is an example of a/an
    Options: common noun / proper noun / countable noun / uncountable noun
    Ans: proper noun
  • Q: Q2. My family lives in Swat. Family is an example of a/an
    Options: collective noun / proper noun / countable noun / uncountable noun
    Ans: collective noun
  • Q: Q3. Don't cry over spilt milk. Milk is an example of a/an
    Options: collective noun / proper noun / common noun / uncountable noun
    Ans: uncountable noun
  • Q: Q4. The hungry fox saw a bunch of grapes. Bunch is a/an
    Options: common noun / uncountable noun / collective noun / proper noun
    Ans: collective noun
  • Q: Q5. Which one is the example of countable noun?
    Options: oil / book / sugar / honey
    Ans: book
  • Q: Q6. Which one is the example of uncountable noun?
    Options: dress / sand / pencil / bottle
    Ans: sand
  • Q: Q7. Which one is the example of collective noun?
    Options: marched / army / up / hill
    Ans: army

Grammar — B. Pick out at least ten each of singular and plural nouns from the story given below. Write down their respective plural and singular forms too. (The Talkative Tortoise)

  • Q: Q1. Pick out at least ten each of singular and plural nouns from the story "The Talkative Tortoise". Write down their respective plural and singular forms too.
    Ans: Singular nouns from the story, with their plurals: 1. tortoise — tortoises 2. stork (in "One stork thought...") — storks 3. friend is used as "friends"; the singular form is friend — friends 4. day — days 5. idea — ideas 6. end — ends 7. stick — sticks 8. mouth — mouths 9. part — parts 10. boy — boys 11. journey — journeys 12. grip — grips Plural nouns from the story, with their singulars: 1. storks — stork 2. friends — friend 3. stories — story 4. places — place 5. wings — wing 6. beaks — beak 7. children — child 8. hands — hand Note: The story contains ten or more singular nouns, but only eight different plural nouns (storks, friends, stories, places, wings, beaks, children, hands), so all of them are listed above with their singular forms.

Grammar — C. Convert each singular noun to plural, and each plural noun to singular. There are a few nouns that have the same singular and plural form.

  • Q: Q1. deer
    Ans: deer (the same in singular and plural form)
  • Q: Q2. quiz
    Ans: quizzes
  • Q: Q3. beech
    Ans: beeches
  • Q: Q4. goose
    Ans: geese
  • Q: Q5. mice
    Ans: mouse (mice is the plural of mouse)
  • Q: Q6. person
    Ans: people
  • Q: Q7. child
    Ans: children
  • Q: Q8. foot
    Ans: feet
  • Q: Q9. fish
    Ans: fish (the same in singular and plural form)
  • Q: Q10. ox
    Ans: oxen

Grammar — D. Change the following compound nouns into plural form.

  • Q: Q1. a tennis shoe
    Ans: three tennis shoes
  • Q: Q2. one assistant headmaster
    Ans: five assistant headmasters
  • Q: Q3. a mother-in-law
    Ans: two mothers-in-law
  • Q: Q4. my toothbrush
    Ans: our toothbrushes
  • Q: Q5. a woman-doctor
    Ans: four women-doctors
  • Q: Q6. a doctor-of-philosophy
    Ans: two doctors-of-philosophy

Articles — Complete the conversations between Safdar and Anwar, by inserting the correct article.

  • Q: There is ______ cricket match at the Stadium tomorrow! Do you want to go?
    Ans: a
  • Q: There is a cricket match at ______ Stadium tomorrow! Do you want to go?
    Ans: the
  • Q: Sure. Do we need ______ ticket?
    Ans: a
  • Q: No, ______ game is free, but the parking costs Rs. 50.
    Ans: the
  • Q: No, the game is free, but ______ parking costs Rs. 50.
    Ans: the
  • Q: Bring ______ hat and an umbrella, because it might rain.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Bring a hat and ______ umbrella, because it might rain.
    Ans: an
  • Q: I will wear ______ cap. They are in fashion.
    Ans: a
  • Q: But ______ cap will not save you from the rain.
    Ans: the
  • Q: But the cap will not save you from ______ rain.
    Ans: the
  • Q: Okay, will ask father to get me ______ new hat and an umbrella.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Okay, will ask father to get me a new hat and ______ umbrella.
    Ans: an
  • Q: See you tomorrow at ______ stadium.
    Ans: the
  • Q: What about ______ time?
    Ans: the

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of 'traced' in 'His family is traced back to Hazrat Ismail'?
options: followed back to the origin or source
mcqs.why: In the lesson 'traced' means followed back to the origin or source, as his family line is followed back to Hazrat Ismail; it is a verb.

mcqs.q: What part of speech is 'dearly' in 'He loved his young nephew dearly'?
mcqs.why: 'Dearly' means very much, with great love and affection, and it describes how he loved, so it is an adverb, abbreviated adv.

mcqs.q: What does 'retire' mean in 'he would retire to Mount Hira for prayers and meditation'?
options: to go away to a quiet or private place
mcqs.why: Here 'retire' means to go away to a quiet or private place; he would retire to Mount Hira for prayers and meditation. It is a verb.

mcqs.q: 'Intense' is an adjective meaning:
options: very strong, great or extreme in degree
mcqs.why: 'Intense' means very strong, great or extreme in degree, felt very strongly, and it is an adjective, abbreviated adj.

mcqs.q: Which word is a synonym of 'vast' in 'the vast expanse of the desert of Arabia'?
mcqs.why: Synonyms of 'vast' are huge, immense and very large; the vast expanse means a very large open area of the desert of Arabia.

mcqs.q: In 'spared no effort', 'spare' means:
mcqs.why: 'Spare' means to save, to hold back or to avoid using; 'spared no effort' means he held back nothing and made every possible effort.

mcqs.q: Which is a synonym of 'hardship' in 'He suffered great hardships'?
mcqs.why: Synonyms of 'hardship' are difficulty, suffering and trouble; it means a difficult condition in which a person has to suffer.

mcqs.q: Quaid-e-Azam is an example of a/an:
mcqs.why: Quaid-e-Azam is the name of a particular person, so it is a proper noun, as given in the book's grammar exercise.

mcqs.q: 'Family' in 'My family lives in Swat' is an example of a/an:
mcqs.why: 'Family' names a group of people taken together as one unit, so it is a collective noun, as given in the book's exercise.

mcqs.q: 'Milk' in 'Don't cry over spilt milk' is an example of a/an:
mcqs.why: Milk cannot be counted in separate units in this use, so it is an uncountable noun, as given in the book's grammar exercise.

mcqs.q: Which one is an example of a countable noun?
mcqs.why: A book can be counted as one book, two books, so 'book' is the countable noun among oil, sugar and honey, which are uncountable.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'goose'?
mcqs.why: The plural of 'goose' is 'geese'; it is an irregular plural in which the vowel changes, as listed in the singular-plural exercise.

mcqs.q: Which noun has the same singular and plural form?
mcqs.why: 'Deer' has the same form in singular and plural, like 'fish'; the exercise notes a few nouns keep the same form in both numbers.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'mother-in-law'?
mcqs.why: In the compound noun 'mother-in-law' the main word 'mother' becomes plural, giving 'mothers-in-law', as in 'two mothers-in-law'.

mcqs.q: Complete the conversation: 'There is ______ cricket match at the Stadium tomorrow!'
mcqs.why: A cricket match is mentioned for the first time and 'cricket' begins with a consonant sound, so the correct article is 'a'.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — A. Complete the mind map and then summarize the last sermon of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him).

  • Q: Q1. Complete the mind map and then summarize the last sermon of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him).
    Ans: Mind map — Last Sermon of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him): 1. Your lives and property are a sacred trust amongst yourselves. 2. You have rights over your wives and your wives have rights over you; treat them with kindness and affection. 3. Be kind to your servants and do not treat them harshly; feed and clothe them as you feed and clothe yourself. 4. Say your five prayers daily, fast during Ramadan, give Zakat and perform Hajj if you can afford to. 5. There is no superiority of Arab over non-Arab or white over black; only goodness and piety makes a man superior. 6. I leave behind me two things, the Qur'an and my Sunnah; follow them and you will never go astray. Summary of the Last Sermon: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) delivered his Last Sermon on the ninth of ZulHijjah, 10 years after Hijrah, in the Uranah Valley of Mount Arafat. He told the people to listen to him carefully, as he might not be amongst them again, and to take his words to those who were not present. He said that their lives and property were a sacred trust and that they would have to appear before their Lord and give an account of all their actions. He advised them to beware of Satan for the safety of their religion. He said that husbands and wives have rights over each other and that wives must be treated with kindness and affection. He forbade usury (interest) and said that all interest obligations would be waived, and that no murders committed during the days of ignorance (Jahiliyyat) were to be avenged. He declared that every Muslim is truly a brother to every other Muslim and that no Arab, non-Arab, white or black is superior to another; only goodness and piety makes a man superior. He urged the people to worship Allah, say their five prayers daily, fast during Ramadan, give their wealth in Zakat and perform Hajj if they could afford it. He told them to feed and clothe their slaves as they fed and clothed themselves and to be kind and just to everyone. At the end he said that no Prophet would come after him and that he was leaving behind the Qur'an and his Sunnah, following which they would never go astray. When he asked, "Have I fulfilled my mission?", the pilgrims replied, "In truth you have," and he said, "Be my witness, O Allah, that I have conveyed your message to your people."

Writing — B. Read the following paragraph carefully. Pick out a clear topic sentence and underline the specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers.

  • Q: Q1. Read the following paragraph carefully. Pick out a clear topic sentence and underline the specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers. (Paragraph: "As a grown-up man, he was so honourable and trust worthy that people would call him Al-Sadiq and Al-Amin. When Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) reached the age of 40, he would retire to Mount Hira for prayers and meditation. One day, while he sat in a cave at Mount Hira, Hazrat Jibrail, the Angel of Revelation, appeared to him and said, 'Iqra' — Read! Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, 'I am not able to read!' But the command was issued twice more, each with the same response from the Rasool. Finally, he was grasped with overwhelming force by the angel. Then Hazrat Jibrail released him and the first verse of the Holy Quran was revealed to him. 'Read in the name of your Lord who created.'")
    Ans: Topic sentence: "As a grown-up man, he was so honourable and trust worthy that people would call him Al-Sadiq and Al-Amin." This sentence states the main idea of the first part of the paragraph, that Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) was known for his truthfulness and trustworthiness. Specific words: honourable, trust worthy, Al-Sadiq, Al-Amin, Mount Hira, Angel of Revelation. These particular words reflect the main idea and name the exact persons and places. Vivid verbs: call, reached, retire, appeared, issued, grasped, released, revealed. These descriptive verbs give detail to the ideas and make the actions clear. Modifiers: grown-up (man), overwhelming (force), first (verse), same (response). These adjectives provide additional information about the nouns they describe.

mcqs.q: According to the summary of the Last Sermon, what are people's lives and property?
mcqs.why: The mind map and summary state: 'Your lives and property are a sacred trust amongst yourselves,' so they must be respected and protected.

mcqs.q: What two things did Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) say he was leaving behind?
mcqs.why: He said, 'I leave behind me two things, the Qur'an and my Sunnah; follow them and you will never go astray.'

mcqs.q: What did the pilgrims reply when he asked, 'Have I fulfilled my mission?'
mcqs.why: When he asked 'Have I fulfilled my mission?', the hundreds of pilgrims replied together, 'In truth you have.'

mcqs.q: According to the summary, what happens to interest obligations?
options: They are paid to the rich
mcqs.why: He forbade usury (interest) and said that all interest obligations would be waived, as summarised from the Last Sermon.

mcqs.q: What does the summary say about murders committed during the days of ignorance (Jahiliyyat)?
options: They were not to be avenged
They were to be reported to the Quraish
They were to be forgiven only for Arabs
mcqs.why: The summary states that no murders committed during the days of ignorance (Jahiliyyat) were to be avenged.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is the topic sentence of the paragraph in Writing B?
options: One day, while he sat in a cave at Mount Hira
As a grown-up man, he was so honourable and trustworthy that people would call him Al-Sadiq and Al-Amin
Read in the name of your Lord who created
mcqs.why: That sentence states the main idea of the first part of the paragraph, that he was known for his truthfulness and trustworthiness, so it is the topic sentence.

mcqs.q: In the paragraph, which words are given as vivid verbs?
options: call, reached, retire, appeared, grasped, released, revealed
mcqs.why: Vivid verbs listed are call, reached, retire, appeared, issued, grasped, released and revealed; these descriptive verbs make the actions clear.

mcqs.q: In the paragraph, 'grown-up', 'overwhelming', 'first' and 'same' are examples of:
mcqs.why: These adjectives are modifiers because they provide additional information about the nouns they describe, such as grown-up man and overwhelming force.

mcqs.q: At what age would Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) retire to Mount Hira, according to the paragraph?
mcqs.why: The paragraph says: 'When Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) reached the age of 40, he would retire to Mount Hira for prayers and meditation.'

mcqs.q: What were the first revealed words quoted in the paragraph?
options: Read in the name of your Lord who created
mcqs.why: After Hazrat Jibrail released him, the first verse revealed was 'Read in the name of your Lord who created.'

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Practice the dialogue with your seat fellows.

  • Q: Q1. Practice the dialogue with your seat fellows. (Greetings, introduction, welcome and invitation between Tahira and Salma)
    Ans: Practise the dialogue in pairs, one student as Tahira and the other as Salma, using polite greetings, introductions and an invitation: Tahira: Asalam-o-Aliakum! How are you? Salma: Walaik-um-Asalam! I am fine. Tahira: I am Tahira. May I know your name please! Salma: I am Salma. Tahira: I welcome you in our class, Salma. Which school have you come from? Salma: I am from Government School Swat. My father got posted here. What about you? Tahira: I have been studying here since grade 1. I would like you to have a cup of tea with me in recess; I will introduce you to my other friends too. Salma: Okay, sure. Thank you. Guide: Greet your partner first, reply to the greeting, introduce yourself and ask your partner's name, welcome a new class fellow warmly, tell about your own school, and end with a friendly invitation and thanks.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the pictures below and tell what place is it?
    Ans: The pictures show the Khyber Pass. One picture shows Bab-e-Khyber (the Khyber Gate) at Jamrud, the entrance to the Pass, and the other shows the winding road passing through the mountains of the Khyber Pass.

Glossary

  • Q: What does 'bridge' mean?
    Ans: A structure that is built over a river, road, or railway to allow people and vehicles to cross from one side to the other.
  • Q: What does 'passage' mean?
    Ans: A usually long and narrow part of a building with rooms on one or both sides, or a covered path that connects places.
  • Q: What does 'cliffs' mean?
    Ans: A high area of rock with a very steep side.
  • Q: What does 'elevation' mean?
    Ans: The height of a place above the level of the sea.
  • Q: What does 'strategic' mean?
    Ans: Used to provide military forces with an advantage.
  • Q: What does 'invasions' mean?
    Ans: An occasion when an army or country uses force to enter and take control of another country.
  • Q: What does 'witnessed' mean?
    Ans: To see something happen.
  • Q: What does 'capture' mean?
    Ans: To take someone as a prisoner, or to take something into your possession, especially by force.
  • Q: What does 'caravans' mean?
    Ans: A group of people with vehicles or animals who travel together for safety through a dangerous area, especially across a desert on camels.
  • Q: What does 'safari' mean?
    Ans: An organized journey to look at, or sometimes hunt, wild animals.
  • Q: What does 'victorious' mean?
    Ans: Having won a game, competition, election, war, etc.
  • Q: What does 'spices' mean?
    Ans: A substance made from a plant, used to give a special flavour to food.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Describe briefly the route from Peshawar to Khyber Pass?
    Ans: 17 km west from the city of Peshawar is a small town Jamrud, which is the entry point to the Khyber Pass. Bab-e-Khyber (Khyber Gate), a monument built in the 10th century and repaired in 1964, stands at the entrance in Jamrud, and next to it is a fort built by the Sikhs. Further some 30 kms ahead is Landi Kotal, the highest point along the Pass. Just a few kilometres further is the Torkham border. The Pass itself is a 53-kilometer passage through the Hindu Kush mountain range, of which 45-kilometers lies in Pakistan.
  • Q: Q2. Why is Landi Kotal a famous place along the pass?
    Ans: Landi Kotal is famous because it is the highest point along the Pass, at which the mountains on either side can be climbed only in a few places. It has a railway station of the Khyber Pass Railway, on which the tourist train, the Khyber train safari, was run. It is also a famous market place where people enjoy eating tikkas and chappli kababs.
  • Q: Q3. What is the historical importance of the Khyber Pass?
    Ans: The history of the Khyber Pass as a strategic gateway dates from 326 B.C., when Alexander the Great and his army marched through the Khyber to reach the plains of India. In the AD 900s, Persian, Mongol, and Tartar armies forced their way through the Khyber, bringing Islam to India, and Sultan Mehmood Ghaznavi crossed the Pass seventeen times to attack South Asia. It witnessed the march of Aryans and the victorious advance of Persian and Greek armies, and Babur established the Moghul Empire in Northern India after coming through the Pass. During the Afghan Wars the Pass was the scene of numerous conflicts between Anglo-Indian soldiers and native Afghans.
  • Q: Q4. What did the camel caravans carry? By what have the camel caravans been replaced?
    Ans: The camel caravans carried bales of cotton, silk and spices from the Sub-continent and China to Afghanistan and beyond, and they brought mirrors, furs, skins and fruits from there for the Sub-continent and the countries to the east. The camel caravans have been replaced by motor vehicles using the road and highway through the Pass, and by trains on the railroad built here in the 1920s, though traders still use this route.
  • Q: Q5. What is the economic importance of Khyber Pass?
    Ans: The Khyber Pass is an important part of the ancient Silk Route and has significant economic importance. It had been a famous trade route: camel caravans carried cotton, silk and spices through it, and traders still use this route. Torkham border is the busiest point of entry between Pakistan and Afghanistan through the Khyber Pass, serving as a major transporting, shipping, and receiving site, and Landi Kotal is a famous market place along the Pass.
  • Q: Q6. What famous conquerors / invaders passed through the Khyber Pass to enter sub-continent?
    Ans: Alexander the Great marched through the Khyber Pass in 326 B.C. Persian, Mongol, and Tartar armies forced their way through it in the AD 900s, and Sultan Mehmood Ghaznavi crossed it seventeen times. Babur also came through the Pass from Afghanistan and established the Moghul Empire in Northern India. The Pass also witnessed the march of the Aryans and the advance of Persian and Greek armies.

Comprehension — B. Choose correct option

  • Q: 1. Torkham border, is one of the major border between Pakistan and Afghanistan because __________.
    Options: at this point, the mountains can be climbed only in a few places. / it is a famous market place where people enjoy eating tikkas / it is a major transporting, shipping, and receiving site. / it is a strategic gateway dates from 326 B.C.,
    Ans: it is a major transporting, shipping, and receiving site.
  • Q: 2. Which countries are linked by the Khyber Pass?
    Options: India and Pakistan / India and Afghanistan / Afghanistan and Pakistan / Afghanistan and Tajikistan
    Ans: Afghanistan and Pakistan
  • Q: 3. Babur succeeded in establishing the __________ in Northern India after coming through the Pass from Afghanistan.
    Options: British Empire / Moghul Empire / Persian Empire / Greek Empire
    Ans: Moghul Empire
  • Q: 4. The Khyber Pass is a narrow __________ pass.
    Options: mountain / hill / plain / forest
    Ans: mountain
  • Q: 5. The Khyber Pass had been known as a famous __________ route.
    Options: silk / cotton / spice / trade
    Ans: trade

Comprehension — C. State whether the following statements are true or false

  • Q: 1. Bab-e-Khyber is a fort built by the Sikhs.
    Ans: False
  • Q: 2. About 50 kilometers from Peshawar is Jamrud.
    Ans: False
  • Q: 3. Khyber is a Greek word meaning a fort.
    Ans: False
  • Q: 4. Parallel to the road, runs the railway line.
    Ans: True
  • Q: 5. Mehmood Ghaznavi crossed the Khyber Pass seventeen times.
    Ans: True

Comprehension — D. Fill in the blanks

  • Q: 1. Khyber Pass has been ______ in history.
    Ans: invasions
  • Q: 2. It has also been a famous ______ route.
    Ans: trade
  • Q: 3. These brave tribes' men fought the mighty ______ Empire.
    Ans: British
  • Q: 4. They ate some ______ and Chapli Kabab.
    Ans: tikkas
  • Q: 5. The road goes down winding through ______ scenery.
    Ans: mountain

mcqs.q: Torkham border is one of the major borders between Pakistan and Afghanistan because:
options: at this point, the mountains can be climbed only in a few places
it is a famous market place where people enjoy eating tikkas
it is a major transporting, shipping, and receiving site
it is a strategic gateway dating from 326 B.C.
mcqs.why: Torkham is the busiest point of entry and a major transporting, shipping and receiving site between Pakistan and Afghanistan, as given in the book.

mcqs.q: Which countries are linked by the Khyber Pass?
mcqs.why: The Khyber Pass lies in the mountains that divide Pakistan and Afghanistan, so it links Afghanistan and Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Babur succeeded in establishing the __________ in Northern India after coming through the Pass from Afghanistan.
mcqs.why: Babur came through the Pass from Afghanistan and established the Moghul Empire in Northern India, as stated in the lesson.

mcqs.q: The Khyber Pass is a narrow __________ pass.
mcqs.why: The Khyber Pass is a narrow mountain pass, a 53-kilometer passage through the Hindu Kush mountain range.

mcqs.q: The Khyber Pass had been known as a famous __________ route.
mcqs.why: It had been a famous trade route and an important part of the ancient Silk Route, with caravans carrying cotton, silk and spices.

mcqs.q: What does 'elevation' mean?
options: The height of a place above the level of the sea
A group travelling together for safety
A structure built over a river
mcqs.why: In the glossary, 'elevation' means the height of a place above the level of the sea, used for high points like Landi Kotal.

mcqs.q: How far west from Peshawar is Jamrud, the entry point to the Khyber Pass?
mcqs.why: 17 km west from the city of Peshawar is the small town Jamrud, which is the entry point to the Khyber Pass, with Bab-e-Khyber at its entrance.

mcqs.q: How many times did Sultan Mehmood Ghaznavi cross the Khyber Pass?
mcqs.why: Sultan Mehmood Ghaznavi crossed the Pass seventeen times to attack South Asia, a true statement confirmed in the lesson.

mcqs.q: What did the camel caravans carry from the Sub-continent and China?
options: Bales of cotton, silk and spices
mcqs.why: The camel caravans carried bales of cotton, silk and spices from the Sub-continent and China to Afghanistan and beyond.

mcqs.q: Which statement is true according to the lesson?
options: Bab-e-Khyber is a fort built by the Sikhs
About 50 kilometers from Peshawar is Jamrud
Parallel to the road, runs the railway line
Khyber is a Greek word meaning a fort
mcqs.why: The true/false exercise confirms that parallel to the road runs the railway line; Bab-e-Khyber is a monument and the Sikh fort stands next to it.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — A. Give pronunciation of the following words with the help of pronunciation key in your dictionary

  • Q: Give the pronunciation of 'Hebrew'.
    Ans: /ˈhiːbruː/ (HEE-broo)
  • Q: Give the pronunciation of 'mountain'.
    Ans: /ˈmaʊntɪn/ (MOUN-tin)
  • Q: Give the pronunciation of 'economic'.
    Ans: /ˌiːkəˈnɒmɪk/ (ee-kuh-NOM-ik)
  • Q: Give the pronunciation of 'cultural'.

  • Q: Give the pronunciation of 'monument'.
