mcqs.q: What is the pronunciation of 'Hebrew' given in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The lesson gives 'Hebrew' as /ˈhiːbruː/, spoken as HEE-broo, with the stress on the first part.

mcqs.q: How is 'mountain' pronounced?
mcqs.why: The lesson gives 'mountain' as /ˈmaʊntɪn/, spoken as MOUN-tin, which is the word used for the Hindu Kush mountain range.

mcqs.q: What is the pronunciation of 'economic'?
mcqs.why: The lesson gives 'economic' as /ˌiːkəˈnɒmɪk/, spoken as ee-kuh-NOM-ik, with the main stress on 'NOM'.

mcqs.q: How is 'cultural' pronounced?
mcqs.why: The lesson gives 'cultural' as /ˈkʌltʃərəl/, spoken as KUL-chuh-rul, with the stress at the beginning of the word.

mcqs.q: What is the pronunciation of 'monument'?
mcqs.why: The lesson gives 'monument' as /ˈmɒnjumənt/, spoken as MON-yuh-munt; Bab-e-Khyber is described as a monument.

mcqs.q: Which word is spoken as HEE-broo?
mcqs.why: HEE-broo is the spoken form given for 'Hebrew', /ˈhiːbruː/, the language in which Khyber means a fort.

mcqs.q: Which word is spoken as MOUN-tin?
mcqs.why: MOUN-tin is the spoken form given for 'mountain', /ˈmaʊntɪn/, as in the mountain passes of the lesson.

mcqs.q: Which word has the spoken form ee-kuh-NOM-ik?
mcqs.why: Ee-kuh-NOM-ik is the spoken form given for 'economic', /ˌiːkəˈnɒmɪk/, relating to the economic importance of the Pass.

mcqs.q: Which word is spoken as KUL-chuh-rul?
mcqs.why: KUL-chuh-rul is the spoken form given for 'cultural', /ˈkʌltʃərəl/, as in the cultural importance of the Khyber Pass.

mcqs.q: Which word is spoken as MON-yuh-munt?
mcqs.why: MON-yuh-munt is the spoken form given for 'monument', /ˈmɒnjumənt/, the word used for Bab-e-Khyber at Jamrud.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — B. Locate synonyms of the following words in children's thesaurus and use the words in sentences of your own

  • Q: Give a synonym of 'numerous' and use 'numerous' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Synonym: many. Sentence: During the Afghan Wars the pass was the scene of numerous conflicts.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'passage' and use 'passage' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Synonym: a narrow way through. Sentence: The Khyber Pass is a 53-kilometer passage through the Hindu Kush mountain range.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'capture' and use 'capture' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Synonym: to seize or take by force. Sentence: The soldiers captured the fort after a long fight.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'feeling' and use 'feeling' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Synonym: emotion, sensation. Sentence: She had a happy feeling when she saw the beautiful mountains of the Khyber Pass.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'brought' and use 'brought' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Synonym: carried, fetched. Sentence: The caravans brought mirrors, furs, skins and fruits from Afghanistan for the Sub-continent.

Grammar — Masculine and Feminine Nouns: A. Fill in the blanks with correct masculine or feminine nouns

  • Q: Fill in the blank: heir — ______ (feminine)
    Ans: heiress
  • Q: Fill in the blank: ______ — tigress (masculine)
    Ans: tiger
  • Q: Fill in the blank: rooster — ______ (feminine)
    Ans: hen
  • Q: Fill in the blank: ______ — cow (masculine)
    Ans: ox
  • Q: Fill in the blank: prince — ______ (feminine)
    Ans: princess
  • Q: Fill in the blank: ______ — aunty (masculine)
    Ans: uncle
  • Q: Fill in the blank: ______ — hostess (masculine)
    Ans: host
  • Q: Fill in the blank: steward — ______ (feminine)
    Ans: stewardess

Grammar — B. Rewrite the following sentences changing the underlined nouns from masculine to feminine

  • Q: Rewrite changing masculine to feminine: 1. The bridegroom was congratulated by his friend.
    Ans: The bride was congratulated by her friend. (friend is a common gender noun, so it does not change.)
  • Q: Rewrite changing masculine to feminine: 2. A boy sat on the back of a stallion.
    Ans: A girl sat on the back of a mare.
  • Q: Rewrite changing masculine to feminine: 3. My brother-in-law is a great poet.
    Ans: My sister-in-law is a great poetess.
  • Q: Rewrite changing masculine to feminine: 4. The headmaster welcomed the students.
    Ans: The headmistress welcomed the students. (students is a common gender noun, so it does not change.)
  • Q: Rewrite changing masculine to feminine: 5. The waiter served the guests.
    Ans: The waitress served the guests. (guests is a common gender noun, so it does not change.)

Grammar — Possessive Forms of Animate and Inanimate Nouns: A. Circle the correct possessive nouns

  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 1. The girls / girl's dress is yellow.
    Ans: girl's dress — The girl's dress is yellow. (Given in the book.)
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 2. My father-in-laws / father-in-law's health is not good.
    Ans: father-in-law's — My father-in-law's health is not good.
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 3. Mr Nafees's / Nafees' office is very far from his house.
    Ans: Nafees's — Mr Nafees's office is very far from his house.
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 4. Table's leg / Leg of the table was fixed by the carpainter.
    Ans: Leg of the table — The leg of the table was fixed by the carpainter. (A table is inanimate, so the 'of' form is used.)
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 5. I really like my mothers / mother's cooking.
    Ans: mother's — I really like my mother's cooking.
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 6. The hood of the car / car's hood was not closed properly.
    Ans: hood of the car — The hood of the car was not closed properly. (A car is inanimate, so the 'of' form is used.)
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 7. The birds / bird's nest fell from the tree.
    Ans: bird's nest — The bird's nest fell from the tree.
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 8. They were burning tree's bark / barks of the tree.
    Ans: bark of the tree — They were burning the bark of the tree. (A tree is inanimate, so the 'of' form is used.)
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 9. All the boys' / boy's uniforms got dirty at that game.
    Ans: boys' — All the boys' uniforms got dirty at that game.
  • Q: Circle the correct possessive noun: 10. Skate's blades / Blades of the skate need sharpening.
    Ans: Blades of the skate — The blades of the skate need sharpening. (A skate is inanimate, so the 'of' form is used.)

Grammar — B. Rewrite each phrase to use a possessive noun

  • Q: Rewrite to use a possessive noun: 1. The cycle belongs to Zafar.
    Ans: It is Zafar's cycle. (Given in the book.)
  • Q: Rewrite to use a possessive noun: 2. The shirt of her brother is white.
    Ans: Her brother's shirt is white.
  • Q: Rewrite to use a possessive noun: 3. That elephant has huge ears.
    Ans: That elephant's ears are huge.
  • Q: Rewrite to use a possessive noun: 4. The house belongs to Qasim.
    Ans: It is Qasim's house.
  • Q: Rewrite to use a possessive noun: 5. All the branches of the trees were waving in the wind.
    Ans: All the branches of the trees were waving in the wind. (Trees are inanimate, so the 'of' form is kept and no possessive ending is used.)
  • Q: Rewrite to use a possessive noun: 6. The teacher looked at the work of all the students.
    Ans: The teacher looked at all the students' work.

mcqs.q: What is a synonym of 'numerous' in 'numerous conflicts'?
mcqs.why: The synonym given for 'numerous' is 'many'; during the Afghan Wars the pass was the scene of numerous, that is many, conflicts.

mcqs.q: What is a synonym of 'capture'?
options: to seize or take by force
mcqs.why: The synonym given for 'capture' is to seize or take by force, as in 'The soldiers captured the fort after a long fight.'

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'heir'?
mcqs.why: The feminine form of 'heir' is 'heiress', formed by adding -ess, as given in the masculine and feminine nouns exercise.

mcqs.q: What is the masculine of 'tigress'?
mcqs.why: The masculine form paired with 'tigress' is 'tiger', as given in the fill-in exercise on masculine and feminine nouns.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'rooster'?
mcqs.why: The feminine form of 'rooster' is 'hen', as given in the masculine and feminine nouns exercise in this lesson.

mcqs.q: What is the masculine of 'cow'?
mcqs.why: The masculine form paired with 'cow' in the exercise is 'ox', as given in the list of masculine and feminine nouns.

mcqs.q: Rewrite changing masculine to feminine: 'The bridegroom was congratulated by his friend.'
options: The bride was congratulated by her friend
The bridegroom was congratulated by her friend
The bride was congratulated by his friend
The groom was congratulated by her friend
mcqs.why: Bridegroom changes to bride and his changes to her; 'friend' is a common gender noun, so it does not change.

mcqs.q: Rewrite changing masculine to feminine: 'A boy sat on the back of a stallion.'
options: A girl sat on the back of a stallion
A girl sat on the back of a mare
A boy sat on the back of a mare
A girl sat on the back of a horse
mcqs.why: Boy changes to girl and stallion changes to mare, giving 'A girl sat on the back of a mare.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive: 'My ______ health is not good.'
mcqs.why: The correct possessive is 'father-in-law's' because the apostrophe-s goes at the end of the whole compound noun for one person.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct form for an inanimate noun: '______ was fixed by the carpenter.'
mcqs.why: A table is inanimate, so the 'of' form is used: 'The leg of the table was fixed by the carpenter.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive: 'I really like my ______ cooking.'
mcqs.why: One mother's cooking is meant, so the singular possessive 'mother's' is correct, as in 'I really like my mother's cooking.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive: 'All the ______ uniforms got dirty at that game.'
mcqs.why: More than one boy is meant and the noun already ends in s, so the plural possessive 'boys'' is correct.

mcqs.q: Rewrite using a possessive noun: 'The cycle belongs to Zafar.'
mcqs.why: For an animate owner the possessive form is used: 'It is Zafar's cycle', as given in the book's example.

mcqs.q: Rewrite using a possessive noun: 'The teacher looked at the work of all the students.'
options: The teacher looked at all the students' work
The teacher looked at all the student work's
The teacher looked at all the students work
The teacher looked at work students' all
mcqs.why: Students are animate and plural, so it becomes 'all the students' work', with the apostrophe after the s.

mcqs.q: Why is 'All the branches of the trees' NOT changed to a possessive with apostrophe-s?
options: Trees are inanimate, so the 'of' form is kept
mcqs.why: Trees are inanimate, so the 'of' form is kept and no possessive ending is used, as explained in the exercise answer.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — A. Read the paragraph carefully to identify the main idea, general statement, specific statement and transition words

  • Q: What is the main idea of the paragraph beginning 'Khyber is a Hebrew word meaning a fort'?
    Ans: The main idea of the paragraph is that the Khyber Pass is one of the most famous mountain passes in the world and has great cultural, economic and geopolitical importance.
  • Q: Which sentence is the general statement (topic sentence) of the paragraph?
    Ans: The general statement is: 'The Khyber Pass is one of the most famous mountain passes in the World.' It informs the readers about the general idea of the paragraph, and all the other sentences support it.
  • Q: Which sentences are the specific statements (supporting details) of the paragraph?
    Ans: The specific statements are the sentences that give details about the main idea: the Pass is located in the mountains that divide Pakistan and Afghanistan and forms the bridge between Central and South Asia; it is a 53-kilometer passage through the Hindu Kush mountain range, of which 45-kilometers lies in Pakistan; it is an important part of the ancient Silk Route; and at its narrowest point, the pass is only 3 meters wide.
  • Q: Which transition words and links are used in the paragraph?
    Ans: The sentences are linked mainly by repeating the subject 'The Khyber Pass' and by the pronoun 'it', and by the conjunction 'and' in 'cultural, economic, and geopolitical importance'. These links join each new detail smoothly to the main idea.

Writing — B. Draw a mind map with name of a historical place at its center

  • Q: Draw a mind map with name of a historical place at its center. Arrange information related to the place around the main theme in the center, use brainstorming strategy.
    Ans: Centre: THE KHYBER PASS. Branches around it: (1) Location — in the Hindu Kush mountains dividing Pakistan and Afghanistan; 53 km long, 45 km in Pakistan; only 3 metres wide at its narrowest point. (2) Places on the route — Jamrud (17 km from Peshawar), Bab-e-Khyber, Landi Kotal, Torkham border. (3) History — Alexander the Great (326 B.C.), Persian, Mongol and Tartar armies, Mehmood Ghaznavi, Babur and the Moghul Empire, the Afghan Wars. (4) Trade — part of the ancient Silk Route; camel caravans carried cotton, silk and spices; Torkham is a major transporting, shipping and receiving site. (5) Transport — road built in 1879, highway and railroad built in the 1920s, the Khyber train safari.

Writing — C. Write a simple and unified paragraph on 'Trip to a Historical Place'

  • Q: After brainstorming and developing ideas, write a simple and unified paragraph on 'Trip to a Historical Place'.
    Ans: Last month I went on a trip to the Khyber Pass, the most famous historical place of our province. We started from Peshawar early in the morning and reached Jamrud after travelling only 17 kilometres. There we saw Bab-e-Khyber, the great gate at the entrance of the Pass, and the old fort built by the Sikhs near Jamrud village. Then our bus climbed the winding road through the dry mountains, and at some places the pass was so narrow that we felt the cliffs were closing in on us. At Landi Kotal, the highest point along the Pass, we ate hot tikkas and chappli kababs in the famous market and saw the station of the Khyber Pass Railway. We then went a few kilometres further to the Torkham border, the busiest point of entry between Pakistan and Afghanistan. Standing there, I thought of Alexander the Great, Mehmood Ghaznavi and Babur, who had all marched through this same gateway. It was a wonderful trip, and I learned that the Khyber Pass is not only a trade route but also a living page of history.

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the paragraph beginning 'Khyber is a Hebrew word meaning a fort'?
options: The Pass is only a trade route
The Khyber Pass is one of the most famous mountain passes in the world and has great cultural, economic and geopolitical importance
The railroad was built in the 1920s
mcqs.why: The main idea is that the Khyber Pass is one of the most famous mountain passes in the world and has great cultural, economic and geopolitical importance.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is the general statement (topic sentence) of that paragraph?
options: It is a 53-kilometer passage through the Hindu Kush
At its narrowest point, the pass is only 3 meters wide
The Khyber Pass is one of the most famous mountain passes in the World
It is an important part of the ancient Silk Route
mcqs.why: The general statement is 'The Khyber Pass is one of the most famous mountain passes in the World'; all other sentences support it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a specific statement supporting the main idea?
options: The Pass is located in the mountains that divide Pakistan and Afghanistan
mcqs.why: Specific statements give details, such as the Pass being located in the mountains that divide Pakistan and Afghanistan and forming a bridge between Central and South Asia.

mcqs.q: How long is the Khyber Pass, and how much of it lies in Pakistan?
mcqs.why: The paragraph states it is a 53-kilometer passage through the Hindu Kush mountain range, of which 45 kilometers lies in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: How wide is the Pass at its narrowest point?
mcqs.why: A specific statement in the paragraph says that at its narrowest point, the pass is only 3 meters wide.

mcqs.q: Which links are used to join the sentences in the paragraph?
options: Repeating the subject 'The Khyber Pass', the pronoun 'it', and the conjunction 'and'
mcqs.why: The sentences are linked mainly by repeating the subject 'The Khyber Pass' and by the pronoun 'it', and by 'and' in 'cultural, economic, and geopolitical importance'.

mcqs.q: In the mind map on the Khyber Pass, which place is listed 17 km from Peshawar?
mcqs.why: The mind map branch 'Places on the route' lists Jamrud (17 km from Peshawar), Bab-e-Khyber, Landi Kotal and the Torkham border.

mcqs.q: In the paragraph on 'Trip to a Historical Place', what did the writer eat at Landi Kotal?
mcqs.why: At Landi Kotal, the highest point along the Pass, the writer ate hot tikkas and chappli kababs in the famous market.

mcqs.q: According to the trip paragraph, where did the writer go after Landi Kotal?
mcqs.why: After Landi Kotal they went a few kilometres further to the Torkham border, the busiest point of entry between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

mcqs.q: What is placed at the centre of a mind map on a historical place?
options: The name of the historical place
mcqs.why: In Writing B the name of a historical place is placed at the centre, with related information arranged around it using brainstorming.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Work in pairs to generate questions for the last paragraph of the text

  • Q: Ask at least one question that is literal (Who? What? When?) for the last paragraph of the text, and answer it.
    Ans: Literal question: What did the camel caravans carry from the Sub-continent and China to Afghanistan and beyond? Answer: They carried bales of cotton, silk and spices. Another literal question: When did the British construct a road through the pass, and when was it converted into a highway? Answer: The British constructed a road through the pass in 1879 and converted it into a highway during the 1920s.
  • Q: Ask at least one question that requires a conclusion (Why? How?) for the last paragraph of the text, and answer it.
    Ans: Conclusion question: Why was a railroad built in the Khyber Pass in the 1920s? Answer: The railroad was laid to carry arms and supplies for the British army, because the Pass was a strategic gateway that the British defended from the British Indian side. Another conclusion question: How did trade through the Pass change with the passage of time? Answer: Formerly camel caravans carried the goods, but later the road, the highway and the railroad took their place, though traders still use this route.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Can the clouds be angry?
    Ans: No. Clouds are not alive, so they cannot really feel anger. In the picture the cloud is only drawn with an angry face; giving it a human feeling like anger is personification.
  • Q: Can the flowers sing and dance?
    Ans: No. Flowers cannot really sing and dance like human beings. When a poet says the flowers sing and dance, he is giving them human qualities, which is personification.
  • Q: Can the sun be happy?
    Ans: No. The sun cannot really be happy, because happiness is a human feeling. A smiling sun in a picture or a poem is an example of personification.
  • Q: Can a person be happy, angry, lonely etc.?
    Ans: Yes. A person is a living human being, so a person can truly be happy, angry, lonely, etc.

Reading — Deduce the meaning of the following words

  • Q: Deduce the meaning of 'suit' from the poem.
    Ans: In the poem, a 'suit' means a set of clothes worn together. The garden puts away its dark winter suits, that is, its bare and dull winter covering is compared to a suit of clothes.
  • Q: Deduce the meaning of 'wrap' from the poem.
    Ans: 'Wrap' means to cover or fold something around a thing or a person. In the poem the garden wraps itself in green shoots, as a person wraps a cloth around himself.
  • Q: Deduce the meaning of 'dull' from the poem.
    Ans: 'Dull' means not bright, without colour and interest. In the poem the garden's winter scarves are dull, in contrast with the bright colours of spring.
  • Q: Deduce the meaning of 'shoot' from the poem.
    Ans: A 'shoot' is a new, young stem or leaf that grows from a plant. In the poem the garden wraps itself in green shoots in spring.
  • Q: Deduce the meaning of 'daffodil' from the poem.
    Ans: A 'daffodil' is a yellow flower that appears in spring. In the poem the garden pulls on skirts of daffodil and primrose.

Glossary

  • Q: What does 'slips' mean?
    Ans: To put clothes on or to take them off quickly and easily.
  • Q: What does 'blossom' mean?
    Ans: A flower or a mass of flowers, especially on a fruit tree or bush.
  • Q: What does 'crocus' mean?
    Ans: A small yellow, purple or white flower that appears in early spring.
  • Q: What does 'snowdrop' mean?
    Ans: A small white flower that appears in early spring.
  • Q: What does 'drab' mean?
    Ans: Without interest or colour; dull and boring.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What are some examples of personification in the poem?
    Ans: The garden is personified as a person changing clothes: 'the garden is changing its clothes'; it is 'putting away its dark winter suits, its dull scarves and drab brown overcoats'; it 'wraps itself in green shoots'; it 'slips on blouses sleeved with pink and white blossom'; it 'pulls on skirts of daffodil and primrose, snowdrop socks and purple crocus shoes'; and in the end it 'dances in the sunlight'. Changing clothes, wrapping, slipping on, pulling on and dancing are all human actions given to the garden.
  • Q: Q2. How does the poet intensify the image of a pleasant day by using personification?
    Ans: The poet dresses nature like a happy person in bright, new clothes — green shoots, blouses of pink and white blossom, skirts of daffodil and primrose, snowdrop socks and purple crocus shoes — and makes the garden dance in the sunlight. Because we can picture a person happily changing into colourful clothes and dancing, the pleasant spring day feels alive, joyful and much more vivid.
  • Q: Q3. What type of poem do you think this is and why?
    Ans: This is a personification poem, that is, a nature poem about spring written in the form of personification. The whole poem gives human attributes to an inanimate object: the garden changes its clothes, wears blouses, skirts, socks and shoes, and dances, just as the book defines personification poems — verses in which inanimate or non-human objects are given human attributes.
  • Q: Q4. What does the poet compare nature with? Why do you think he did this?
    Ans: The poet compares nature, that is, the garden in spring, with a person — a girl or woman — who puts away her dark and dull winter clothes and puts on bright new clothes, and then dances happily. He did this to make nature look alive and full of joy, and to help the readers picture and feel the beauty and freshness of spring in a lively way.
  • Q: Q5. Write the main idea of the poem.
    Ans: The main idea of the poem is that in spring the garden throws off its dark, dull winter covering and dresses itself in fresh green shoots and colourful flowers, and dances happily in the sunlight. In other words, spring brings new life, colour and joy to nature.
  • Q: Q6. Write down the inanimate nouns used in the poem.
    Ans: The inanimate nouns used in the poem are: garden, clothes, suits, scarves, overcoats, shoots, blouses, blossom, skirts, daffodil, primrose, snowdrop, socks, crocus, shoes and sunlight.
  • Q: Q7. Reread second and last line of the poem. What natural item is described as having a human mood? What human mood does this item have?
    Ans: The natural item is the garden. In the second line it is 'changing its clothes' and in the last line it 'dances in the sunlight', so the human mood it has is a happy, joyful and lively mood, like a person happily dancing.

Comprehension — B. Pick out all the adjectives in the lesson

  • Q: Pick out all the adjectives in the lesson and write them in your note books.
    Ans: The adjectives in the poem are: dark, dull, drab, brown, green, pink, white and purple. (Examples: dark winter suits, dull scarves, drab brown overcoats, green shoots, pink and white blossom, purple crocus shoes.)

Comprehension — C. Choose the correct option

  • Q: 1. What season does John Foster describe in the poem 'It's Spring'?
    Options: unpleasantly hot summer season / cold and nasty winter season / beautiful but sad autumn season / fresh spring season
    Ans: fresh spring season
  • Q: 2. Which sentence contains personification?
    Options: It's spring / And the garden is changing its clothes, / Putting away / Its dark winter suits,
    Ans: And the garden is changing its clothes,
  • Q: 3. The word 'drab' in the poem suggests that
    Options: nature is doubtful or weak / nature lives in a state of royalty or power / nature is changeable / nature is changing its dull cloths
    Ans: nature is changing its dull cloths

Comprehension — D. Gapped Summary: Fill in the gaps with suitable words from the text

  • Q: 1. The poet says that nothing is as beautiful as ______ season.
    Ans: spring
  • Q: 2. He says that nature is changing its ______.
    Ans: clothes
  • Q: 3. It is putting away its ______ cloths.
    Ans: winter
  • Q: 4. It wraps itself in ______ shoots.
    Ans: green
  • Q: 5. A lot of growing leaves and ______ make the sight beautiful.
    Ans: flowers

Comprehension — E. Use the idea written below to write a sentence using personification

  • Q: Write a sentence using personification: The car ______
    Ans: The car groaned and complained as it climbed the steep hill.
  • Q: Write a sentence using personification: The stairs ______
    Ans: The stairs groaned under our heavy feet as we climbed up.
  • Q: Write a sentence using personification: The flowers ______
    Ans: The flowers danced happily in the cool spring breeze.
  • Q: Write a sentence using personification: The traffic ______
    Ans: The traffic crawled slowly and waited impatiently at the signal.
  • Q: Write a sentence using personification: My house ______
    Ans: My house welcomes me with open arms when I return home in the evening.

mcqs.q: What season does John Foster describe in the poem 'It's Spring'?
mcqs.why: John Foster describes the fresh spring season, when the garden puts away its winter clothes and dresses in green shoots and flowers.

mcqs.q: Which sentence contains personification?
options: And the garden is changing its clothes
mcqs.why: A garden cannot really change clothes; giving it the human action of changing its clothes is personification, as given in the book.

mcqs.q: The word 'drab' in the poem suggests that:
options: nature lives in a state of royalty or power
nature is changing its dull clothes
mcqs.why: In the book's answer, 'drab' suggests nature is changing its dull clothes, putting away its drab brown overcoats for spring.

mcqs.q: Can the clouds really be angry?
options: No, clouds are not alive, so giving them anger is personification
mcqs.why: Clouds are not alive, so they cannot really feel anger; a cloud drawn with an angry face is personification, giving it a human feeling.

mcqs.q: What does 'shoot' mean in the poem?
options: A set of clothes worn together
A new, young stem or leaf that grows from a plant
mcqs.why: A 'shoot' is a new, young stem or leaf that grows from a plant; in spring the garden wraps itself in green shoots.

mcqs.q: What is a 'daffodil'?
options: A small white flower of early spring
A yellow flower that appears in spring
A flower on a fruit tree
mcqs.why: A daffodil is a yellow flower that appears in spring; the garden pulls on skirts of daffodil and primrose.

mcqs.q: What does 'drab' mean?
options: Without interest or colour; dull and boring
mcqs.why: In the glossary, 'drab' means without interest or colour, dull and boring, like the garden's drab brown overcoats in winter.

mcqs.q: Complete the gapped summary: 'The poet says that nothing is as beautiful as ______ season.'
mcqs.why: The gapped summary from the text says nothing is as beautiful as spring season, the season of new life, colour and joy.

mcqs.q: What human mood does the garden have in the last line of the poem?
options: A happy, joyful and lively mood
mcqs.why: In the last line the garden 'dances in the sunlight', so it has a happy, joyful and lively mood, like a person happily dancing.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an adjective used in the poem?
mcqs.why: The adjectives in the poem are dark, dull, drab, brown, green, pink, white and purple; 'dark' describes the winter suits.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar — Subject and Object Pronoun: A. Fill in the blanks with the correct subject and object pronoun

  • Q: 1. Jameel and I are friends. ______ are friends.
    Ans: We
  • Q: 2. The computer is broken. ______ is broken.
    Ans: It
  • Q: 3. She will talk to Jameela later today. She will talk to ______ later today.
    Ans: her
  • Q: 4. He does not know Palwasha and Maria. He does not know ______.
    Ans: them
  • Q: 5. The teacher helped my friend and me. The teacher helped ______.
    Ans: us

Grammar — Possessive Pronoun: Write the correct possessive pronoun into the gap

  • Q: 1. That photograph belongs to them. That photograph is ______.
    Ans: theirs
  • Q: 2. That bracelet belongs to me. That bracelet is ______.
    Ans: mine
  • Q: 3. This suitcase belongs to us. This suitcase is ______.
    Ans: ours
  • Q: 4. These boots belongs to him. These boots are ______.
    Ans: his
  • Q: 5. This computer belongs to me and my brother. This computer is ______.
    Ans: ours

Grammar — Reflexive Pronoun: Fill in the blanks with the correct reflexive pronouns

  • Q: 1. My little sister can dress ______.
    Ans: herself
  • Q: 2. I wash my clothes ______.
    Ans: myself
  • Q: 3. He repaired the computer ______.
    Ans: himself
  • Q: 4. They don't like to talk about ______.
    Ans: themselves
  • Q: 5. Sarah looks at ______ in the mirror for hours.
    Ans: herself
  • Q: 6. We hurt ______ in the accident.
    Ans: ourselves

Grammar — Question Words: Make questions for the following answers using question words

  • Q: Make a question for the answer: The best season of the year is spring.
    Ans: What is the best season of the year? (Given in the book.)
  • Q: Make a question for the answer: I am playing.
    Ans: What are you doing?
  • Q: Make a question for the answer: I am fine, thank you.
    Ans: How are you?
  • Q: Make a question for the answer: This is my book.
    Ans: What is this?
  • Q: Make a question for the answer: I will visit the library tomorrow.
    Ans: When will you visit the library?

Grammar — Indefinite Pronouns: Fill in the blanks with the correct indefinite pronouns

  • Q: 1. The store is full. We don't need to buy ______.
    Ans: anything
  • Q: 2. I forgot my purse at home. Can ______ give me a bit of money?
    Ans: someone
  • Q: 3. Isma is a very good teacher. ______ likes and admires her.
    Ans: Everyone
  • Q: 4. I went to Saleem's shop this morning but there was ______ at the shop.
    Ans: no one
  • Q: 5. ______ was ready to go for picnic.
    Ans: Everyone

Grammar — Pronoun Antecedent Agreement: Circle the correct pronoun that agrees with its antecedent

  • Q: 1. Javeria and Sarah said (she, they) were too tired to skate any longer.
    Options: she / they
    Ans: they
  • Q: 2. Every student wants to impress (his or her, their) teacher.
    Options: his or her / their
    Ans: his or her
  • Q: 3. Both Tania and Javed said (he, they) were not exercising regularly.
    Options: he / they
    Ans: they
  • Q: 4. The cat is eating from (its, their) pot.
    Options: its / their
    Ans: its
  • Q: 5. Please remind each student to bring (his or her, their) homework tomorrow.
    Options: his or her / their
    Ans: his or her

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Jameel and I are friends. ______ are friends.'
mcqs.why: Jameel and I together are the subject, so the subject pronoun 'We' is correct: 'We are friends.'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'The computer is broken. ______ is broken.'
mcqs.why: The computer is a thing and the subject of the sentence, so the subject pronoun 'It' is correct: 'It is broken.'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'She will talk to Jameela later today. She will talk to ______ later today.'
mcqs.why: Jameela is the object of 'talk to', so the object pronoun 'her' is correct in 'She will talk to her later today.'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'He does not know Palwasha and Maria. He does not know ______.'
mcqs.why: Palwasha and Maria are two people and the object of the verb, so the object pronoun 'them' is correct.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'That photograph belongs to them. That photograph is ______.'
mcqs.why: The photograph belongs to them, so the possessive pronoun is 'theirs': 'That photograph is theirs.'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'That bracelet belongs to me. That bracelet is ______.'
mcqs.why: The bracelet belongs to me, so the possessive pronoun is 'mine': 'That bracelet is mine.'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'My little sister can dress ______.'
mcqs.why: My little sister is female and singular, so the reflexive pronoun is 'herself': she can dress herself.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'We hurt ______ in the accident.'
mcqs.why: The subject is 'We', so the matching reflexive pronoun is 'ourselves': 'We hurt ourselves in the accident.'

mcqs.q: Which question fits the answer 'I will visit the library tomorrow'?
options: When will you visit the library?
mcqs.why: The answer gives a time, tomorrow, so the question word must be 'When': 'When will you visit the library?'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'The store is full. We don't need to buy ______.'
mcqs.why: In a negative sentence the correct indefinite pronoun is 'anything': 'We don't need to buy anything.'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'I forgot my purse at home. Can ______ give me a bit of money?'
mcqs.why: The sentence asks for a person who can give money, so the indefinite pronoun 'someone' is correct.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'I went to Saleem's shop this morning but there was ______ at the shop.'
mcqs.why: The shop was empty, so 'no one' is correct: there was no one at the shop that morning.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Javeria and Sarah said (she, they) were too tired to skate any longer.'
mcqs.why: The antecedent 'Javeria and Sarah' is plural, so the pronoun must be 'they' to agree with its antecedent.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The cat is eating from (its, their) pot.'
mcqs.why: The antecedent 'cat' is singular, so the singular possessive pronoun 'its' agrees with it: the cat eats from its pot.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Every student wants to impress (his or her, their) teacher.'
mcqs.why: The antecedent 'Every student' is singular, so 'his or her' is the pronoun that agrees with it in this exercise.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Write a unified paragraph on each of the pictures by personifying the nouns using verbs

  • Q: Write a unified paragraph personifying the picture of the shoe. (The first picture, the book, has been done in the book.)
    Ans: I am a shoe and I live in a shoe rack near the door. I have two eyes to see the road, a mouth that opens when my laces are untied, and a strong sole to walk and run all day. I walk to school in the morning and play in the ground in the evening. I feel tired when my owner jumps in mud and makes me dirty. I am happy when he cleans me and keeps me in the sun to dry. Someday I wish to travel to far-off places with my owner and see the whole world.
  • Q: Write a unified paragraph personifying the picture of the cherries.
    Ans: We are two cherries hanging together on one stem. We have round red faces and we smile at the sun all day. We dance and swing on our branch when the spring breeze blows. We talk to the green leaf that gives us shade and protects us from the hot sun. We are happy because children love us and wait for us to ripen. Someday someone will pick us gently and enjoy our sweet taste.
  • Q: Write a unified paragraph personifying the picture of the house holding a STOP sign.
    Ans: I am a little house standing at the corner of the road. I have two eyes to watch the street, a smiling mouth to welcome my family, and two legs to stand firm in rain and wind. I hold a STOP sign in my hand to stop the fast cars and keep the children safe. I feel happy when my family laughs inside me in the evening. I feel sad when I am left alone and locked for many days. I will always guard my family and give them shelter with love.

mcqs.q: In the paragraph about the shoe, what does the shoe say it has to see the road?
mcqs.why: The personified shoe says, 'I have two eyes to see the road, a mouth that opens when my laces are untied, and a strong sole to walk and run all day.'

mcqs.q: In the shoe paragraph, when does the shoe feel tired?
options: When its owner jumps in mud and makes it dirty
When it stays in the sun
mcqs.why: The shoe says it feels tired when its owner jumps in mud and makes it dirty; it is happy when he cleans it and keeps it in the sun to dry.

mcqs.q: In the cherries paragraph, what do the cherries do when the spring breeze blows?
options: They dance and swing on their branch
mcqs.why: The two cherries say, 'We dance and swing on our branch when the spring breeze blows,' a human action given to cherries.

mcqs.q: In the cherries paragraph, what does the green leaf do for the cherries?
options: It gives them shade and protects them from the hot sun
It makes them ripen at night
mcqs.why: The cherries talk to the green leaf that gives them shade and protects them from the hot sun, as written in the paragraph.

mcqs.q: In the house paragraph, why does the house hold a STOP sign?
options: To stop the fast cars and keep the children safe
mcqs.why: The house says, 'I hold a STOP sign in my hand to stop the fast cars and keep the children safe.'

mcqs.q: In the house paragraph, when does the house feel sad?
options: When its family laughs inside it
When it rains and winds blow
When it is left alone and locked for many days
mcqs.why: The house feels happy when its family laughs inside it in the evening and sad when it is left alone and locked for many days.

mcqs.q: Which human quality is given to the shoe in its paragraph?
options: It can see, walk, feel tired and wish to travel
mcqs.why: The shoe is personified with eyes to see, walking and running, feeling tired and happy, and wishing to travel to far-off places.

mcqs.q: What do the cherries wish will happen someday?
options: Someone will pick them gently and enjoy their sweet taste
They will travel to far places
They will be cleaned and dried
mcqs.why: The cherries say, 'Someday someone will pick us gently and enjoy our sweet taste,' because children love them and wait for them to ripen.

mcqs.q: Where does the shoe say it lives?
options: At the corner of the road
In a shoe rack near the door
Inside a house by the window
mcqs.why: The shoe begins, 'I am a shoe and I live in a shoe rack near the door,' then describes its daily walk to school and play in the ground.

mcqs.q: What is the writing task in this lesson?
options: Write a summary of a poem
Write a unified paragraph personifying the nouns using verbs
mcqs.why: The task is to write a unified paragraph on each picture by personifying the nouns using verbs, as done for the shoe, the cherries and the house.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking

  • Q: What is being personified in the pictures below?
    Ans: Four things are personified in the pictures: an alarm clock, a tree, a car and a bird. Each of them is drawn with a human face and human expressions.
  • Q: What specific human activities are they performing that they can't do in the real world?
    Ans: The alarm clock is shouting with its mouth wide open, the tree is standing sadly with arms and a tired face, the car is smiling, and the bird is looking angry. In the real world these objects cannot shout, smile, stand with arms or feel sad and angry, because these are human activities and feelings.
  • Q: Work in pairs and think of more inanimate objects and give them human qualities.
    Ans: More examples made in pairs: the wind whispered through the trees; my school bag groaned under the heavy books; the sun smiled at us in the morning; the clock stared at me during the test; the rain knocked at the window all night. In each sentence an inanimate object is given a human quality, such as whispering, groaning, smiling, staring or knocking.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Look at the pictures and name the public places.
    Ans: The pictures show a hospital, a school and a post office. These are public places, built by the government for the use of all the people.
  • Q: Q2. Who is responsible for taking care of these places?
    Ans: The government is responsible for building and maintaining these places, but it is also the duty of the people to help the government in maintaining them and to use them with care.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. How can we take care of public property?
    Ans: We can take care of public property by using it as carefully as we use our own things. We should not waste water and electricity, should not tear pages from library books, should not scribble on walls, cut bus seat covers, or throw garbage in public places. We should also pay our taxes on time so that the government has funds to maintain these properties.
  • Q: Q2. What is the importance of public property?
    Ans: Public property is built with public money that we pay in the form of taxes, and it exists for the benefit of all. Roads, hospitals, libraries, parks and government offices serve everyone jointly. It costs a lot of money to build or maintain these properties, and if they are destroyed, it will not be easy to replace them.
  • Q: Q3. What is a public place?
    Ans: A public place is a place that is dedicated to public use and is owned by the government and the people of the country jointly. For example, public parks and grounds, hospitals, libraries and government offices are public places.
  • Q: Q4. How do you feel when people litter in parks?
    Ans: I feel sad and annoyed when people litter in parks. The text tells us that some people scatter bits of paper everywhere in public parks and throw garbage in open public places. Other people have to suffer because of this unethical behaviour, and the park becomes dirty and unfit for everyone to enjoy.
  • Q: Q5. Do you respect public or others property? How?
    Ans: Yes, I respect public property and the property of others. I use public property as carefully as I use my own things. I do not damage electric lights and fans, do not tear pages from library books, do not write on walls, and I throw garbage in its proper place instead of on the road.
  • Q: Q6. What is the right way to protest if you have any demands?
    Ans: The right way is to approach the authorities peacefully. If we have any grievances or any legitimate demands, we can present them peacefully. Destruction of public property is no solution of any problem, because by destroying it we harm ourselves as well as the progress of the country.

Comprehension B — What's the place called?

  • Q: Q1. A place where children go to learn
    Ans: School
  • Q: Q2. A place where a doctor treats his patients
    Ans: Hospital
  • Q: Q3. A place where we borrow books
    Ans: Library
  • Q: Q4. A place where people can buy and eat a meal
    Ans: Restaurant
  • Q: Q5. A place where historic objects are shown
    Ans: Museum
  • Q: Q6. A place where bread and cakes are made
    Ans: Bakery
  • Q: Q7. A place where animals and birds are kept
    Ans: Zoo
  • Q: Q8. A place where people offer prayers
    Ans: Mosque
  • Q: Q9. A place where letters are posted
    Ans: Post office
  • Q: Q10. A place where we can find Police Officers
    Ans: Police station

Glossary

  • Q: Give the meaning of: amenities
    Ans: Things considered to be necessary to live comfortably.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: tearing
    Ans: To pull or be pulled apart, or to pull pieces off.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: scribble
    Ans: To write or draw something quickly or carelessly.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: monuments
    Ans: A structure or building that is built to honour a special person or event.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: frustration
    Ans: The feeling of being annoyed or less confident because you cannot achieve what you want, or something that makes you feel like this.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: legitimate
    Ans: Reasonable and acceptable, allowed by law.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: grievances
    Ans: A complaint or a feeling that you have been treated unfairly.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: recklessly
    Ans: Doing something dangerous and not worrying about the risks and the possible results.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: inconvenience
    Ans: A state or an example of problems or trouble, often causing a delay or loss of comfort.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: defaced
    Ans: To damage and spoil the appearance of something by writing or drawing on it.

mcqs.q: What is a public place?
options: A place owned by one rich person
A place dedicated to public use and owned by the government and the people jointly
A place only for government officers
A place where only children may go
mcqs.why: A public place is dedicated to public use and is owned by the government and the people of the country jointly, like parks, hospitals and libraries.

mcqs.q: How can we take care of public property?
options: By tearing pages from library books
By using it as carefully as we use our own things and paying taxes on time
mcqs.why: We should use public property as carefully as our own things, not waste water or electricity, not tear library books, and pay taxes on time for its maintenance.

mcqs.q: Why is public property important?
options: It is built with private money for one family
It exists for the benefit of all and is built with public money paid as taxes
It is easy to replace when destroyed
It belongs only to the government officers
mcqs.why: Public property is built with public money that we pay in the form of taxes and exists for the benefit of all; roads, hospitals and parks serve everyone jointly.

mcqs.q: What is the right way to protest if we have demands?
options: Approach the authorities peacefully and present demands peacefully
mcqs.why: The right way is to approach the authorities peacefully and present grievances or legitimate demands peacefully; destruction of public property is no solution.

mcqs.q: A place where children go to learn is called a:
mcqs.why: In 'What's the place called?', a place where children go to learn is a school, one of the public places shown in the pictures.

mcqs.q: A place where we borrow books is called a:
mcqs.why: A place where we borrow books is a library; tearing pages from library books is given as a way people damage public property.

mcqs.q: What does 'scribble' mean?
options: To write or draw something quickly or carelessly
mcqs.why: In the glossary, 'scribble' means to write or draw something quickly or carelessly, as people scribble on walls of public places.

mcqs.q: What does 'legitimate' mean?
options: Reasonable and acceptable, allowed by law
mcqs.why: In the glossary, 'legitimate' means reasonable and acceptable, allowed by law, as in legitimate demands presented peacefully.

mcqs.q: What does 'defaced' mean?
options: To damage and spoil the appearance of something by writing or drawing on it
To build a structure to honour an event
mcqs.why: In the glossary, 'defaced' means to damage and spoil the appearance of something by writing or drawing on it, like scribbling on walls.

mcqs.q: Who is responsible for taking care of public places?
options: Only the government, people have no duty
The government builds and maintains them, but people must also help and use them with care
mcqs.why: The government is responsible for building and maintaining these places, but it is also the duty of the people to help the government and use them with care.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:

mcqs.q: Build the minimal pair (/v/ and /w/): vet and ______
