mcqs.q: Build the minimal pair (/ya/): yard and ______
mcqs.why: Yard beginning with /ya/ pairs with 'card' in the lesson's /ya/ list, giving the pair yard — card.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A — Use dictionary skills to find the meaning, locate guide words and identify part of speech

  • Q: Q1. organize — meaning, guide words and part of speech
    Ans: Meaning: to make arrangements for something to happen, or to arrange things in a system. In the text, people organize a protest when they are angry about something. Part of speech: verb. Guide words: it is the entry word found on the dictionary page whose two guide words (the first and last entries printed at the top of the page) come just before and just after 'organize' in alphabetical order.
  • Q: Q2. collectively — meaning, guide words and part of speech
    Ans: Meaning: together, as a group. The text says public property is something we own collectively and use jointly. Part of speech: adverb. Guide words: it is the entry word found on the dictionary page whose two guide words (the first and last entries printed at the top of the page) come just before and just after 'collectively' in alphabetical order.
  • Q: Q3. protest — meaning, guide words and part of speech
    Ans: Meaning: a public action or statement that shows disagreement or anger about something. In the text, when people are angry about something they organize a protest. Part of speech: noun (it is also used as a verb). Guide words: it is the entry word found on the dictionary page whose two guide words (the first and last entries printed at the top of the page) come just before and just after 'protest' in alphabetical order.
  • Q: Q4. disrupt — meaning, guide words and part of speech
    Ans: Meaning: to interrupt something and stop it from continuing as usual. The text says that when electric and telephone lines are cut and damaged, communication gets disrupted. Part of speech: verb. Guide words: it is the entry word found on the dictionary page whose two guide words (the first and last entries printed at the top of the page) come just before and just after 'disrupt' in alphabetical order.
  • Q: Q5. damage — meaning, guide words and part of speech
    Ans: Meaning: to harm or spoil something. The text tells us that people damage electric lights and fans of public places, and telephone booths, post offices and letter-boxes are damaged. Part of speech: verb (it is also used as a noun). Guide words: it is the entry word found on the dictionary page whose two guide words (the first and last entries printed at the top of the page) come just before and just after 'damage' in alphabetical order.

mcqs.q: What does 'organize' mean?
options: to make arrangements for something to happen, or to arrange things in a system
mcqs.why: 'Organize' means to make arrangements for something to happen, or to arrange things in a system; in the text people organize a protest when angry.

mcqs.q: What part of speech is 'organize'?
mcqs.why: 'Organize' is a verb because it names an action, making arrangements for something to happen, as identified in the dictionary exercise.

mcqs.q: What does 'collectively' mean in 'something we own collectively'?
mcqs.why: 'Collectively' means together, as a group; the text says public property is something we own collectively and use jointly.

mcqs.q: What part of speech is 'collectively'?
mcqs.why: 'Collectively' is an adverb because it describes how something is owned, together as a group, and it ends in -ly like many adverbs.

mcqs.q: What does 'protest' mean?
options: a public action or statement that shows disagreement or anger about something
to interrupt something and stop it
mcqs.why: 'Protest' means a public action or statement that shows disagreement or anger about something; when people are angry they organize a protest.

mcqs.q: What does 'disrupt' mean in 'communication gets disrupted'?
options: to interrupt something and stop it from continuing as usual
mcqs.why: 'Disrupt' means to interrupt something and stop it from continuing as usual; when electric and telephone lines are cut, communication gets disrupted.

mcqs.q: What part of speech is 'disrupt'?
mcqs.why: 'Disrupt' is a verb because it names the action of interrupting something and stopping it from continuing as usual.

mcqs.q: What does 'damage' mean?
mcqs.why: 'Damage' means to harm or spoil something; the text tells us people damage electric lights and fans of public places.

mcqs.q: Which word in the lesson is a verb meaning to harm or spoil something?
mcqs.why: 'Damage' is used as a verb meaning to harm or spoil something, though it is also used as a noun, as noted in the exercise.

mcqs.q: In the text, what gets disrupted when electric and telephone lines are cut and damaged?
mcqs.why: The text says that when electric and telephone lines are cut and damaged, communication gets disrupted, that is, interrupted.

mcqs.q: In the text, when do people organize a protest?
options: When they are angry about something
mcqs.why: In the text, people organize a protest when they are angry about something, showing disagreement or anger publicly.

mcqs.q: What are guide words in a dictionary?
options: The first and last entries printed at the top of a dictionary page
The part of speech of a word
mcqs.why: Guide words are the first and last entries printed at the top of a dictionary page; an entry word is found on the page whose guide words come just before and just after it in alphabetical order.

mcqs.q: Which word is an adverb in this lesson?
mcqs.why: 'Collectively' is the adverb in this lesson, meaning together as a group, while organize and disrupt are verbs and protest is mainly a noun.

mcqs.q: Which word can be used as both a noun and a verb in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The exercise notes that 'protest' is a noun and is also used as a verb, and 'damage' is likewise a verb also used as a noun.

mcqs.q: Which things does the text say are damaged by people?
options: Electric lights and fans, telephone booths, post offices and letter-boxes
mcqs.why: The text tells us people damage electric lights and fans of public places, and telephone booths, post offices and letter-boxes are damaged.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A — Draw a mind map for 'Duties of a Good Citizen' and write a simple and unified paragraph on 'Duties of a Good Citizen'

  • Q: Write a simple and unified paragraph on "Duties of a Good Citizen".
    Ans: Mind map (main theme in the centre: Duties of a Good Citizen): be kind; be helpful; be a responsible citizen; do his duties honestly; obey the rules; use public property with care. Paragraph: A good citizen loves his country and does his duties honestly. He obeys the rules and laws of the country. He is kind and helpful to other people. He uses public property as carefully as he uses his own things, because public property belongs to everyone. He does not damage roads, parks, hospitals, schools or libraries. He pays his taxes on time so that the government can build and maintain public property. He keeps public places clean and does not throw garbage on the road. If he has any grievance or demand, he approaches the authorities peacefully instead of destroying public property. In this way, a good citizen helps in the progress of his country.

mcqs.q: What is the main theme placed in the centre of the mind map in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The mind map has 'Duties of a Good Citizen' as the main theme in the centre, with the citizen's duties arranged around it.

mcqs.q: According to the paragraph, a good citizen loves his country and:
mcqs.why: The paragraph begins: a good citizen loves his country and does his duties honestly, and he obeys the rules and laws of the country.

mcqs.q: How does a good citizen use public property?
options: As carefully as he uses his own things
mcqs.why: A good citizen uses public property as carefully as he uses his own things, because public property belongs to everyone.

mcqs.q: Why does a good citizen pay his taxes on time?
options: So he can organize a protest
So the government can build and maintain public property
So he can damage lights and fans
mcqs.why: He pays his taxes on time so that the government can build and maintain public property for the benefit of all people.

mcqs.q: What does a good citizen do if he has a grievance or demand?
options: He throws garbage on the road
mcqs.why: If he has any grievance or demand, he approaches the authorities peacefully instead of destroying public property.

mcqs.q: Which of these is listed as a branch in the mind map?
mcqs.why: The mind map branches are: be kind; be helpful; be a responsible citizen; do his duties honestly; obey the rules; use public property with care.

mcqs.q: According to the paragraph, a good citizen is kind and ______ to other people.
mcqs.why: The paragraph says he is kind and helpful to other people, matching the 'be kind' and 'be helpful' branches of the mind map.

mcqs.q: What does a good citizen NOT do, according to the paragraph?
options: Damage roads, parks, hospitals, schools or libraries
mcqs.why: He does not damage roads, parks, hospitals, schools or libraries; he keeps public places clean and does not throw garbage on the road.

mcqs.q: How does a good citizen help in the progress of his country, according to the paragraph?
options: By destroying public property when angry
By doing all these duties honestly and peacefully
mcqs.why: By obeying rules, using public property with care, paying taxes and approaching authorities peacefully, a good citizen helps in the progress of his country.

mcqs.q: Which places are named in the paragraph as public property a good citizen does not damage?
options: Roads, parks, hospitals, schools and libraries
mcqs.why: The paragraph names roads, parks, hospitals, schools and libraries as public property that a good citizen does not damage.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — In a group of four complete the bubble and discuss the issues

  • Q: Q1. Complete the speech bubble: a boy is scribbling on a wall and a man speaks to him.
    Ans: "Wow! this looks like you are having fun." "But my dear boy, instead of scribbling on walls, put your ideas on a piece of paper." (This is the text printed in the book. Discuss in your group why scribbling on public walls is wrong: it defaces public property, which belongs to everyone.)
  • Q: Q2. Complete the speech bubble: a man throws a banana peel on the path and another man slips on it.
    Ans: Model bubble for the man who slipped: "What have you done? You dropped the banana peel on the way and I slipped on it. Please throw such things to a side, in a dustbin, so that the way stays safe for everyone." Discuss in your group: throwing garbage on the road makes others suffer, so public places must be kept clean.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. What is meant by healthy and unhealthy food?
    Ans: Healthy food is food that gives us the correct amount of nutrients — protein, fat, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals — that we need to maintain good health. A healthy or balanced diet contains the right amounts of all the food groups, i.e. fruit, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein, and does not include too much or too little of any kind of food. Unhealthy food is the opposite: food like only burgers and sandwiches taken whenever we feel hungry, which does not give us the right amounts of all the food groups.

Glossary

  • Q: Give the meaning of: temper
    Ans: The tendency to become angry / happy very quickly.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: proportion
    Ans: The number or amount of a group or part of something when compared to the whole.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: idle
    Ans: Not working or being used.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: appreciate
    Ans: Used when you are thanking someone or showing that you are grateful.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: sufficient
    Ans: To have enough.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What possible diseases may unbalanced diet cause?
    Ans: The text does not name any particular disease. It tells us that Sameena feels very weak because she is skipping meals and does not get enough time to eat properly. Tahira says that good nutrition reduces the risk of diseases and promotes health, and that exercise helps people lose weight and lowers the risk of some diseases. So an unbalanced diet makes a person weak and increases the risk of diseases.
  • Q: Q2. What piece of advice does the author give at the end of the text?
    Ans: At the end of the text, Tahira advises Sameena not to forget the saying: "Early to bed and early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise". In other words, she advises her to take a balanced diet, exercise regularly and go to bed early and rise early.
  • Q: Q3. Explain the saying: "Early to bed and early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise".
    Ans: The saying means that a person who goes to sleep early at night and gets up early in the morning lives a healthy and regular life. Such a person stays fresh and active, so he remains healthy. He gets more time to work, so he can become wealthy. His mind also works well, so he becomes wise. In short, early rising is the key to health, wealth and wisdom.
  • Q: Q4. Is it better to be healthy than wealthy? Why?
    Ans: Yes, it is better to be healthy than wealthy. Tahira says that good health is the greatest blessing of Allah and a treasure. A healthy person excels in every field of life: as a student, he/she shines in his examinations, and as a public worker, he/she renders valuable service and is duly rewarded. A healthy person keeps a cheerful temper and goes through life's journey with joy, because a sound mind lives in a sound body. Wealth without health cannot give this happiness.
  • Q: Q5. Why are burgers and sandwiches considered unbalanced diet? Explain.
    Ans: Burgers and sandwiches are considered an unbalanced diet because they do not contain the right amounts of all the food groups. A balanced diet contains the right amounts of fruit, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein, and it does not include too much or too little of any kind of food. Sameena just takes a sandwich or burger whenever she feels hungry, so she does not get the correct amount of all the nutrients — protein, fat, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals — that she needs to maintain good health.
  • Q: Q6. What food do you take daily? Does it contain correct amount of nutrients?
    Ans: Model answer: I daily take bread or rice with vegetables, pulses, milk and sometimes meat, along with seasonal fruit. Yes, mostly it contains the correct amount of nutrients, because it includes the different food groups — grains, vegetables, dairy products, fruit and protein. I also drink about eight glasses of water daily, as advised in the text. When I only take a burger or sandwich in a hurry, my diet for that day is not balanced.

Comprehension B — Use summary skills to complete the cloze paragraph

  • Q: Healthy eating is about ______ the correct amount of nutrients
    Ans: getting
  • Q: Healthy eating is about getting the correct amount of ______ — protein, fat, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals
    Ans: nutrients
  • Q: — protein, fat, carbohydrates, vitamins ______ minerals you need to maintain good health
    Ans: and
  • Q: — vitamins and minerals you need to ______ good health
    Ans: maintain
  • Q: Foods that ______ the same type of nutrients are grouped together
    Ans: contain
  • Q: Foods that contain the same type of ______ are grouped together on each of the shelves of the Food Pyramid
    Ans: nutrients
  • Q: Foods are grouped together on ______ of the shelves of the Food Pyramid
    Ans: each
  • Q: Foods are grouped together on each of the shelves of ______ Food Pyramid
    Ans: the

Comprehension C — Choose the correct option

  • Q: Q1. The text is in the form of a ______.
    Options: story / dialogue / letter / narrative
    Ans: dialogue
  • Q: Q2. Healthy eating is about getting the correct amount of ______.
    Options: proteins / carbohydrates / minerals / all nutrients
    Ans: all nutrients
  • Q: Q3. We should drink atleast ______ glasses of water daily.
    Options: six / seven / eight / nine
    Ans: eight
  • Q: Q4. Food that contain same type of the nutrients is grouped together in ______.
    Options: balanced diet / food pyramid / healthy diet / unhealthy diet
    Ans: food pyramid
  • Q: Q5. To lead a healthy life we should ______.
    Options: take balanced diet / exercise daily / sleep and rise early / eat burgers only
    Ans: take balanced diet

Comprehension D — Read silently and with comprehension to extract main idea and supporting detail

  • Q: Q1. Read the paragraph and extract its main idea and supporting detail. Paragraph: "I think you are forgetting the fact that good health is the greatest blessing of Allah and a treasure. A healthy person excel in every field of life. As a student, he/she shines in his examinations. As a public worker, he/she renders valuable service and is duly rewarded. He/she keeps a cheerful temper and goes through life's journey with joy."
    Ans: Main idea: Good health is the greatest blessing of Allah and a treasure, and a healthy person succeeds in every field of life. Supporting details: a healthy student shines in his examinations; a healthy public worker renders valuable service and is duly rewarded; and a healthy person keeps a cheerful temper and goes through life's journey with joy.

mcqs.q: The text about healthy eating is in the form of a ______.
mcqs.why: The text is a conversation between Sameena and Tahira, so it is written as a dialogue, not as a story, letter or narrative.

mcqs.q: Healthy eating is about getting the correct amount of ______.
mcqs.why: Healthy eating means getting the correct amount of all the nutrients — protein, fat, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals — needed to maintain good health.

mcqs.q: We should drink at least ______ glasses of water daily.
mcqs.why: The text advises drinking about eight glasses of water daily, which is the amount mentioned in the model daily diet as well.

mcqs.q: Foods that contain the same type of nutrients are grouped together in the ______.
mcqs.why: On each shelf of the Food Pyramid, foods that contain the same type of nutrients are grouped together, as the cloze paragraph states.

mcqs.q: To lead a healthy life we should ______.
mcqs.why: The book's key gives taking a balanced diet as the answer, because a balanced diet gives the right amounts of all the food groups.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'temper' mean?
options: The number or amount compared to the whole
The tendency to become angry or happy very quickly
mcqs.why: In the glossary, 'temper' means the tendency to become angry or happy very quickly, as in keeping a cheerful temper.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'sufficient' mean?
options: A part compared to the whole
mcqs.why: The glossary explains 'sufficient' as to have enough, which is different from 'appreciate', 'idle' and 'proportion'.

mcqs.q: Why does Sameena feel very weak?
options: She is skipping meals and does not eat properly
mcqs.why: Sameena feels weak because she is skipping meals and does not get enough time to eat properly, so her diet is unbalanced.

mcqs.q: According to the saying, early to bed and early to rise makes a man ______.
mcqs.why: Tahira ends with the saying that early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise, giving health, time to work and a fresh mind.

mcqs.q: A balanced diet contains the right amounts of ______.
options: fruit, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein
too much of one kind of food
mcqs.why: A healthy or balanced diet contains the right amounts of all the food groups: fruit, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein, with not too much or too little of any kind.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — Context / comparison clues: deduce the meaning of underlined words and find their synonyms and antonyms from thesaurus

  • Q: Q1. The girls languidly put on their jackets as if they had no energy at all. Using the comparison clue, what does the word 'languidly' mean? Also give its synonym and antonym.
    Ans: The word 'languidly' in this sentence means unenergetically. Deduced meaning: tiredly. Synonym: lazily. Antonym: actively. (The comparison clue is 'as if they had no energy at all'.)
  • Q: Q2. The mother was determined to prove her son's innocence; the father was resolute as well. Using the comparison clue, the word 'resolute' in this sentence means ______.
    Options: wavering / determined / not determined / unsure
    Ans: determined
  • Q: Q2 (continued). Give a synonym and an antonym of 'resolute'.
    Ans: Synonym of 'resolute': determined (firm). Antonym of 'resolute': wavering (unsure).
  • Q: Q3. Some people feel perplexed by brain teasers, while others figure them out quickly. Using the comparison clue, the word 'perplexed' in this sentence means ______.
    Options: troubled / at ease / calm / relaxed
    Ans: troubled
  • Q: Q3 (continued). Give a synonym and an antonym of 'perplexed'.
    Ans: Synonym of 'perplexed': puzzled (confused). Antonym of 'perplexed': at ease (clear and relaxed).
  • Q: Q4. After being unable to get a good night's sleep for many days, Ahmad became lethargic. Using the comparison clue, the word 'lethargic' in this sentence means ______.
    Options: active / bubbly / exhausted / lively
    Ans: exhausted
  • Q: Q4 (continued). Give a synonym and an antonym of 'lethargic'.
    Ans: Synonym of 'lethargic': sluggish (tired and without energy). Antonym of 'lethargic': lively (active).

Grammar — Linking verbs: Read the sentences and circle the linking verb

  • Q: Q1. Javeria enjoyed the game, but the popcorn tasted bad. Circle the linking verb.
    Options: enjoyed / tasted / game / popcorn
    Ans: tasted
  • Q: Q2. Mohsin didn't get cut even though the knife felt sharp. Circle the linking verb.
    Options: didn't / cut / felt / sharp
    Ans: felt
  • Q: Q3. Bacteria grew on the bread, and it turned moldy. Circle the linking verb.
    Options: turned / bacteria / grew / bread
    Ans: turned
  • Q: Q4. The man worked all day and looked tired. Circle the linking verb.
    Options: worked / all / looked / day
    Ans: looked
  • Q: Q5. His friend argued a lot but he remained silent. Circle the linking verb.
    Options: argued / remained / silent / friend
    Ans: remained

Grammar — Modal verbs A: Identify the verb in each sentence (modal verbs once and action verbs twice)

  • Q: Q1. He shall bring the food very soon. Identify the modal verb and the action verb.
    Ans: Modal verb: shall. Action verb: bring.
  • Q: Q2. We can definitely win the game. Identify the modal verb and the action verb.
    Ans: Modal verb: can. Action verb: win.
  • Q: Q3. May I sit down now? Identify the modal verb and the action verb.
    Ans: Modal verb: May. Action verb: sit.
  • Q: Q4. I must go now. Identify the modal verb and the action verb.
    Ans: Modal verb: must. Action verb: go.
  • Q: Q5. Could you pass me the ketchup? Identify the modal verb and the action verb.
    Ans: Modal verb: Could. Action verb: pass.

Grammar — Modal verbs B: Complete each sentence with a modal verb

  • Q: People ______ walk on grass.
    Ans: can
  • Q: Drivers ______ stop when the traffic lights are red.
    Ans: must
  • Q: ______ I ask a question? Yes, of course.
    Ans: May
  • Q: You ______ take your umbrella. It is not raining.
    Ans: shouldn't
  • Q: Q5. ______ you speak Italian? No, I ______. Complete the sentence with modal verbs.
    Ans: Can you speak Italian? No, I cannot (can't).

Grammar — Modal verbs C: Make affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences using need and dare

  • Q: Q1. Make affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences using 'need'.
    Ans: Using 'need': Affirmative — I need to have my hair cut. Negative — You needn't worry about that. Interrogative — Need you make so much noise? (These are the examples given in the book.)
  • Q: Q2. Make affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences using 'dare'.
    Ans: Using 'dare': Affirmative — I dare say this. Negative — I dare not say this. Interrogative — Dare she say this? (These are the examples given in the book.)

Grammar — Transitive and intransitive verbs A: Decide whether the verbs in bold are transitive or intransitive

  • Q: Q1. She was crying. Is the verb in bold (crying) transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Intransitive — 'crying' has no object.
  • Q: Q2. We showed her the photo album. Is the verb in bold (showed) transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Transitive — 'showed' has the objects 'her' and 'the photo album'.
  • Q: Q3. It was raining. Is the verb in bold (raining) transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Intransitive — 'raining' has no object.
  • Q: Q4. She laughed at the joke. Is the verb in bold (laughed) transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Intransitive — 'laughed' has no object; 'at the joke' is a prepositional phrase.
  • Q: Q5. She gave a cookie to the child. Is the verb in bold (gave) transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Transitive — 'gave' has the object 'a cookie'.

Grammar — Transitive and intransitive verbs B: State whether the verb is used transitively or intransitively and pick out the objects

  • Q: Q1. The wind is blowing fiercely. State whether the verb is used transitively or intransitively, and pick out the object if there is any.
    Ans: Intransitive. There is no object.
  • Q: Q2. Somebody opened the door. State whether the verb is used transitively or intransitively, and pick out the object if there is any.
    Ans: Transitive. Object: the door.
  • Q: Q3. The boy went to the park. State whether the verb is used transitively or intransitively, and pick out the object if there is any.
    Ans: Intransitive. There is no object; 'to the park' is a prepositional phrase, not an object.
  • Q: Q4. I like climbing mountains. State whether the verb is used transitively or intransitively, and pick out the object if there is any.
    Ans: Transitive. Object: climbing mountains (mountains).
  • Q: Q5. I am going to buy flowers. State whether the verb is used transitively or intransitively, and pick out the object if there is any.
    Ans: Transitive. Object: flowers.

Grammar — Complete the following sentences with the help of words in the box (the correct number, a teacher, my good friend, late, for three hours, my younger sister)

  • Q: They came ______.
    Ans: late
  • Q: He walked ______.
    Ans: for three hours
  • Q: Sadia is ______.
    Ans: my younger sister
  • Q: Rabab is ______.
    Ans: my good friend
  • Q: It seems to be ______.
    Ans: the correct number
  • Q: He became ______.
    Ans: a teacher

Revision Unit 1-5 A — Identify the underlined word in each sentence as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun

  • Q: Q1. The Zalmi will play cricket tonight. Identify the underlined word (Zalmi) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Proper noun
  • Q: Q2. The family will eat together. Identify the underlined word (family) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Common noun
  • Q: Q3. We travelled down the Indus River. Identify the underlined word (Indus River) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Proper noun
  • Q: Q4. I will walk home after school. Identify the underlined word (school) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Common noun (countable)
  • Q: Q5. I live in Haripur District. Identify the underlined word (Haripur District) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Proper noun
  • Q: Q6. They will reach on Monday. Identify the underlined word (Monday) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Proper noun
  • Q: Q7. The children are playing in the garden. Identify the underlined word (children) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Common noun (countable)
  • Q: Q8. I prefer to have tea. Identify the underlined word (tea) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Uncountable noun
  • Q: Q9. We need some glue to fix this vase. Identify the underlined word (glue) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Uncountable noun
  • Q: Q10. I bought three bottles of water. Identify the underlined word (three bottles) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Countable noun
  • Q: Q11. A rise in oil prices is inevitable. Identify the underlined word (oil) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Uncountable noun
  • Q: Q12. My mother uses butter to prepare cakes. Identify the underlined word (butter) as a proper, common, countable or uncountable noun.
    Ans: Uncountable noun

Revision Unit 1-5 B — Complete the following sentences, making the underlined singular noun plural

  • Q: Q1. The student studied for the history midterm. (Many ______ studied for the history midterm.)
    Ans: Many students studied for the history midterm.
  • Q: Q2. I studied a story book while I was sick. (I studied several ______ while I was sick.)
    Ans: I studied several story books while I was sick.
  • Q: Q3. The library has a collection of rare books. (Most ______ have ______ of rare books.)
    Ans: Most libraries have collections of rare books.
  • Q: Q4. I wrote an essay for my history class. (I wrote many ______ for my history class.)
    Ans: I wrote many essays for my history class.
  • Q: Q5. The woman ran a day-care center. (The three ______ ran a day-care center together.)
    Ans: The three women ran a day-care center together.

Revision Unit 1-5 C — Complete the following sentences using appropriate collective nouns (bunch, flock, swarm, crowd, plague, bouquet)

  • Q: A large ______ gathered in the street.
    Ans: crowd
  • Q: The hungry fox saw a ______ of grapes hanging from the vine.
    Ans: bunch
  • Q: We were attacked by a ______ of bees.
    Ans: swarm
  • Q: A ______ of locusts attacked the crops.
    Ans: plague
  • Q: A ______ of birds is always a beautiful sight.
    Ans: flock
  • Q: They welcomed the chief guest with a ______ of flowers.
    Ans: bouquet

Revision Unit 1-5 D — Choose the correct modal verb for each of these sentences

  • Q: Q1. When he was young, he ______ swim very well. He won medals and championships!
    Options: had to / can / could / must
    Ans: could
  • Q: Q2. The company ______ go bankrupt if they don't find a lot of money quickly!
    Options: should / shouldn't / might / must
    Ans: might
  • Q: Q3. You look very confused by the homework, Arshad. ______ I help you?
    Options: will / can / must / can't
    Ans: can
  • Q: Q4. I left my purse at home. Lily, ______ you lend me ten dollars?
    Options: may / could / shouldn't / may not
    Ans: could
  • Q: Q5. It's wet and windy outside today. You ______ go out without an umbrella.
    Options: shouldn't / won't / can / don't have to
    Ans: shouldn't
  • Q: Q6. I think that sign means we ______ enter the building. Look, there's a security.
    Options: won't / have to / mustn't / should
    Ans: mustn't

mcqs.q: The mother was determined to prove her son's innocence; the father was resolute as well. The word 'resolute' means ______.
mcqs.why: The comparison clue is that the mother was determined and the father was resolute 'as well', so resolute means determined, the opposite of wavering.

mcqs.q: Some people feel perplexed by brain teasers, while others figure them out quickly. The word 'perplexed' means ______.
mcqs.why: The contrast with people who figure teasers out quickly shows that perplexed people are troubled or puzzled, not at ease, calm or relaxed.

mcqs.q: After being unable to get a good night's sleep for many days, Ahmad became lethargic. The word 'lethargic' means ______.
mcqs.why: Many days without a good night's sleep leave a person exhausted and without energy, which is the meaning of lethargic; its antonym is lively.

mcqs.q: The girls languidly put on their jackets as if they had no energy at all. A synonym of 'languidly' is ______.
mcqs.why: The clue 'as if they had no energy at all' shows languidly means unenergetically, and its synonym given in the notes is lazily.

mcqs.q: Javeria enjoyed the game, but the popcorn tasted bad. The linking verb is ______.
mcqs.why: 'Tasted' links the popcorn to how it was, so it is the linking verb; 'enjoyed' is an action verb in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Mohsin didn't get cut even though the knife felt sharp. The linking verb is ______.
mcqs.why: 'Felt' links the knife to the description 'sharp', so felt is the linking verb circled in the notes for this sentence.

mcqs.q: Bacteria grew on the bread, and it turned moldy. The linking verb is ______.
mcqs.why: 'Turned' links 'it' to 'moldy' and shows a change of state, so turned is the linking verb, while grew is an action verb.

mcqs.q: He shall bring the food very soon. The modal verb in this sentence is ______.
mcqs.why: In this sentence 'shall' is the modal verb used once, and 'bring' is the action verb that follows it.

mcqs.q: Drivers ______ stop when the traffic lights are red.
mcqs.why: Drivers must stop when the traffic lights are red, because stopping at a red light is a necessary duty, not a free choice.

mcqs.q: She was crying. The verb 'crying' is ______.
mcqs.why: 'Crying' has no object after it, so it is used intransitively in the sentence 'She was crying.'

mcqs.q: Somebody opened the door. The verb 'opened' is transitive and its object is ______.
mcqs.why: 'Opened' is used transitively here because it has an object, and the thing that was opened is the door.

mcqs.q: The Zalmi will play cricket tonight. The word 'Zalmi' is a ______.
mcqs.why: 'Zalmi' is the name of a particular team, so it is a proper noun, like Indus River, Haripur District and Monday in the revision exercise.

mcqs.q: I prefer to have tea. The word 'tea' is a ______.
mcqs.why: Tea cannot be counted as separate items in this use, so it is an uncountable noun, like glue, oil and butter in the same exercise.

mcqs.q: We were attacked by a ______ of bees.
mcqs.why: The collective noun for a group of bees that attacks is a swarm; a bunch is for grapes, a flock for birds and a bouquet for flowers.

mcqs.q: When he was young, he ______ swim very well. He won medals and championships!
mcqs.why: The sentence talks about a past ability when he was young, so 'could' is correct; 'can' is used for present ability.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Write a dialogue between two friends on the importance of healthy eating

  • Q: Write a dialogue between two friends on the importance of healthy eating.
    Ans: Ali: Assalam-o-Alaikum, Bilal! You look very weak and tired today. Bilal: Wa-Alaikum-Assalam, Ali. You are right. I often skip my meals and just take a burger whenever I feel hungry. Ali: That is very careless of you. Good health is the greatest blessing of Allah and a treasure. Bilal: I agree, but tell me what I should eat in order to stay fit and healthy. Ali: Eat a balanced diet. It contains the right amounts of all the food groups — fruit, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein. Bilal: What is the Food Pyramid? Ali: The Food Pyramid makes healthy eating easier. Foods that contain the same type of nutrients are grouped together on each of its shelves. Bilal: How much water should I drink? Ali: You should take at least eight glasses of water daily. Also take regular exercise, because exercise helps us lose weight and lowers the risk of some diseases. Bilal: Thank you, Ali. I will also remember the saying, "Early to bed and early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise". Ali: You are most welcome, my dear friend.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, why does Bilal look very weak and tired?
options: He often skips his meals and just takes a burger when hungry
He drinks eight glasses of water
mcqs.why: Bilal himself says he often skips his meals and just takes a burger whenever he feels hungry, which is why he looks weak and tired.

mcqs.q: What does Ali call good health in the dialogue?
options: The greatest blessing of Allah and a treasure
mcqs.why: Ali tells Bilal that good health is the greatest blessing of Allah and a treasure, echoing the main idea of the lesson text.

mcqs.q: According to Ali, a balanced diet contains the right amounts of ______.
options: fruit, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein
mcqs.why: Ali explains that a balanced diet contains the right amounts of all the food groups: fruit, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein.

mcqs.q: What does the Food Pyramid do, according to the dialogue?
options: It tells us to skip meals
It groups foods with the same type of nutrients on each of its shelves
mcqs.why: Ali explains that the Food Pyramid makes healthy eating easier because foods containing the same type of nutrients are grouped together on each shelf.

mcqs.q: How much water does Ali advise Bilal to drink daily?
mcqs.why: Ali advises Bilal to take at least eight glasses of water daily, the same advice given in the lesson text.

mcqs.q: According to the dialogue, regular exercise helps us to ______.
options: lose weight and lowers the risk of some diseases
mcqs.why: Ali says to take regular exercise because exercise helps us lose weight and lowers the risk of some diseases, as Tahira also says in the text.

mcqs.q: Which saying does Bilal promise to remember at the end of the dialogue?
options: A burger a day keeps weakness away
Early to bed and early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise
mcqs.why: Bilal ends by saying he will remember the saying about going early to bed and rising early, which makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise.

mcqs.q: Who looks weak and tired at the start of the dialogue?
mcqs.why: The dialogue opens with Ali greeting Bilal and telling him that he looks very weak and tired today, and Bilal agrees.

mcqs.q: What does Bilal take whenever he feels hungry?
mcqs.why: Bilal says he just takes a burger whenever he feels hungry instead of eating proper meals, which makes his diet unbalanced.

mcqs.q: What does Ali advise Bilal to eat in order to stay fit and healthy?
mcqs.why: When Bilal asks what he should eat to stay fit and healthy, Ali advises him to eat a balanced diet with the right amounts of all food groups.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Informal and formal dialogues

  • Q: Q1. Read the informal dialogue between two friends. Identify the characters, their relationship, the context, and the language features of oral speech.
    Ans: The informal dialogue is between two friends (one of them is Ahmed). Characters and relationship: they are close friends, so the conversation is casual. Context: they meet and greet each other informally. Language: short, casual sentences of oral speech are used, such as "Bad, really bad!", "Come on, it can't be that bad!" and "Do you think I'm joking?" The tone is free and friendly, with no formal words of respect.
  • Q: Q2. Read the formal dialogue between counter clerk and customer. Identify the characters, their relationship, the context, and why this dialogue is formal.
    Ans: The formal dialogue is between a counter clerk and a customer in a bank. Characters and relationship: the clerk is serving the customer; they are strangers, and the customer is treated with respect. Context: the customer has come to cash a cheque and asks about the teller system. Language: the conversation is polite and respectful, with formal expressions such as "Good morning Sir! How can I help you?", "Please go to the first counter on the left" and "You are welcome. Have a nice day, sir."

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Have you ever seen a corn field?
    Ans: Yes, I have seen a cornfield. It is a field full of tall green corn plants with long leaves and cobs, stretching far to the right and left, just as the poet describes in the poem.
  • Q: Q2. Do you like eating corns?
    Ans: Yes, I like eating corn. Boiled or roasted corn is sweet and tasty, and it is grown in the green cornfields like the one described in this poem.
  • Q: Q3. Do you remember any poetic device you have read earlier?
    Ans: Yes. One poetic device is alliteration, which is used in this unit. It is a literary device in which a number of words having the same first consonant sound occur close together in a series, for example, 'But a better butter makes a batter better.'

Reading: Deduce the meaning of the following words

  • Q: Q1. Deduce the meaning of the word: sing
    Ans: To make musical sounds with the voice. In the poem, the skylark sings above the corn: 'A singing speck above the corn.'
  • Q: Q2. Deduce the meaning of the word: walk
    Ans: To move along on foot. In the poem, the poet walks through the cornfield: 'To right and left beside my walks.'
  • Q: Q3. Deduce the meaning of the word: nest
    Ans: A place built by a bird to live in and lay its eggs. In the poem, the skylark has a nest hidden among the corn stalks: 'I knew he had a nest unseen / Somewhere among the million stalks.'
  • Q: Q4. Deduce the meaning of the word: longer
    Ans: For a greater length of time. In the poem, the skylark's mate listened for more time than the poet did: 'And listened longer than I did.'
  • Q: Q5. Deduce the meaning of the word: sunny
    Ans: Bright with sunlight. In the poem, it is a sunny morning: 'I saw and heard one sunny morn.'

Glossary

  • Q: What does 'morn' mean?
    Ans: A morning.
  • Q: What does 'skylark' mean?
    Ans: A small, brown bird that is known for its beautiful singing.
  • Q: What does 'speck' mean?
    Ans: A very small mark, piece, or amount.
  • Q: What does 'gay' mean?
    Ans: Happy. If a place is gay, it is bright and attractive.
  • Q: What does 'accord' mean?
    Ans: Agreement.
  • Q: What does 'soared' mean?
    Ans: (Of a bird or aircraft) to rise high in the air while flying without moving the wings or using power.
  • Q: What does 'sank' mean?
    Ans: To (cause something or someone to) go down below the surface or to the bottom of a liquid or soft substance.
  • Q: What does 'stretched' mean?
    Ans: To cause something to reach, often as far as possible, in a particular direction.
  • Q: What does 'tender' mean?
    Ans: Gentle, loving, or kind.
  • Q: What does 'stalks' mean?
    Ans: The main stem of a plant, or the narrow stem that joins leaves, flowers, or fruit to the main stem of a plant.
  • Q: What does 'swift' mean?
    Ans: Happening or moving quickly or within a short time, especially in a smooth and easy way.
  • Q: What does 'slid' mean?
    Ans: To (cause to) move easily and without interruption over a surface.
  • Q: What does 'mate' mean?
    Ans: Partner.
  • Q: What does 'moments' mean?
    Ans: A very short period of time, a particular time or occasion.

Comprehension A: Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Write down the main idea of the poem.
    Ans: The main idea of the poem is the beauty and peace of nature on a sunny morning. The poet walks through a green cornfield under a blue sky and enjoys the sweet song of a skylark flying above the corn, while white butterflies dance below. She pauses to listen to the bird's song and feels happy and content in the beautiful natural scene.
  • Q: Q2. The poet has used alliteration in the following stanza. One example has been underlined. Find another example from the same stanza. (A stage below, in gay accord, / White butterflies danced on the wing, / And still the singing skylark soared, / And silent sank and soared to sing.)
    Ans: Another example of alliteration in the same stanza is 'And silent sank and soared to sing', where the 's' sound is repeated in silent, sank, soared and sing. The words 'White' and 'wing' in 'White butterflies danced on the wing' also repeat the same first sound.
  • Q: Q3. What effect is the poet trying to achieve with the technique of alliteration?
    Ans: Through alliteration, the poet makes the poem musical and smooth so that it flows quickly as the sounds are repeated. The repeated sounds emphasise the words, create clear pictures of the skylark and the cornfield in the reader's mind, and create a light, happy mood, just like the bird's song.
  • Q: Q4. How do we know that the poet leaves the cornfield before the skylark has stopped singing?
    Ans: In the last stanza the poet says that the skylark's mate 'sat listening long, / And listened longer than I did.' This shows that the poet stopped listening and left, while the mate was still listening to the skylark's song. So the poet leaves the cornfield before the skylark stops singing.
  • Q: Q5. List the colours that have been used in the poem. What do you think?
    Ans: The colours used in the poem are green (the green earth and the tender green cornfield), blue (the blue sky) and white (the white butterflies). I think these fresh and bright colours make the scene look beautiful, peaceful and full of life, and they show the poet's happiness on the sunny morning.
  • Q: Q6. Where did the poet pause? Explain.
    Ans: The poet paused in the cornfield, on her walk, with the cornfield stretching a tender green to the right and left beside her. She paused there to hear the skylark's song: 'And as I paused to hear his song / While swift the sunny moments slid.'

Comprehension B: Gapped Summary — Choose the correct word to complete the summary of the poem

  • Q: 1. The poet describes how ______ she feels as she walks through a cornfield.
    Options: content / sad / lonely
    Ans: content
  • Q: 2. As she walks along, she sees a skylark ______.
    Options: flying away from the cornfield / flying in the sky / falling towards her
    Ans: flying in the sky
  • Q: 3. It doesn't sing as it flies ______.
    Options: lower / higher
    Ans: lower
  • Q: 4. Below it, butterflies ______ in the cornfield.
    Options: sit quietly / move slowly / move quickly
    Ans: move quickly
  • Q: 5. The poet knows that the skylark's nest is ______ the cornfield.
    Options: visible in / hidden in / far away from
    Ans: hidden in
  • Q: 6. She ______ that its companion is also listening somewhere in the cornfield.
    Options: notices / imagines / knows
    Ans: imagines

Comprehension C: Choose the correct options

  • Q: 1. The pronoun 'his' in the line 'And as I paused to hear his song' has been used for the ______.
    Options: poet / skylark / butterfly / parrot
    Ans: skylark
  • Q: 2. In the lines 'The cornfield stretched a tender green / To right and left beside my walks', 'my walks' refers to the ______.
    Options: paces / path / steps / fields
    Ans: path
  • Q: 3. The pronoun 'he' in the line 'I knew he had a nest unseen' has been used for the ______.
    Options: butterfly / poet / skylark / cornfield
    Ans: skylark
  • Q: 4. 'I' in the lines 'Perhaps his mate sat listening long, / And listened longer than I did' refers to the ______.
    Options: butterfly / poet / skylark / cornfield
    Ans: poet
  • Q: 5. In the lines 'The cornfield stretched a tender green / To right and left beside my walks', 'beside' means ______.
    Options: between / far from / onto / next to
    Ans: next to

mcqs.q: The pronoun 'his' in the line 'And as I paused to hear his song' has been used for the ______.
mcqs.why: The song the poet pauses to hear is the skylark's song, so 'his' refers to the skylark, as given in the book's comprehension key.

mcqs.q: In 'The cornfield stretched a tender green / To right and left beside my walks', 'my walks' refers to the ______.
mcqs.why: In these lines 'my walks' means the path along which the poet walks through the cornfield, according to the book's key.

mcqs.q: The pronoun 'he' in the line 'I knew he had a nest unseen' has been used for the ______.
mcqs.why: The nest hidden among the corn stalks belongs to the skylark, so 'he' in this line refers to the skylark.

mcqs.q: In 'Perhaps his mate sat listening long, / And listened longer than I did', 'I' refers to the ______.
mcqs.why: The speaker of the poem is the poet, and she says the skylark's mate listened longer than she did, so 'I' refers to the poet.

mcqs.q: In 'To right and left beside my walks', the word 'beside' means ______.
mcqs.why: The cornfield stretches to the right and left next to the poet's path, so 'beside' here means next to, as in the book's key.

mcqs.q: In the summary of the poem, the poet describes how ______ she feels as she walks through the cornfield.
mcqs.why: The gapped summary says the poet feels content as she walks through the cornfield, enjoying the skylark's song on a sunny morning.

mcqs.q: As she walks along, the poet sees a skylark ______.
mcqs.why: The summary states that the poet sees the skylark flying in the sky above the corn, singing as a small speck above the field.

mcqs.q: The poet knows that the skylark's nest is ______ the cornfield.
mcqs.why: The poet knew the skylark had a nest unseen somewhere among the million stalks, so the nest is hidden in the cornfield.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'morn' mean?
options: The main stem of a plant
mcqs.why: In the glossary, 'morn' means a morning, as in the line where the poet saw and heard the skylark one sunny morn.

mcqs.q: What is a 'skylark'?
options: A small, brown bird known for its beautiful singing
mcqs.why: The glossary defines a skylark as a small, brown bird that is known for its beautiful singing, which the poet hears above the corn.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A: Point out alliteration used in the following tongue twisters

  • Q: Q1. Point out the alliteration in: 'A big black bug blew big blue bubbles.'
    Ans: The alliteration is the repetition of the 'b' sound in big, black, bug, blew, big and blue, which occur close together in the sentence.
  • Q: Q2. Point out the alliteration in: 'Many mini mice make nice merry music.'
    Ans: The alliteration is the repetition of the 'm' sound in Many, mini, mice, make, merry and music. The word 'nice' keeps the same rhythm, but the repeated first consonant sound is 'm'.

Vocabulary B: How many syllables do the following words have?

  • Q: Q1. How many syllables does 'September' have?
    Ans: 3 syllables: Sep-tem-ber.
  • Q: Q2. How many syllables does 'information' have?
    Ans: 4 syllables: in-for-ma-tion.
  • Q: Q3. How many syllables does 'discovery' have?
    Ans: 3 syllables: dis-cov-ery.
  • Q: Q4. How many syllables does 'television' have?
    Ans: 4 syllables: tel-e-vi-sion.
  • Q: Q5. How many syllables does 'stalk' have?
    Ans: 1 syllable: stalk.

Vocabulary C: Find three rhyming words from the poem and create three more rhyming words for the words found

  • Q: Q1. Find three rhyming words from the poem and create three more rhyming words for the words found.
    Ans: Rhyming words found in the poem: 'blue' rhymes with 'two', 'morn' rhymes with 'corn', and 'sing' rhymes with 'wing'. Three more rhyming words created for them: blue — glue, morn — born, sing — ring.

mcqs.q: In 'A big black bug blew big blue bubbles', the alliteration is the repetition of the ______ sound.
mcqs.why: Alliteration here is the repetition of the first consonant sound 'b' in big, black, bug, blew, big and blue, close together in the sentence.

mcqs.q: In 'Many mini mice make nice merry music', the repeated first consonant sound is ______.
mcqs.why: The 'm' sound is repeated in Many, mini, mice, make, merry and music; 'nice' keeps the rhythm but does not start with 'm'.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word 'September' have?
mcqs.why: September is divided as Sep-tem-ber, which makes three syllables in total, as shown in the syllable exercise.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word 'information' have?
mcqs.why: Information is divided as in-for-ma-tion, giving four syllables, the same number as television in this exercise.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word 'discovery' have?
mcqs.why: Discovery is divided as dis-cov-ery, so it has three syllables, like September in the same exercise.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word 'television' have?
mcqs.why: Television is divided as tel-e-vi-sion, which gives four syllables in total, as counted in the notes.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word 'stalk' have?
mcqs.why: 'Stalk' is spoken as one undivided sound unit, so it has only one syllable, unlike the longer words in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Which word from the poem rhymes with 'blue'?
mcqs.why: Among the rhyming words found in the poem, 'blue' rhymes with 'two', while 'morn' rhymes with 'corn' and 'sing' with 'wing'.

mcqs.q: Which word from the poem rhymes with 'morn'?
mcqs.why: In the poem 'morn' rhymes with 'corn', and the notes create the further rhyming word 'born' for the same sound.

mcqs.q: Which word from the poem rhymes with 'sing'?
mcqs.why: 'Sing' rhymes with 'wing' in the poem, as in the white butterflies that danced on the wing while the skylark sang.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar: Comparative Adjectives — Fill in the spaces with the appropriate comparative adjective

  • Q: 1. Dawood is ______ (old) than Kiran.
    Ans: older
  • Q: 2. I am ______ (tall) than the bookshelf.
    Ans: taller
  • Q: 3. My dog is ______ (fast) than my cat.
    Ans: faster
  • Q: 4. The soup is ______ (hot) than the milk.
    Ans: hotter
  • Q: 5. The rock is ______ (hard) than the banana.
    Ans: harder

Grammar: Absolute Adjectives — How about these words, are they absolute adjectives or not?

  • Q: 1. opposite is...
    Options: not an absolute adjective / an absolute adjective
    Ans: an absolute adjective
  • Q: 2. beautiful is...
    Options: not an absolute adjective / an absolute adjective
    Ans: not an absolute adjective
  • Q: 3. round is...
    Options: an absolute adjective / not an absolute adjective
    Ans: an absolute adjective
  • Q: 4. unique is...
    Options: an absolute adjective / not an absolute adjective
    Ans: an absolute adjective
  • Q: 5. green is...
    Options: an absolute adjective / not an absolute adjective
    Ans: not an absolute adjective
  • Q: 6. healthy is...
    Options: an absolute adjective / not an absolute adjective
    Ans: not an absolute adjective

Grammar A: Write down the comparative and superlative degrees of the following adjectives

  • Q: Q1. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'far'.
    Ans: Comparative: farther. Superlative: farthest. (This one has been done in the book.)
  • Q: Q2. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'bad'.
    Ans: Comparative: worse. Superlative: worst.
  • Q: Q3. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'ugly'.
    Ans: Comparative: uglier. Superlative: ugliest.
  • Q: Q4. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'pretty'.
    Ans: Comparative: prettier. Superlative: prettiest.
  • Q: Q5. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'expensive'.
    Ans: Comparative: more expensive. Superlative: most expensive.
  • Q: Q6. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'tall'.
    Ans: Comparative: taller. Superlative: tallest.
  • Q: Q7. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'good'.
    Ans: Comparative: better. Superlative: best.
  • Q: Q8. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'cheap'.
    Ans: Comparative: cheaper. Superlative: cheapest.
  • Q: Q9. Write the comparative and superlative degrees of 'many'.
    Ans: Comparative: more. Superlative: most.

Grammar: Forming Adjectives — Fill in the blanks with the adjectives formed from the nouns in brackets

  • Q: 1. Atif is a ______ boy. (mischief)
    Ans: mischievous
  • Q: 2. The man's property was seized because he was ______. (dishonesty)
    Ans: dishonest
  • Q: 3. Her ______ behaviour won her no friends. (outrage)
    Ans: outrageous
  • Q: 4. I am ______ of no one. (envy)
    Ans: envious
  • Q: 5. "Pleased to meet you," he said in a ______ tone of voice. (respect)
    Ans: respectful
  • Q: 6. The ______ violence seen in the film is repulsive. (sense)
    Ans: senseless
  • Q: 7. He is a ______ soldier. (courage)
    Ans: courageous
  • Q: 8. It is not a ______ mistake. (pardon)
    Ans: unpardonable
  • Q: 9. Dark ______ clouds gathered in the sky. (storm)
    Ans: stormy

mcqs.q: Dawood is ______ (old) than Kiran.
mcqs.why: With 'than' we use the comparative degree, and the comparative of 'old' is 'older', as filled in the comparative exercise.

mcqs.q: The soup is ______ (hot) than the milk.
mcqs.why: The comparative of 'hot' is 'hotter', with the final consonant doubled, because the soup is compared with the milk using 'than'.

mcqs.q: Is 'opposite' an absolute adjective or not?
mcqs.why: The notes mark 'opposite' as an absolute adjective, like round and unique, because such a quality cannot be graded in degrees.

mcqs.q: Is 'beautiful' an absolute adjective or not?
mcqs.why: 'Beautiful' is not an absolute adjective, because something can be more or less beautiful; green and healthy are also not absolute.

mcqs.q: Is 'unique' an absolute adjective or not?
mcqs.why: 'Unique' is an absolute adjective in the notes, since a thing is either one of a kind or not, and the quality does not come in degrees.

mcqs.q: What are the comparative and superlative degrees of 'bad'?
mcqs.why: 'Bad' has irregular degrees: its comparative is 'worse' and its superlative is 'worst', as listed in the degrees exercise.

mcqs.q: What are the comparative and superlative degrees of 'good'?
mcqs.why: 'Good' also changes its form completely: comparative 'better' and superlative 'best', as given in the notes.

mcqs.q: What is the comparative degree of 'expensive'?
mcqs.why: Long adjectives like 'expensive' form the comparative with 'more', giving 'more expensive', and the superlative with 'most expensive'.

mcqs.q: What is the superlative degree of 'tall'?
mcqs.why: The superlative of 'tall' is 'tallest', formed by adding -est, while 'taller' is only its comparative degree.

mcqs.q: What is the comparative degree of 'many'?
mcqs.why: The comparative of 'many' is 'more' and its superlative is 'most', as listed among the degrees in the notes.

mcqs.q: Atif is a ______ boy. (mischief)
mcqs.why: The adjective formed from the noun 'mischief' is 'mischievous', which correctly describes the boy in this sentence.

mcqs.q: The man's property was seized because he was ______. (dishonesty)
mcqs.why: The adjective formed from 'dishonesty' needed here is 'dishonest', describing why the man's property was seized.

mcqs.q: He said in a ______ tone of voice. (respect)
mcqs.why: The adjective formed from 'respect' is 'respectful', so the man spoke in a respectful tone of voice.

mcqs.q: He is a ______ soldier. (courage)
mcqs.why: The adjective formed from the noun 'courage' is 'courageous', which describes the brave soldier in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Dark ______ clouds gathered in the sky. (storm)
mcqs.why: The adjective formed from 'storm' is 'stormy', so dark stormy clouds gathered in the sky before the bad weather.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: Q1. Write an imaginary story to describe a real or imaginary person. Use precise, as well as vivid adjectives to describe this real or imaginary person.
    Ans: In a small green village, there lived a tall, thin old man named Baba Karim. He had a long white beard, bright kind eyes and a warm, gentle smile. Every morning he wore a clean white shalwar kameez and a soft brown cap, and he walked slowly to the village well with his strong wooden stick. Baba Karim was a wise and generous person. He kept a big clay pot of cool water outside his little mud house for thirsty travellers. Poor children loved him because he told them wonderful old stories in his deep, sweet voice. His tiny garden was full of red roses and sweet-smelling jasmine, and he shared its fresh fruit with everyone. One hot summer day, a tired young traveller fainted near the well. Baba Karim quickly gave him cold water and fresh bread. The traveller thanked the kind old man again and again. From that day, everyone called Baba Karim the kindest man in the whole village.

mcqs.q: How is Baba Karim described at the start of the story?
mcqs.why: The story begins by describing Baba Karim as a tall, thin old man who lived in a small green village.

mcqs.q: What did Baba Karim's beard look like?
mcqs.why: Baba Karim had a long white beard, bright kind eyes and a warm, gentle smile, as the vivid adjectives in the story describe him.

mcqs.q: What did Baba Karim wear every morning?
options: A blue coat and a red cap
A clean white shalwar kameez and a soft brown cap
A black suit and a hat
mcqs.why: Every morning he wore a clean white shalwar kameez and a soft brown cap before walking slowly to the village well.

mcqs.q: With what did Baba Karim walk to the village well?
mcqs.why: He walked slowly to the village well with his strong wooden stick, as described in the opening paragraph of the story.

mcqs.q: What did Baba Karim keep outside his little mud house for thirsty travellers?
options: A big clay pot of cool water
mcqs.why: Baba Karim kept a big clay pot of cool water outside his little mud house so that thirsty travellers could drink from it.

mcqs.q: What flowers grew in Baba Karim's tiny garden?
mcqs.why: His tiny garden was full of red roses and sweet-smelling jasmine, and he shared its fresh fruit with everyone.

mcqs.q: What happened to the young traveller near the well one hot summer day?
mcqs.why: One hot summer day a tired young traveller fainted near the well, and Baba Karim quickly helped him.

mcqs.q: What did Baba Karim give the fainted traveller?
mcqs.why: Baba Karim quickly gave the traveller cold water and fresh bread, after which the traveller thanked him again and again.

mcqs.q: Why did poor children love Baba Karim?
options: He told them wonderful old stories in his deep, sweet voice
mcqs.why: Poor children loved him because he told them wonderful old stories in his deep, sweet voice, showing his kind and generous nature.

mcqs.q: What did everyone call Baba Karim from that day?
options: The wisest traveller of the village
The kindest man in the whole village
The richest man in the village
mcqs.why: After he helped the traveller, everyone called Baba Karim the kindest man in the whole village, as the story ends.

lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking

  • Q: Q1. Say the following sentences, paying attention to the sounds. Work with a partner and practice the following tongue twisters until you memorize them. When you have memorized, say it for your teacher: (i) If two witches were watching two watches, which witch would watch which watch? (ii) Woodson's waistcoat is weirdly vented.
    Ans: Practice guide: Read each tongue twister slowly first, then faster, keeping the sounds clear. In the first twister, note the repeated 'w' sound in witches, were, watching, watches, which, witch, would and watch. In the second, note the repeated 'w' sound in Woodson's, waistcoat and weirdly, and the 'v' sound in vented. Repeat each twister with your partner until you can say it from memory without a mistake, then say it for your teacher.

chapters.title: Unit 7: Whose Pleasure Shall We Seek?

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Do you usually listen to other people's opinion carefully?
    Ans: Yes, I usually listen to other people's opinions carefully, because a good opinion can help me. But I think about it first before I follow it, because in this unit we learn that there are as many opinions as there are people in the world.
  • Q: Q2. Do you accept their opinions mostly?
    Ans: No, I do not accept their opinions mostly. I accept an opinion only when I feel it is right, because if we try to follow everyone's opinion, we can please no one, as the father and son in the story could not please the people.
  • Q: Q3. What do you feel when another person tells you to do something?
    Ans: I feel a little disturbed when another person tells me to do something, especially when I am already doing the right thing. Still, I listen politely and then follow my own instinct, because we can never please everyone.

Glossary

  • Q: What does 'wise' mean?
    Ans: Having or showing the ability to make good judgments, based on a deep understanding and experience of life.
  • Q: What does 'seeking' mean?
    Ans: To try to find or get something.
  • Q: What does 'succeed' mean?
    Ans: To achieve something that you have been aiming for.
  • Q: What does 'tie' mean?
    Ans: To relate to or connect to.
  • Q: What does 'obeyed' mean?
    Ans: To act according to what you have been asked.
  • Q: What does 'ride' mean?
    Ans: To sit on something such as a bicycle, motorbike, or horse and travel along on it controlling its movements.
  • Q: What does 'impolite' mean?
    Ans: Not polite; offensive or embarrassing.
  • Q: What does 'manners' mean?
    Ans: Ways of behaving toward people.
  • Q: What does 'bridge' mean?
    Ans: A structure that is built over a river, road, or railway to allow people and vehicles to cross from one side to the other.
  • Q: What does 'criticism' mean?
    Ans: The act of giving your opinion or judgment about the good or bad qualities of something or someone.
  • Q: What does 'further' mean?
    Ans: To a greater distance or degree, or at a more advanced level.
  • Q: What does 'instinct' mean?
    Ans: The way people naturally react or behave.

Comprehension A: Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Do you like the story? Why?
    Ans: Yes, I like the story very much. It is interesting, with the father, the son and the donkey meeting different groups of people, and it teaches a great lesson: whatever we do, we cannot please all the people of the world, so we should seek the pleasure of God and follow our own instincts.
  • Q: Q2. How does the author describe the characters of people?
    Ans: The author describes people as critics who are never satisfied. Whatever a person does, people find fault with it, because the tongue has no bone and can speak even without thought. There are as many opinions as there are people in the world, so their criticism never ends.
  • Q: Q3. Explain "Please all and you will please none" as taught in the lesson.
    Ans: It means that if a person tries to make everyone happy, he will make no one happy, because every person wants something different. In the lesson, the father and son changed their way again and again to please each group of people — the son rode, then the father rode, then both walked, then both rode, and at last they carried the donkey — yet people still criticised them, and in the end the donkey fell into the river and died. So, in pleasing all, they pleased none and lost their donkey too.
  • Q: Q4. If you were the boy or his father, would you take others suggestions? Why?
    Ans: If I were the boy or his father, I would listen to the people's suggestions politely, but I would not follow every suggestion blindly. I would use my own judgment and follow my instinct, because the suggestions of people oppose each other, and following all of them only brings loss, as it did in the story.
  • Q: Q5. Is it good that you do not take others suggestions at all?
    Ans: No, it is not good to refuse all suggestions. Some suggestions are wise and useful, and we should think over them carefully. The lesson only teaches us not to follow every opinion just to please people. We should accept a good suggestion and reject a bad one by our own judgment, and always seek the pleasure of God.
  • Q: Q6. Why did the boy get off the donkey?
    Ans: The boy got off the donkey because a group of people called him an impolite and bad boy. They said that the old father was walking on foot while the young son was comfortably riding the donkey, and that this was no manner to show respect to one's father. Hearing this, the son came down and the old man rode the animal.
  • Q: Q7. Why did the man and his son carry the donkey?
    Ans: The man and his son carried the donkey because they wanted to please the people. At the river bridge, some people called them very unkind and cruel for both riding on the poor donkey, which could hardly take their entire burden. They got off and, thinking of what they could do now, they cut down a pole, tied the donkey's feet to it, and raised the pole and the donkey to their shoulders.

Comprehension B: Tell whether each of the following sentences is true or false

  • Q: 1. The father was not a wise man.
    Ans: False
  • Q: 2. It is always good to take others suggestions.
    Ans: False
  • Q: 3. The man and his son carried the donkey.
    Ans: True
  • Q: 4. The people said, "The father and his son are unkind."
    Ans: True

Comprehension C: Fill in the blanks to complete the cloze paragraph

  • Q: 1. Many, many years ago ______ lived a man.
    Ans: there
  • Q: 2. He ______ very wise.
    Ans: was
  • Q: 3. One day ______ said to his son,
    Ans: he
  • Q: 4. "______ son! Do not tie your heart in seeking the pleasure of people."
    Ans: Oh
  • Q: 5. "Do not tie ______ heart in seeking the pleasure of people."
    Ans: your
  • Q: 6. "Do not tie your heart in seeking the ______ of people."
    Ans: pleasure
  • Q: 7. "You are ______ likely to succeed."
    Ans: not
  • Q: 8. "Do ______ pay attention to what people say."
    Ans: not
  • Q: 9. "Do not pay attention to what ______ say."
    Ans: people
  • Q: 10. "Instead tell yourself ______ to seek the pleasure of God."
    Ans: always
  • Q: 11. "Instead tell yourself always to seek the pleasure ______ God."
    Ans: of
  • Q: 12. He wanted this ______ to be always remembered.
    Ans: lesson
  • Q: 13. He wanted this lesson to be always remembered. ______ to be forgotten.
    Ans: Never
  • Q: 14. He ______ of a way.
    Ans: thought
  • Q: 15. He ______ told his son to ride a donkey.
    Ans: then
  • Q: 16. He then told his son to ______ a donkey.
    Ans: ride
  • Q: 17. The son ______.
    Ans: obeyed

mcqs.q: What does the word 'wise' mean?
options: Having the ability to make good judgments from deep understanding and experience
mcqs.why: The glossary defines 'wise' as having or showing the ability to make good judgments, based on a deep understanding and experience of life.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'seeking' mean?
options: To try to find or get something
mcqs.why: 'Seeking' means to try to find or get something, as in the father's advice not to tie the heart in seeking the pleasure of people.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'instinct' mean?
options: The way people naturally react or behave
mcqs.why: Instinct is the way people naturally react or behave, and the lesson advises following our own instinct instead of every opinion.

mcqs.q: Why did the boy get off the donkey?
options: People called him impolite and bad for riding while his old father walked
His father ordered him to carry it
mcqs.why: A group of people called the son impolite and bad because the old father walked while the young son rode comfortably, so the son came down.

mcqs.q: Why did the man and his son carry the donkey?
options: People had called them unkind and cruel for both riding on the poor donkey
mcqs.why: At the river bridge people called them very unkind and cruel for both riding on the donkey, so they tied its feet to a pole and carried it.

mcqs.q: Tell whether this sentence is true or false: 'The father was not a wise man.'
mcqs.why: The statement is false, because the story begins by telling us that the man was very wise and wanted to teach his son a lasting lesson.

mcqs.q: Complete the cloze sentence: 'Many, many years ago ______ lived a man.'
mcqs.why: The cloze paragraph begins 'Many, many years ago there lived a man', so the missing word in the first blank is 'there'.

mcqs.q: What did the father advise his son to seek instead of the pleasure of people?
mcqs.why: The father told his son always to seek the pleasure of God and not to tie his heart in seeking the pleasure of people.

mcqs.q: What does 'Please all and you will please none' mean?
options: If you try to make everyone happy, you will make no one happy
mcqs.why: It means that trying to make everyone happy makes no one happy, because every person wants something different, as the father and son found.

mcqs.q: What happened to the donkey in the end?
options: It ran away to a field
It was sold at the bridge
It fell into the river and died
It carried both of them home
mcqs.why: In pleasing all, the father and son pleased none and lost their donkey too, because in the end the donkey fell into the river and died.

Comprehension D: Underline silent letters in the words below

  • Q: Q1. Underline the silent letter in the word: climb
    Ans: The letter 'b' is silent in 'climb'.
  • Q: Q2. Underline the silent letter in the word: handkerchief
    Ans: The letter 'd' is silent in 'handkerchief'.
  • Q: Q3. Underline the silent letter in the word: drive
    Ans: The letter 'e' at the end is silent in 'drive'.
  • Q: Q4. Underline the silent letter in the word: Wednesday
    Ans: The first letter 'd' is silent in 'Wednesday'.
  • Q: Q5. Underline the silent letter in the word: dumb
    Ans: The letter 'b' is silent in 'dumb'.
  • Q: Q6. Underline the silent letter in the word: foreign
    Ans: The letter 'g' is silent in 'foreign'.
  • Q: Q7. Underline the silent letter in the word: sign
    Ans: The letter 'g' is silent in 'sign'.
  • Q: Q8. Underline the silent letter in the word: feign
    Ans: The letter 'g' is silent in 'feign'.
  • Q: Q9. Underline the silent letter in the word: gave
    Ans: The letter 'e' at the end is silent in 'gave'.
  • Q: Q10. Underline the silent letter in the word: site
    Ans: The letter 'e' at the end is silent in 'site'.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'climb'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'b' at the end of 'climb' is silent, so the word is pronounced without the b sound, like 'dumb' in the same list.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'handkerchief'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'd' is silent in 'handkerchief', so we do not pronounce the d when we say this word.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'drive'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'e' at the end of 'drive' is silent, just as the final e is silent in 'gave' and 'site'.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'Wednesday'?
mcqs.why: The first letter 'd' in 'Wednesday' is silent, which is why the word is not pronounced the way it is spelled.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'dumb'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'b' is silent in 'dumb', in the same way as the final b is silent in the word 'climb'.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'foreign'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'g' is silent in 'foreign', just as it is silent in the words 'sign' and 'feign' in this exercise.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'sign'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'g' is silent in 'sign', so the word ends with the n sound even though a g is written before it.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'feign'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'g' is silent in 'feign', matching the silent g in 'foreign' and 'sign' from the same list of words.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'gave'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'e' at the end of 'gave' is silent; it only changes the sound of the vowel before it.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'site'?
mcqs.why: The letter 'e' at the end of 'site' is silent, like the final silent e in 'drive' and 'gave'.

Grammar B: Fill in the blanks with suitable adverbs or adverb phrases from the list above (A)

    Ans: gladly
  • Q: 2. There is ______ any water in the pond.
    Ans: scarcely

    Ans: rarely
