mcqs.q: 'Never' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Never' tells how often something happens, so it is an adverb of frequency, like rarely, usually and once a month.

mcqs.q: 'Almost' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Almost' shows the extent or degree to which something is true, so it is an adverb of degree, like nearly, scarcely and hardly.

mcqs.q: 'Somewhere' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Somewhere' answers the question 'where?', so it is an adverb of place, like there, at school and at home.

mcqs.q: 'Seriously' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Seriously' tells how an action is done, so it is an adverb of manner, like calmly, gladly, slowly and fast.

mcqs.q: 'Soon' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Soon' tells when something will happen, so it is an adverb of time, like then, today and after lunch.

mcqs.q: 'Rarely' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Rarely' tells how often something happens, so it belongs with the adverbs of frequency such as never and usually.

mcqs.q: 'Scarcely' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Scarcely' shows a very small degree or amount, so it is an adverb of degree, like almost, nearly and hardly.

mcqs.q: 'Today' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Today' answers the question 'when?', so it is an adverb of time, together with soon, then and next day.

mcqs.q: 'At home' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'At home' tells where something happens, so it is an adverb of place, like at school, in the city and on board.

mcqs.q: 'Slowly' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: 'Slowly' describes how an action is performed, so it is an adverb of manner, like seriously, calmly and generously.

mcqs.q: His son sings ______.
mcqs.why: The suitable adverb of manner from the list is 'gladly', so the sentence reads 'His son sings gladly.'

mcqs.q: There is ______ any water in the pond.
mcqs.why: The adverb of degree 'scarcely' fits here: 'There is scarcely any water in the pond' means there is hardly any water.

mcqs.q: He is ______ seen these days.
mcqs.why: 'Rarely', an adverb of frequency, completes the sentence: he is rarely seen these days, meaning he is not often seen.

mcqs.q: He has to visit a doctor ______.
mcqs.why: The frequency phrase 'once a month' completes the sentence, telling how often he has to visit a doctor.

mcqs.q: ______ they clean this tank.
mcqs.why: The sentence begins with the adverb of frequency 'Usually', telling how often they clean this tank.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing: Transitional Devices

  • Q: Q1. What are transitional devices?
    Ans: Transitional devices are words or phrases that help carry a thought from one sentence to another, from one idea to another, and from one paragraph to another. They link sentences and paragraphs together smoothly.
  • Q: Q2. Which transitional devices are used for Addition?
    Ans: and, again, and then, besides, finally, further, furthermore, nor, too, next, lastly, moreover, in addition, first.
  • Q: Q3. Which transitional devices are used for Alternative?
    Ans: either, or, nor, on the other hand, however, neither, otherwise.
  • Q: Q4. Which transitional devices are used for Comparison and contrast?
    Ans: whereas, but, yet, on the other hand, however, nevertheless, where, compared to, up against, although, conversely, in contrast.
  • Q: Q5. Which transitional devices are used for Illustration?
    Ans: for example, for instance, in this case, in another case, on this occasion, in this situation, to demonstrate, to illustrate.
  • Q: Q6. Which transitional devices are used for Sequence?
    Ans: first, second, third, then, at this time, now, after, afterward, finally, previously, before this, thus, therefore, hence, next, soon, etc.
  • Q: Q7. Which transitional devices are used for Conclusion?
    Ans: in brief, on the whole, summing up, to conclude, as I have shown, as I have said, hence, therefore, accordingly, thus, as a result, consequently.
  • Q: Q8. Which transitional devices are used for Cause / effect?
    Ans: therefore, consequently, as a result.

Writing: Analyze the paragraph to identify the main idea, definition, transitional devices, cause and effect, illustration and evidence

  • Q: Q1. Analyze the paragraph (about teenagers dropping out of school) and identify its main idea.
    Ans: The main idea is given in the first sentence: for many teenagers, there are numerous negative factors that can lead them to give up on their education and drop out of school. The whole paragraph supports this idea.
  • Q: Q2. Analyze the paragraph and identify the definition.
    Ans: The paragraph does not give a separate dictionary definition. It explains the main idea in the opening sentence itself: dropping out of school means giving up on one's education, and the rest of the paragraph describes the factors that cause it.
  • Q: Q3. Analyze the paragraph and identify the transitional devices.
    Ans: The transitional devices used are: 'The first cause is...', 'Also', 'Another factor...', 'If', and 'The third and final factor...'. These words arrange the causes in order and link the sentences smoothly.
  • Q: Q4. Analyze the paragraph and identify the evidence.
    Ans: The supporting evidence is the three factors described in the paragraph: many teenagers lack positive role models in their lives; another factor is a lack of determination; and the third and final factor is peer pressure. Sentences such as 'Many students find it difficult to stay focused on school when they feel that getting an education is useless' also support the main idea.
  • Q: Q5. Analyze the paragraph and identify the cause and effect.
    Ans: Cause: the lack of an encouraging adult in their lives, getting involved in negative activities, a lack of determination, and peer pressure. Effect: teenagers think negatively about themselves, do not live up to their full potential, do not focus on school, and at last give up on their education and drop out of school.
  • Q: Q6. Analyze the paragraph and identify the illustration.
    Ans: The illustration is the sentence: 'Also, when students get involved in negative activities, they usually don't focus on school. This can lead many impressionable young children to give up on their education.' It shows, by an example, how one cause leads teenagers to drop out.

mcqs.q: What are transitional devices?
options: Words that name people and places
Words or phrases that help carry a thought from one sentence, idea or paragraph to another
mcqs.why: Transitional devices are words or phrases that help carry a thought from one sentence to another, one idea to another and one paragraph to another, linking them smoothly.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a transitional device used for Addition?
mcqs.why: 'Moreover' is listed among the addition devices with and, besides, further, furthermore and in addition, while the others belong to other groups.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a transitional device used for Alternative?
mcqs.why: 'Either' is listed for Alternative with or, nor, on the other hand, however, neither and otherwise.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a transitional device used for Comparison and contrast?
mcqs.why: 'Whereas' is listed under Comparison and contrast with but, yet, however, nevertheless, although, conversely and in contrast.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a transitional device used for Illustration?
mcqs.why: 'For example' is an illustration device, listed with for instance, in this case, to demonstrate and to illustrate.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a transitional device used for Sequence?
mcqs.why: 'Second' belongs to the sequence list with first, third, then, now, after, finally, next and soon, which shows the order of ideas.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a transitional device used for Conclusion?
mcqs.why: 'To conclude' is listed for Conclusion with in brief, on the whole, summing up, hence, therefore and as a result.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a transitional device used for Cause / effect?
mcqs.why: The cause and effect devices listed in the notes are therefore, consequently and as a result, so 'consequently' is correct here.

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the paragraph about teenagers dropping out of school?
options: Teenagers have many positive role models
For many teenagers, numerous negative factors can lead them to give up on their education and drop out of school
Peer pressure is the only factor
All teenagers stay focused on school
mcqs.why: The main idea is given in the first sentence: numerous negative factors can lead many teenagers to give up on their education and drop out of school.

mcqs.q: Which one is given in the paragraph as one of the three factors that lead teenagers to drop out?
mcqs.why: The evidence in the paragraph names three factors: lack of positive role models, lack of determination, and the third and final factor, peer pressure.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking

  • Q: Q1. Work in groups of four and practice the conversation between four friends using adverbs. (Rashida, Seema, Nadia and Ayesha)
    Ans: Model practice: Work in a group of four and take the parts of Rashida, Seema, Nadia and Ayesha. Rashida asked her friends eagerly, "What do you all usually do on a Monday?" Seema said quickly, "I often go to the market for grocery." Nadia said softly, "I sometimes go to see my parents." Ayesha said thoughtfully, "I always go to see my parents and friends." Then take turns and extend the conversation with your own sentences, using adverbs of manner (eagerly, quickly, softly, thoughtfully) and adverbs of frequency (usually, often, sometimes, always), for example: "I usually finish my homework early, and then I happily help my mother at home."

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Do you like reading?
    Ans: Yes, I like reading very much. Reading is my favourite pastime because it increases my knowledge and keeps my mind active and healthy.
  • Q: Q2. Which book are you reading these days?
    Ans: These days I am reading a book of interesting short stories. I also read my English reader and other extra books, because the students who excel academically are those who read extra books.
  • Q: Q3. How long do you take in reading every day?
    Ans: I take about one hour for reading every day. I read regularly, because we should take time to read on a regular basis in order to seek knowledge.

Glossary

  • Q: What does 'elevate' mean?
    Ans: To make someone or something more important, or to improve something.
  • Q: What does 'monstrous' mean?
    Ans: Very cruel.
  • Q: What does 'bleak' mean?
    Ans: If a place is bleak, it is empty, and not welcoming or attractive.
  • Q: What does 'gauge' mean?
    Ans: To calculate an amount, especially by using a measuring device.
  • Q: What does 'spare' mean?
    Ans: If something is spare, it is available to use because it is extra.
  • Q: What does 'chase' mean?
    Ans: To hurry after someone or something in order to catch him, her, or it.
  • Q: What does 'brooding' mean?
    Ans: Making you feel uncomfortable or worried, as if something bad is going to happen.
  • Q: What does 'testifies' mean?
    Ans: To speak seriously about something, especially in a law court, or to give or provide proof.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What is an informal letter? Why do we need to write a letter?
    Ans: An informal letter is a friendly letter written to family members and close friends in a simple, personal tone and style, like the letter Inam Ullah Khan writes to his son Aman Ullah in this unit. We need to write letters to share our news and feelings, to congratulate someone, and to give useful advice, just as the father congratulates his son on his good grades and advises him to develop the habit of reading.
  • Q: Q2. Who do you write informal letters to?
    Ans: We write informal letters to our family members and close friends, for example a father writes an informal letter to his son, as in this unit.
  • Q: Q3. What is your very favourite book? Do you have a favourite author?
    Ans: My very favourite book is a book of short stories, because whatever we read should be informative and should elevate our spirit and thoughts. Yes, I have a favourite author; I like the way he writes simple and interesting stories that give a good lesson.
  • Q: Q4. What type of books do you like to read (adventure, science fiction, etc.)? Give reason for your answer.
    Ans: I like to read adventure books. They are full of excitement, and at the same time they increase my knowledge, expand my vocabulary and improve my focus and concentration.
  • Q: Q5. Do you have any favourite magazines or comics? Name them.
    Ans: Yes, I have favourite magazines and comics. I like reading children's magazines and story comics in my spare time, because the habit of reading is the best pastime and it keeps a person busy when he has nothing else to do.
  • Q: Q6. Is there a library in your city / village / school? Are you a member of the library? How often do you visit the library?
    Ans: Yes, there is a library in my school. I am a member of the library. I visit the library twice a week and borrow extra books, because the students who excel academically are those who read extra books.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'elevate' mean?
options: To hurry after someone to catch them
To make someone or something more important, or to improve something
To calculate an amount with a measuring device
To speak seriously in a law court
mcqs.why: The glossary defines 'elevate' as to make someone or something more important, or to improve something, as reading should elevate our spirit and thoughts.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'monstrous' mean?
options: Available to use because it is extra
Worried as if something bad will happen
mcqs.why: The glossary gives 'monstrous' as very cruel, which is different from 'bleak' meaning empty and not welcoming or attractive.

mcqs.q: If a place is described as 'bleak', it is:
options: Empty, and not welcoming or attractive
Serious and spoken in a law court
mcqs.why: The glossary explains that a bleak place is empty, and not welcoming or attractive, which matches the description given in the lesson notes.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'gauge' mean?
options: To collect things over a long time
To hurry after someone in order to catch them
To calculate an amount, especially by using a measuring device
mcqs.why: The glossary defines 'gauge' as to calculate an amount, especially by using a measuring device, and the lesson uses it for measuring a nation's progress.

mcqs.q: What does 'spare' mean in the phrase 'in my spare time'?
options: Available to use because it is extra
mcqs.why: The glossary says 'spare' means available to use because it is extra, so spare time is extra time when a person has nothing else to do.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'chase' mean?
options: To hurry after someone or something in order to catch him, her, or it
mcqs.why: The glossary defines 'chase' as to hurry after someone or something in order to catch him, her, or it, which is the meaning used in the lesson.

mcqs.q: What does 'brooding' mean?
options: Making you feel uncomfortable or worried, as if something bad is going to happen
mcqs.why: The glossary explains 'brooding' as making you feel uncomfortable or worried, as if something bad is going to happen.

mcqs.q: What does 'testifies' mean?
options: To hurry after someone to catch them
To calculate with a measuring device
To speak seriously about something, especially in a law court, or to give or provide proof
mcqs.why: The glossary defines 'testifies' as to speak seriously about something, especially in a law court, or to give or provide proof.

mcqs.q: An informal letter is best described as:
options: A formal letter to an office in a strict style
A friendly letter written to family members and close friends in a simple, personal tone and style
A letter written only to congratulate a stranger
A letter written only to give a business order
mcqs.why: The comprehension answer defines an informal letter as a friendly letter to family members and close friends in a simple, personal tone and style, like the father's letter in this unit.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, the students who excel academically are those who:
options: Read only their course books once
Visit the library only once a year
Spend spare time only on comics
mcqs.why: The notes state clearly that the students who excel academically are those who read extra books, which is why the student visits the library twice a week to borrow them.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — A. Underline the silent letters. Then write the words on the correct line

  • Q: Words with silent 'k'
    Ans: knee, knead, knock, knowledge.
  • Q: Words with silent 'w'
    Ans: wrap, wrinkle, wrist, wrote.
  • Q: Words with silent 't'
    Ans: listen, fasten, castle.
  • Q: Words with silent 'b'
    Ans: bomb.

Vocabulary — B. Make two sentences each with the words present and export showing them as noun and verb depending on whether the stress is on first or second syllable

  • Q: Make two sentences with the word 'present' as a noun and as a verb.
    Ans: As a noun (stress on the first syllable, PREsent): I gave a present to my friend on his birthday. As a verb (stress on the second syllable, preSENT): The students will present their work before the class today.
  • Q: Make two sentences with the word 'export' as a noun and as a verb.
    Ans: As a noun (stress on the first syllable, EXport): Cotton is a major export of Pakistan. As a verb (stress on the second syllable, exPORT): We export raw cash crops to other countries.

mcqs.q: Which word has a silent 'k'?
mcqs.why: In 'knee' the letter k is silent, and the notes list knee, knead, knock and knowledge as words with a silent k.

mcqs.q: Which word has a silent 'w'?
mcqs.why: In 'wrap' the letter w is silent, and the notes list wrap, wrinkle, wrist and wrote as words with a silent w.

mcqs.q: Which word has a silent 't'?
mcqs.why: In 'listen' the letter t is silent, and the notes list listen, fasten and castle as words with a silent t.

mcqs.q: Which word has a silent 'b'?
mcqs.why: In 'bomb' the final letter b is silent, and the notes give bomb as the example of a word with a silent b.

mcqs.q: Which word belongs with 'knock' and 'knowledge' in the silent-letter grouping?
mcqs.why: Knock and knowledge both have a silent k, and knead also has a silent k, so it belongs in the same group in the notes.

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'I gave a present to my friend on his birthday', the word 'present' is used as:
options: A verb with stress on the second syllable
A noun with stress on the first syllable, PREsent
A verb with stress on the first syllable
mcqs.why: The notes show 'present' as a noun meaning a gift, with stress on the first syllable PREsent, in the sentence about giving a present on a birthday.

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'The students will present their work before the class today', the word 'present' is used as:
options: A noun with stress on the first syllable
A verb with stress on the second syllable, preSENT
A noun meaning an export item
mcqs.why: The notes show 'present' as a verb meaning to show work, with stress on the second syllable preSENT, in the sentence about students presenting before the class.

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'Cotton is a major export of Pakistan', the word 'export' is used as:
options: A verb with stress on the second syllable
An adjective with stress on the second syllable
A verb with stress on the first syllable
A noun with stress on the first syllable, EXport
mcqs.why: The notes show 'export' as a noun for a product sold abroad, with stress on the first syllable EXport, in the sentence about cotton being a major export.

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'We export raw cash crops to other countries', the word 'export' is used as:
options: A verb with stress on the second syllable, exPORT
A noun with stress on the first syllable
A noun meaning a birthday gift
An adjective meaning present in class
mcqs.why: The notes show 'export' as a verb meaning to send goods to other countries, with stress on the second syllable exPORT, in the sentence about exporting raw cash crops.

mcqs.q: Which word has a silent 'w' like 'wrist'?
mcqs.why: Wrist has a silent w, and wrote also has a silent w, as listed in the notes with wrap, wrinkle, wrist and wrote.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar — A. Fill in the blanks with appropriate preposition

  • Q: 1. My best friend lives ______ Jinnah Road.
    Ans: at
  • Q: 2. Since he met his new friend, Jamal never seems to be ______ home.
    Ans: at
  • Q: 3. I'll be ready to leave ______ about twenty minutes.
    Ans: in
  • Q: 4. The child responded to his mother's demands ______ throwing a tantrum.
    Ans: by
  • Q: 5. I think she spent the entire afternoon ______ the phone.
    Ans: on

Grammar — Prepositions since / for: Fill in the blanks with appropriate preposition since / for

  • Q: 1. I have been living in Manshera ______ 1 year.
    Ans: for
  • Q: 2. I haven't seen you ______ a week.
    Ans: for
  • Q: 3. I have been waiting ______ 12.30.
    Ans: since
  • Q: 4. I've lived here ______ 5 years.
    Ans: for
  • Q: 5. She has been married ______ ten years.
    Ans: for
  • Q: 6. They exercise ______ two hours daily.
    Ans: for
  • Q: 7. He has owned his dog ______ his cat died.
    Ans: since

Grammar — Prepositions of movement or direction: Fill in the blanks with the prepositions of movement and direction. Choose prepositions from the given list (to, across, down, around, along)

  • Q: 1. Let's go for a walk ______ the park.
    Ans: around
  • Q: 2. He's walking ______ the path.
    Ans: down
  • Q: 3. I prefer to ride my bike ______ the hill.
    Ans: across
  • Q: 4. I go ______ school by bus.
    Ans: to
  • Q: 5. The boat will take you ______ the river.
    Ans: along

mcqs.q: My best friend lives ______ Jinnah Road.
mcqs.why: The correct preposition is 'at' for a specific road address in this exercise, so the sentence reads 'lives at Jinnah Road' as given in the notes.

mcqs.q: Since he met his new friend, Jamal never seems to be ______ home.
mcqs.why: The phrase is 'at home', so 'at' is correct here, as shown in the grammar exercise in the lesson notes.

mcqs.q: I'll be ready to leave ______ about twenty minutes.
mcqs.why: We use 'in' for a period of time after which something will happen, so 'in about twenty minutes' is correct as given in the notes.

mcqs.q: The child responded to his mother's demands ______ throwing a tantrum.
mcqs.why: The correct preposition is 'by', showing how the child responded, so the sentence reads 'by throwing a tantrum' as in the notes.

mcqs.q: I think she spent the entire afternoon ______ the phone.
mcqs.why: The fixed phrase is 'on the phone', so 'on' is the correct preposition as given in the grammar exercise.

mcqs.q: I have been living in Manshera ______ 1 year.
mcqs.why: We use 'for' with a length of time such as 1 year, so 'for 1 year' is correct, while 'since' is used with a starting point.

mcqs.q: I haven't seen you ______ a week.
mcqs.why: A week is a length of time, so 'for a week' is correct; 'since' would need a starting point such as a day or a time.

mcqs.q: I have been waiting ______ 12.30.
mcqs.why: 12.30 is a starting point in time, so 'since 12.30' is correct, as shown in the since and for exercise in the notes.

mcqs.q: I've lived here ______ 5 years.
mcqs.why: Five years is a duration, so 'for 5 years' is correct; 'since' is used with a point in time, not with a number of years.

mcqs.q: She has been married ______ ten years.
mcqs.why: Ten years is a length of time, so 'for ten years' is correct as given in the exercise on since and for.

mcqs.q: They exercise ______ two hours daily.
mcqs.why: Two hours is a duration of time, so 'for two hours daily' is correct, while 'since' needs a starting point.

mcqs.q: He has owned his dog ______ his cat died.
mcqs.why: His cat dying is a starting point event in the past, so 'since his cat died' is correct as shown in the notes.

mcqs.q: Let's go for a walk ______ the park.
mcqs.why: For movement in a circle or all sides of a place, 'around' is correct, so the sentence reads 'a walk around the park' as in the notes.

mcqs.q: I go ______ school by bus.
mcqs.why: Movement towards a destination takes 'to', so 'go to school by bus' is correct as given in the movement prepositions exercise.

mcqs.q: The boat will take you ______ the river.
mcqs.why: Movement following the length of the river takes 'along', so 'along the river' is correct as shown in the notes for this exercise.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: 1. Write a letter to your uncle, asking him to bring you a dictionary to help you in your studies. (Highlight importance of dictionary in body of the letter; follow conventions of informal letter with respect to layout, salutations etc.; use appropriate vocabulary, style and tone.)
    Ans: House # 4, Abdara Road, University Town, Peshawar. 2nd June, 2017. My dear Uncle, How are you? We all are well by the grace of Allah. I hope you and aunt are also in good health. Dear uncle, my studies are going well, but I face one difficulty. While reading my English books, I meet many new and difficult words, and I cannot understand their meanings. A good dictionary will help me a lot in my studies. It will give me the meanings of difficult words, expand my vocabulary, and improve my focus and understanding of every lesson. With its help I can read extra books easily and, Insha Allah, get even better grades. So I request you to please bring me a good English dictionary when you come home. I shall be very thankful to you. Please give my regards to aunt and love to the children. Your loving nephew, Aman Ullah
  • Q: 2. Write your uncle's address on the envelop below.
    Ans: On the envelope, write the uncle's name and address clearly in the proper format on the front, for example: Inam Ullah Khan, House # 4, Abdara Road, University Town, Peshawar. Fix the stamp at the top right corner of the envelope, as shown in the book.

chapters.title: Unit 9: The Golden Age of Islam

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the picture and predict what could be the lesson about.
    Ans: The pictures show Muslim scholars of old times studying, teaching and working on knowledge near a Masjid. So the lesson is about the period of Muslim learning and progress, that is, the Golden Age of Islam, when science, economic development and cultural works flourished in the Islamic world.

Glossary

  • Q: What does 'empire' mean?
    Ans: A group of countries ruled by a single person, government, or country.
  • Q: What does 'inauguration' mean?
    Ans: The act of putting a service, system, etc. into action, or an occasion when this happens.
  • Q: What does 'mandated' mean?
    Ans: The authority given to an elected group of people, such as a government, to perform an action or govern a country.
  • Q: What does 'unrivalled' mean?
    Ans: Having no equal; better than any other of the same type.
  • Q: What does 'humanities' mean?
    Ans: Literature, language, history, philosophy, and other subjects that are not a science, or the study of these subjects.
  • Q: What does 'medieval' mean?
    Ans: Related to the Middle Ages (the period in European history from about AD 600 to AD 1500).
  • Q: What does 'cartography' mean?
    Ans: The science or art of making or drawing maps.
  • Q: What does 'accumulated' mean?
    Ans: To collect a large number of things over a long period of time.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What is the golden age of Islam?
    Ans: The Islamic Golden Age is the era in the history of Islam, dated from the 8th century to the 13th century, during which much of the historically Islamic world was ruled by various caliphates and science, economic development and cultural works flourished.
  • Q: Q2. Who were the real founders of modern science and technology?
    Ans: The early Muslim scientists and scholars of the Golden Age were the real founders of modern science and technology. Scholars from various parts of the world gathered at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad and translated all of the world's classical knowledge into the Arabic language, and Muslim engineers made great progress, especially in relation to water.
  • Q: Q3. What methods did the Muslim scientists proposed to store water?
    Ans: The Muslim scientists proposed methods of collecting, transporting and storing water, because the dry and harsh environment of much of the Muslim lands made it important. In the tenth century al-Kindi proposed a plan to dam the Nile. They constructed dams, reservoirs and aqueducts, perfected the waterwheel, and built underground water channels some fifty feet underground, with manholes so that they could be cleaned and repaired.
  • Q: Q4. Describe some of the inventions of the early Muslim scientists.
    Ans: Muslim engineers perfected the waterwheel; the Syrian waterwheel is still working. They built underground water channels some fifty feet underground, which had manholes (openings from the street) so that they could be cleaned and repaired. They also constructed many dams, reservoirs and aqueducts throughout the Islamic world, many of which still survive. Under al-Ma'mun, astronomical observatories were also set up.
  • Q: Q5. Can you name some famous scientists of Pakistan?
    Ans: Some famous scientists of Pakistan are Dr. Abdus Salam, the Nobel Prize winning physicist, and Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan, the famous nuclear scientist. (This is a general-knowledge question; these names are not given in the lesson text.)
  • Q: Q6. Do we still use waterwheel in our cities and villages? Have you seen one?
    Ans: Model answer: The waterwheel is not commonly seen in our big cities now, but it can still be seen in some villages where water is lifted from canals and wells. I have seen one in a village. The lesson also tells us that the Syrian waterwheel is still working.

Comprehension — B. Fill in the missing words to complete the cloze paragraph

  • Q: Muslim engineers also perfected the ______ and built underground water channels some fifty feet underground.
    Ans: waterwheel
  • Q: Muslim engineers also perfected the waterwheel and built underground water channels ______ fifty feet underground.
    Ans: some
  • Q: The underground ______ had manholes (openings from the street) so that they could be cleaned and repaired.

  • Q: The underground channels had manholes (openings from the ______) so that they could be cleaned and repaired.
    Ans: street
  • Q: The underground channels had manholes (openings from the street) so that they could be ______ and repaired.
    Ans: cleaned
  • Q: Syrian waterwheel is ______ working.
    Ans: still

  • Q: Muslims translated most of the scientific works of antiquity into Arabic.
    Ans: True
  • Q: The significant achievements made by Muslims led to the naming of this period as the Islamic Golden Age.

    Ans: False

    Ans: False

Vocabulary — A. Find the meaning of the following words from the dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviation used

  • Q: Find the meaning of 'technology' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: the knowledge and skill needed to design and make machines and other man-made things. Part of speech: noun (n).
  • Q: Find the meaning of 'invention' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: a thing that is made or designed for the first time. Part of speech: noun (n).
  • Q: Find the meaning of 'discovered' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: found out or learnt something that nobody knew before. Part of speech: verb (v).
  • Q: Find the meaning of 'carried' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: took or moved something or someone from one place to another. Part of speech: verb (v).
  • Q: Find the meaning of 'reservoir' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: a large lake, especially an artificial one, where water is stored before it is supplied to people's houses. Part of speech: noun (n).

Vocabulary — B. Consult a thesaurus and find out the synonyms

  • Q: Synonym of 'heat'
    Ans: Warmth; hotness.
  • Q: Synonym of 'fact'

  • Q: Synonym of 'knowledge'
    Ans: Learning; information; understanding.

  • Q: A. Write down the summary of the first and second paragraph of the lesson.
    Ans: Islam emerged as a religious movement in 622 AD, when Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) migrated to Madina. One hundred and fifty years later this religion grew and established an empire, which stretched from Syria to southern China and from India across to North Africa and southern Spain. chapters.title: Unit 10: The Happiness and Prosperity of the Home

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Read the title and predict what could be the lesson about.
    Ans: The title and the picture of a big dam suggest that the lesson is about the progress and prosperity of Pakistan, our home: how we can make our country strong and prosperous by using our resources properly, adopting modern techniques and technology, ending unemployment and promoting education.

Glossary

  • Q: What does 'democratic' mean?
    Ans: Controlled by representatives who are elected by the people of a country; connected with this system.
  • Q: What does 'streamline' mean?
    Ans: To give something a smooth even shape (in the lesson: to organize and use resources properly in order to gain progress and prosperity).
  • Q: What does 'prosperity' mean?
    Ans: The state of being successful, especially in making money.
  • Q: What does 'illiterate' mean?
    Ans: Not knowing how to read or write.
  • Q: What does 'sweep' mean?
    Ans: To move or push somebody/something suddenly and with a lot of force.
  • Q: What does 'strive' mean?
    Ans: To try very hard to achieve something.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. How can our country flourish if we adopt modern technique of irrigation?
    Ans: If we adopt modern techniques of irrigation and cultivation, farmers will produce more crops. Sufficient quantity of fertilizer, water supply and seed should be provided to the farmers, so that our country becomes strong and self-sufficient in cash and edible crops, and we may save our wealth by not importing food crops from other countries. In this way our country will flourish.
  • Q: Q2. How can we eradicate unemployment from our country?
    Ans: We can eradicate unemployment by taking immediate steps: we should expand new industries in all the possible places where resources are easily available, and promote technical education so that more and more people become skilled and get work. The lesson says it is very essential to take immediate steps to wipe out unemployment from Pakistan.
  • Q: Q3. How can we make our country self-sufficient in cash and edible crops?
    Ans: To make our country self-sufficient in cash and edible crops, we should adopt the modern techniques of irrigation and cultivation. Sufficient quantity of fertilizer, water supply and seed should be provided to the farmers, so that they can produce more crops and we may save our wealth by not importing food crops from other countries.
  • Q: Q4. How unemployment leads to social, economic and political problems?
    Ans: Unemployment is a curse for a country; it creates a lot of economic, social and political problems. It causes many evils in the country and the government is compelled to face these serious problems. The educated, illiterate, farmers, skilled and unskilled are all suffering from this serious problem.
  • Q: Q5. What role does education play in the progress of a country?
    Ans: Education plays the key role in the prosperity of a country. Therefore we must strive hard to increase the literacy rate of our country, and both male and female education should be promoted in order to achieve happiness and prosperity of our home.
  • Q: Q6. Why technical education should be promoted in our country?
    Ans: Technical education should be promoted because the need for technical education is very great: our country is on the way to industrialization, so it is necessary that there should be a shift of emphasis in our education, and more and more people should get technical education. This will also help to end unemployment and add to the progress and prosperity of Pakistan.

Vocabulary — A. Find the meaning of the following words from the dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviation used

  • Q: Find the meaning of 'technology' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: the scientific knowledge used in practical ways in industry, for example in designing and making machines. Part of speech: noun (n).
  • Q: Find the meaning of 'economic' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: connected with the way a country or a person organizes and manages money and trade. Part of speech: adjective (adj).
  • Q: Find the meaning of 'skilled' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: having a special ability or training in doing something well. Part of speech: adjective (adj).
  • Q: Find the meaning of 'sufficient' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: enough for a particular purpose. Part of speech: adjective (adj).
  • Q: Find the meaning of 'resources' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: the natural or man-made wealth and supplies of a country that can be used for its progress. Part of speech: noun (n, plural).

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: Write a short essay on "how to improve the methods of cultivation in our country."
    Ans: Pakistan is a developing country with abundant mineral and natural resources, but our methods of cultivation are old. To improve them, we should first of all adopt the modern techniques of irrigation and cultivation. Farmers should be provided with a sufficient quantity of fertilizer, good seed and a proper water supply, so that they can produce more crops. Modern machinery should be used in the fields instead of old tools, and farmers should be trained in the use of new technology. Secondly, new dams and water channels should be built so that no water is wasted and every field gets water in time. If we use our resources in this planned way, we will become self-sufficient in cash and edible crops. We will save our wealth by not importing food crops from other countries, and we will be able to export our extra crops. In this way, improved methods of cultivation will make our farmers happy, end much of the unemployment in the villages, and add to the progress and prosperity of our beloved homeland, Pakistan.

mcqs.q: What is Pakistan described as in the essay on improving cultivation?
options: A developed country with modern methods only
A developing country with abundant mineral and natural resources
A country with no natural resources
A country that imports all its crops only
mcqs.why: The essay begins by describing Pakistan as a developing country with abundant mineral and natural resources, but with old methods of cultivation.

mcqs.q: What is the first step to improve methods of cultivation, according to the essay?
options: Use old tools in the fields
Import food crops from other countries
Adopt the modern techniques of irrigation and cultivation
mcqs.why: The essay says first of all we should adopt the modern techniques of irrigation and cultivation to improve our methods and produce more crops.

mcqs.q: What should farmers be provided with to produce more crops?
options: Sufficient quantity of fertilizer, good seed and a proper water supply
mcqs.why: The essay states farmers should be provided with a sufficient quantity of fertilizer, good seed and a proper water supply so they can produce more crops.

mcqs.q: What should be used in the fields instead of old tools?
mcqs.why: The essay says modern machinery should be used in the fields instead of old tools, and farmers should be trained in the use of new technology.

mcqs.q: Why should new dams and water channels be built?
options: So water is wasted in fields
So no water is wasted and every field gets water in time
So old tools can be stored there
mcqs.why: The essay explains new dams and water channels should be built so that no water is wasted and every field gets water in time.

mcqs.q: If resources are used in a planned way, Pakistan will become:
options: Self-sufficient in cash and edible crops
mcqs.why: The essay states that using resources in a planned way will make us self-sufficient in cash and edible crops and save wealth by not importing food crops.

mcqs.q: What will Pakistan be able to do with its extra crops?
mcqs.why: The essay says we will save wealth by not importing food crops and will be able to export our extra crops to other countries.

mcqs.q: How should farmers be helped to use new technology?
options: They should be given old tools only
They should be left without training
They should be trained in the use of new technology
mcqs.why: The essay states farmers should be trained in the use of new technology, along with being provided fertilizer, good seed and water supply.

mcqs.q: What effect will improved cultivation have on unemployment, according to the essay?
options: It will increase unemployment in villages
It will end much of the unemployment in the villages
It will have no effect on villages
It will end education in villages
mcqs.why: The essay concludes improved methods of cultivation will make farmers happy and end much of the unemployment in the villages.

mcqs.q: What is the final result of improved cultivation for Pakistan, according to the essay?
options: It will add to the progress and prosperity of Pakistan
It will make Pakistan import more food
It will stop farmers from working
mcqs.why: The essay concludes improved cultivation will add to the progress and prosperity of our beloved homeland, Pakistan.
