lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — A. Write a short paragraph on "Struggle for Pakistan as a separate State"

  • Q: Write a short paragraph on "Struggle for Pakistan as a separate State." Show cause and effect of events in your writing.
    Ans: The Muslims of India wanted a separate state because they were a separate nation from the Hindus. Allama Iqbal explained this idea in his Allahabad Address in 1930, and as a result the Muslims woke from their sleep and started a strong struggle. Because Iqbal's poetry and speeches gave them courage and hope, the Muslims united under one cause. The leaders worked day and night, therefore the demand for a separate homeland became stronger every day. Many people faced hardships and gave sacrifices, but they did not stop, so their struggle continued with full spirit. Ultimately, their efforts bore fruit and a separate Muslim state, Pakistan, came into being. Thus, the cause was the dream of a free homeland, and the effect was the creation of Pakistan.

Writing — B. Who is your favourite personality. Give his/ her detailed physical description and personality traits

  • Q: Who is your favourite personality. Give his/ her detailed physical description and personality traits. (description of face, description of build, description of clothes, description of habits, description of attitudes)
    Ans: My favourite personality is Allama Iqbal, the National Poet of Pakistan. description of face: He had a thoughtful and serious face that showed his deep thinking and wisdom. description of build: He was a well-built man with a strong and dignified personality. description of clothes: He wore neat and simple clothes, and after taking his Barrister's Degree from London he also wore the dress of a barrister. description of habits: He had a habit of deep study and writing. He wrote poetry in Urdu and Persian and was greatly influenced by the philosophical teachings of Jalalud Din Mohammad Rumi. description of attitudes: He was a great mystic, a moralist, a reformer and an educationist. He was deeply concerned about the youth and wanted them to focus on their self-realization.

mcqs.q: In the paragraph on the struggle for Pakistan, what was the cause of the Muslims' demand for a separate state?
options: They wanted a separate state because they were a separate nation from the Hindus.
They wanted Iqbal to become a barrister in London.
They wanted to write poetry in Urdu and Persian.
They wanted to preside over the Allahabad meeting.
mcqs.why: The paragraph shows cause and effect: the Muslims wanted a separate state because they were a separate nation from the Hindus.

mcqs.q: What was the effect of Iqbal's Allahabad Address of 1930, as shown in the paragraph?
options: The Muslims went back to sleep.
The Muslims woke from their sleep and started a strong struggle.
Pakistan came into being the same year.
The demand for a homeland became weaker.
mcqs.why: The paragraph says that as a result of Iqbal's Address the Muslims woke from their sleep and started a strong struggle for a separate homeland.

mcqs.q: Why did the Muslims unite under one cause, according to the paragraph?
options: Because their leaders worked day and night only.
Because many people faced hardships and sacrifices.
Because Iqbal's poetry and speeches gave them courage and hope.
Because their efforts had already borne fruit.
mcqs.why: The paragraph gives this cause: because Iqbal's poetry and speeches gave them courage and hope, the Muslims united under one cause.

mcqs.q: What was the final effect of the Muslims' struggle, as the paragraph concludes?
options: Their struggle stopped after many hardships.
The leaders gave up the demand for a homeland.
Iqbal delivered another address in Allahabad.
A separate Muslim state, Pakistan, came into being.
mcqs.why: The paragraph concludes that ultimately their efforts bore fruit and a separate Muslim state, Pakistan, came into being — the dream's effect.

mcqs.q: How is Allama Iqbal's face described in the description of the favourite personality?
options: A lean, suntanned face with horns covered by a turban
A thoughtful and serious face that showed his deep thinking and wisdom
A smiling face that showed his humour and playfulness
A weary and sad face wrinkled with age
mcqs.why: The description of face says he had a thoughtful and serious face that showed his deep thinking and wisdom.

mcqs.q: How is Allama Iqbal's build described?
options: A weak man with a bent back
A tall man with a thin and delicate build
A well-built man with a strong and dignified personality
A little man who was talkative and quick
mcqs.why: The description of build says he was a well-built man with a strong and dignified personality.

mcqs.q: What is said about Allama Iqbal's clothes?
options: He wore the dress of a king with a turban.
He wore neat and simple clothes, and after his Barrister's Degree from London he also wore the dress of a barrister.
He wore wrinkled clothes because of his hard work.
He wore the clothes of a soldier in the struggle.
mcqs.why: The description of clothes says he wore neat and simple clothes and, after taking his Barrister's Degree from London, also wore the dress of a barrister.

mcqs.q: What habit of Allama Iqbal is described?
options: A habit of combing his hair in different styles
A habit of resting while others worked
A habit of deep study and writing, in Urdu and Persian
A habit of travelling to distant places
mcqs.why: The description of habits says he had a habit of deep study and writing and wrote poetry in Urdu and Persian.

mcqs.q: By whose philosophical teachings was Allama Iqbal greatly influenced?
options: The poetess Ellen M. H. Gates
The leaders of the Muslim League
mcqs.why: The description of habits says he was greatly influenced by the philosophical teachings of Jalalud Din Mohammad Rumi.

mcqs.q: Which set of attitudes is given for Allama Iqbal in the description?
options: He was vain, boastful and unkind to the youth.
He was a famous musician and a great novelist.
He was a great mystic, a moralist, a reformer and an educationist, deeply concerned about the youth.
He was a barrister who cared only for law cases.
mcqs.why: The description of attitudes calls him a great mystic, a moralist, a reformer and an educationist who was deeply concerned about the youth and their self-realization.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking

  • Q: Describe your favourite place in front of the class.
    Ans: Model speech: My favourite place is Hazuri Bagh in Lahore, because the tomb of my favourite poet, Allama Iqbal, is located there. It is the enclosed garden between the entrance of the Badshahi Mosque and the Lahore Fort. It is a peaceful and beautiful place, and official guards provided by the Government of Pakistan are present at the tomb. When I stand there, I remember Iqbal's poetry and his dream for Pakistan, and I feel proud and calm. That is why Hazuri Bagh is my favourite place.

chapters.title: Unit 14: Why the Sea is Salty?

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Predict the story by looking at the title of the story.
    Ans: By looking at the title "Why the Sea is Salty", we can predict that the story will explain, in the form of a myth, how the sea became salty. It will tell about someone or something that poured salt into the sea.
  • Q: Q2. Where do you think the story is taking place?
    Ans: The story seems to take place in a village near a forest and the sea, because the story is about two brothers, a demon living in a forest cave, and fishermen catching fish at the sea.
  • Q: Q3. How many characters you think are there in the story?
    Ans: There are two main brothers in the story, the elder rich brother and the younger poor brother. There are also other characters like the younger brother's wife, the elder brother's wife and the demon.
  • Q: Q4. What types of stories do you like i.e. fairy tales, folk tales or fables?
    Ans: I like folk tales and fables because they are simple stories passed on from person to person and they often give a moral lesson, like this story which teaches us that greed brings destruction.

Myth and Legend

  • Q: What are myth and legend?
    Ans: Myth and legend are semi-true stories passed on from person-to-person. Myths are often used to explain universal and local beginnings and involve supernatural beings.

Glossary

  • Q: Give the meaning of: millstone
    Ans: one of a pair of large, circular, flat stones used, especially in the past, to crush grain to make flour
  • Q: Give the meaning of: generous
    Ans: willing to give money, help, kindness, etc., especially more than is usual or expected
  • Q: Give the meaning of: hoof
    Ans: the hard part on the bottom of the feet of animals such as horses, sheep, and deer
  • Q: Give the meaning of: pouring
    Ans: to make a substance flow from a container
  • Q: Give the meaning of: demons
    Ans: an evil spirit
  • Q: Give the meaning of: scrumptious
    Ans: tasting extremely good / delicious
  • Q: Give the meaning of: rowed
    Ans: the activity of making a boat move through water using oars
  • Q: Give the meaning of: heaps
    Ans: a lot of
  • Q: Give the meaning of: grinding
    Ans: to make something into small pieces or a powder by pressing between hard surfaces
  • Q: Give the meaning of: bottom
    Ans: the lowest part of something
  • Q: Give the meaning of: cave
    Ans: a large hole in the side of a hill, cliff, or mountain, or one that is underground

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Who are the main characters of the story?
    Ans: The main characters of the story are the two brothers — the elder brother, who was rich, selfish and arrogant, and the younger brother, who was poor, kind-hearted and generous — and the demon who had the magical millstone.
  • Q: Q2. Are there any minor characters in the story? If so who are they?
    Ans: Yes, there are minor characters in the story. They are the younger brother's wife, who asked him to bring food, the elder brother's wife, who brought the goat's hoof from the kitchen, and the fishermen at the sea who were catching fish and putting them in salt.
  • Q: Q3. Is there any moral in the story? If so what is it?
    Ans: Yes, there is a moral in the story. The moral is that greed is a curse and brings destruction, while kindness, patience and using a gift wisely bring happiness. The kind younger brother used the millstone wisely and became happy, but the greedy elder brother snatched it, could not control it, and drowned.
  • Q: Q4. Do you think the sea water is salty due to the millstone? Why?
    Ans: No, in real life the sea water is not salty due to the millstone. This is a myth — a semi-true story passed on from person-to-person to explain a beginning. According to the story, the magical millstone is still grinding at the bottom of the sea and pouring out salt, thus making the sea salty, but this is only the story's way of explaining it.
  • Q: Q5. Which character do you dislike and why?
    Ans: I dislike the elder brother because he was very selfish and arrogant. He gave his starving younger brother only a goat's hoof instead of food, and later, overcome with greed, he snatched the magical millstone away from him. His greed finally caused his own death.
  • Q: Q6. Who is your favourite character in the story and why?
    Ans: My favourite character is the younger brother because he was kind-hearted and generous. He was poor and starving, yet he remained patient and polite. He used the magical millstone wisely, said "Enough, the work is done!" at the right time, and from that day he and his wife were poor no more.
  • Q: Q7. What do you think the poor man will do, now that he doesn't have a magic millstone to make gold, jewel and food for him?
    Ans: The poor man will now live on what the millstone has already given him — good clothes, scrumptious food and a big house — and he will work honestly to earn his living. He is kind-hearted, patient and not greedy, so he will remain content and happy even without the magical millstone.

Comprehension — B. Write in the space provided, the category each of the sentence falls in i.e. character, setting or problem

  • Q: Write the category the sentence falls in i.e. character, setting or problem: 1. Poor man and demon
    Ans: character
  • Q: Write the category the sentence falls in i.e. character, setting or problem: 2. In his excitement, the elder brother forgot how to stop the millstone.
    Ans: problem
  • Q: Write the category the sentence falls in i.e. character, setting or problem: 3. The forest was dark and gloomy.
    Ans: setting

mcqs.q: What does 'millstone' mean in the story?
options: One of a pair of large, circular, flat stones used to crush grain to make flour
A large hole in the side of a hill
The hard part on the bottom of an animal's feet
mcqs.why: The glossary defines a millstone as one of a pair of large, circular, flat stones used, especially in the past, to crush grain to make flour.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'generous' mean?
options: Willing to give money, help or kindness, more than is usual or expected
mcqs.why: The glossary explains that 'generous' means willing to give money, help, kindness, etc., especially more than is usual or expected.

mcqs.q: Who are the main characters of the story 'Why the Sea is Salty?'
options: Only the fishermen at the sea
The two brothers and the demon who had the magical millstone
Only the two wives of the brothers
mcqs.why: The main characters are the two brothers, the rich elder brother and the poor younger brother, and the demon who had the magical millstone.

mcqs.q: What is the moral of the story?
options: Greed is a curse and brings destruction, while kindness and patience bring happiness
Everyone should live near the sea
mcqs.why: The moral is that greed is a curse and brings destruction, while kindness, patience and using a gift wisely bring happiness, as the two brothers' fates show.

mcqs.q: Why is the elder brother disliked in the story?
options: He worked honestly in a small shop
He said 'Enough, the work is done!' at the right time
He was selfish and arrogant and gave his starving brother only a goat's hoof
mcqs.why: The elder brother is disliked because he was very selfish and arrogant: he gave his starving younger brother only a goat's hoof and later snatched the millstone in greed.

mcqs.q: Why is the younger brother the favourite character?
options: He snatched the millstone and ran to the sea
He was kind-hearted and generous and used the millstone wisely
He forgot how to stop the millstone
He lived in a cave in the forest
mcqs.why: The younger brother is the favourite because he was kind-hearted and generous, remained patient and polite, and used the magical millstone wisely.

mcqs.q: What does 'demons' mean?
mcqs.why: According to the glossary, 'demons' means an evil spirit, and in the story the demon lived in a forest cave and owned the magical millstone.

mcqs.q: What does 'scrumptious' mean?
mcqs.why: The glossary gives 'scrumptious' as tasting extremely good or delicious, and the younger brother later enjoyed scrumptious food with his wife.

mcqs.q: In story elements, 'The forest was dark and gloomy' falls in which category?
mcqs.why: A description of the place and atmosphere, such as 'The forest was dark and gloomy', describes the setting of the story, not a character or a problem.

mcqs.q: What are myths and legends?
options: Semi-true stories passed on from person to person, often explaining beginnings
Lists of difficult words and meanings
mcqs.why: Myth and legend are semi-true stories passed on from person to person; myths are often used to explain universal and local beginnings and involve supernatural beings.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — A. Find the meaning of the following words in a dictionary and tell which part of speech they are

  • Q: Find the meaning of the word and tell which part of speech it is: gloomy
    Ans: dark, dull and sad; almost dark so that it is difficult to see clearly — Adjective.
  • Q: Find the meaning of the word and tell which part of speech it is: drowned
    Ans: died by being under water and unable to breathe; was sunk under water — Verb.
  • Q: Find the meaning of the word and tell which part of speech it is: sank
    Ans: went down below the surface of water; moved downwards to the bottom — Verb.
  • Q: Find the meaning of the word and tell which part of speech it is: suddenly
    Ans: quickly and unexpectedly; in a sudden way — Adverb.
  • Q: Find the meaning of the word and tell which part of speech it is: greedy
    Ans: wanting more food, money, etc. than one needs or deserves — Adjective.

Vocabulary — B. Rewrite the sentences below in your notebooks using capital letters and punctuation marks in the correct places

  • Q: Rewrite the sentence using capital letters and punctuation marks in the correct places: 1. did the class go for a nature walk
    Ans: Did the class go for a nature walk?
  • Q: Rewrite the sentence using capital letters and punctuation marks in the correct places: 2. the rope almost broke because too many people pulled on it
    Ans: The rope almost broke because too many people pulled on it.
  • Q: Rewrite the sentence using capital letters and punctuation marks in the correct places: 3. that effect was spectacular,we enjoyed it very much
    Ans: That effect was spectacular, we enjoyed it very much.
  • Q: Rewrite the sentence using capital letters and punctuation marks in the correct places: 4. the solution to the problem was posted on the board
    Ans: The solution to the problem was posted on the board.
  • Q: Rewrite the sentence using capital letters and punctuation marks in the correct places: 5. i feel so alive today
    Ans: I feel so alive today.

Vocabulary — C. Put the three pictures below in sequence

  • Q: Put the three pictures below in sequence with which event happened first. After you have ordered the pictures, write a sentence about what is happening in each picture using sequence markers first, next, then and last.
    Ans: First, the children are waiting at the bus stop for their school bus. Next, the school bus arrives and stops at the bus stop. Then, a boy runs quickly to catch the bus before it leaves. Last, the school bus, full of children, drives away to school.

Grammar — Analogy: Complete each analogy using a word from the box

  • Q: In is to out as up is to ______
    Ans: down
  • Q: Go is to green as red is to ______
    Ans: stop
  • Q: Wheel is to bike as tire is to ______
    Ans: car
  • Q: Land is to dirt as ocean is to ______
    Ans: water
  • Q: Toe is to foot as finger is to ______
    Ans: hand
  • Q: Day is to month as minute is to ______
    Ans: hour
  • Q: Purple is to grapes as red is to ______
    Ans: cherries
  • Q: Word is to sentence as page is to ______
    Ans: book
  • Q: Small is to large as little is to ______
    Ans: big
  • Q: Three is to triangle as four is to ______
    Ans: square
  • Q: Smell is to nose as sight is to ______
    Ans: eye
  • Q: Top is to bottom as over is to ______
    Ans: under

mcqs.q: What part of speech is 'gloomy', meaning dark, dull and sad?
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise lists 'gloomy', meaning dark, dull and sad, as an adjective because it describes the quality of a place or scene.

mcqs.q: What part of speech is 'drowned', meaning died by being under water?
mcqs.why: 'Drowned', meaning died by being under water and unable to breathe, is listed as a verb because it shows an action or happening.

mcqs.q: What part of speech is 'suddenly', meaning quickly and unexpectedly?
mcqs.why: 'Suddenly', meaning quickly and unexpectedly or in a sudden way, is an adverb because it tells how an action happens.

mcqs.q: What does 'greedy' mean?
options: Dark so that it is difficult to see clearly
Went down below the surface of water
Wanting more food, money, etc. than one needs or deserves
mcqs.why: The notes define 'greedy' as wanting more food, money, etc. than one needs or deserves, and it is an adjective describing such a person.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correctly written with capital letters and punctuation?
options: did the class go for a nature walk
Did the class go for a nature walk?
Did the class go for a nature walk.
did the class go for a nature walk?
mcqs.why: A question begins with a capital letter and ends with a question mark, so the correct form is 'Did the class go for a nature walk?'

mcqs.q: Which is the correct form of 'the rope almost broke because too many people pulled on it'?
options: The rope almost broke because too many people pulled on it.
the rope almost broke because too many people pulled on it
The rope almost broke because too many people pulled on it?
The Rope Almost Broke Because Too Many People Pulled On It
mcqs.why: A statement begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, giving 'The rope almost broke because too many people pulled on it.'

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
mcqs.why: The pronoun 'I' is always written with a capital letter and the statement ends with a full stop: 'I feel so alive today.'

mcqs.q: In the picture sequence, what happens FIRST?
options: The school bus, full of children, drives away to school
A boy runs quickly to catch the bus
The school bus arrives and stops at the bus stop
The children are waiting at the bus stop for their school bus
mcqs.why: Using sequence markers, the first event is that the children are waiting at the bus stop for their school bus, before the bus arrives.

mcqs.q: In the picture sequence, what happens LAST?
options: The children are waiting at the bus stop
The school bus, full of children, drives away to school
The school bus arrives at the bus stop
A boy runs to catch the bus
mcqs.why: The last event in the sequence is that the school bus, full of children, drives away to school, marked by the sequence word 'Last'.

mcqs.q: Complete the analogy: In is to out as up is to ______.
mcqs.why: In and out are opposites, so up pairs with its opposite, down, in the analogy given in the grammar exercise.

mcqs.q: Complete the analogy: Go is to green as red is to ______.
mcqs.why: Green means go in traffic signals, so red, the opposite signal colour, pairs with stop in this analogy.

mcqs.q: Complete the analogy: Toe is to foot as finger is to ______.
mcqs.why: A toe is part of a foot, just as a finger is part of a hand, so the analogy is completed by the word 'hand'.

mcqs.q: Complete the analogy: Day is to month as minute is to ______.
mcqs.why: Days make up a month in the same way that minutes make up a larger unit of time, an hour, in this analogy.

mcqs.q: Complete the analogy: Word is to sentence as page is to ______.
mcqs.why: Words join to make a sentence, just as pages join to make a book, so 'book' completes the analogy correctly.

mcqs.q: Complete the analogy: Smell is to nose as sight is to ______.
mcqs.why: Smell is the sense of the nose, and sight is the sense of the eye, so the analogy is completed by the word 'eye'.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — A. Write down the character sketches of elder and younger brother from the story in your notebooks

  • Q: Write down the character sketch of the elder brother from the story. Give detailed physical description and personality traits.
    Ans: The elder brother was rich, while his younger brother was poor. In personality, he was very selfish and arrogant. When his starving younger brother came to him for food, he did not help him properly and only gave him the goat's hoof which the demon wanted. He secretly saw his younger brother using the magical millstone and, overcome with greed, he snatched the millstone away from him. He ran to the beach and rowed out to the sea to make salt and become richer, but in his excitement he forgot how to stop the millstone. In the end, his greed destroyed him and he drowned in the sea.
  • Q: Write down the character sketch of the younger brother from the story. Give detailed physical description and personality traits.
    Ans: The younger brother was poor, but he was kind-hearted and generous. When he and his wife had been starving for two days, he went to his elder brother and politely pleaded for some food. He took the goat's hoof to the demon, greeted him respectfully, and firmly asked for the magical millstone in return, refusing silver, gold and even diamonds. At home, he used the millstone wisely: he wished for food, ate well with his wife, and stopped the millstone at the right time by saying, "Enough, the work is done!" From that day on, he and his wife were poor no more and lived happily with good clothes, scrumptious food and a big house.

Writing — B. Write a story with the following beginning

  • Q: Write a story with the following beginning: Once there was a man. He wanted to be wealthy.
    Ans: Once there was a man. He wanted to be wealthy. He worked hard in his small shop from morning till evening, but he earned only a little money. One day, he found a small bag of gold coins buried near his house. He became very happy and thought that his days of poverty were over. Instead of wasting the gold, he used it wisely. He bought a bigger shop, treated his customers kindly, and helped the poor people of his village. Because of his honesty and hard work, his business grew day by day. People trusted him and liked to buy things from him. In a few years, he truly became a wealthy man. But he never became proud or greedy, because he had learned that wealth earned with honesty and used wisely brings real happiness.

mcqs.q: How is the elder brother described in his character sketch?
options: A demon living in a forest cave
mcqs.why: The character sketch describes the elder brother as rich in wealth but very selfish and arrogant in personality, unlike his poor younger brother.

mcqs.q: What did the elder brother give his starving younger brother?
options: A big house and good clothes
mcqs.why: When the starving younger brother came for food, the elder brother did not help him properly and only gave him the goat's hoof the demon wanted.

mcqs.q: What did the elder brother do after secretly seeing the millstone?
options: He snatched the millstone away from him
He gave him silver and diamonds
He stopped the millstone for him
mcqs.why: Overcome with greed, the elder brother secretly watched his brother using the millstone and then snatched the magical millstone away from him.

mcqs.q: How did the elder brother die?
options: He was punished by the demon
He worked too hard in his shop
He forgot how to stop the millstone at sea and drowned
mcqs.why: He rowed out to sea to make salt, but in his excitement he forgot how to stop the millstone, and his greed destroyed him as he drowned in the sea.

mcqs.q: For how long had the younger brother and his wife been starving before he asked for food?
mcqs.why: The younger brother's sketch says that he and his wife had been starving for two days when he went to his elder brother and politely pleaded for food.

mcqs.q: What did the younger brother refuse from the demon?
options: A boat to row to sea
mcqs.why: The younger brother greeted the demon respectfully and firmly asked for the magical millstone, refusing silver, gold and even diamonds in return.

mcqs.q: How did the younger brother stop the millstone at the right time?
options: By throwing it into the sea
By saying, 'Enough, the work is done!'
By calling the demon for help
mcqs.why: At home the younger brother used the millstone wisely and stopped it at the right time by saying, 'Enough, the work is done!'

mcqs.q: In the model story, what did the man find buried near his house?
options: A small bag of gold coins
mcqs.why: In the story beginning 'Once there was a man. He wanted to be wealthy', the man found a small bag of gold coins buried near his house.

mcqs.q: How did the man in the model story use his gold?
options: He hid it and told nobody
He used it wisely, bought a bigger shop and helped the poor
He threw it into the sea
mcqs.why: Instead of wasting the gold, the man used it wisely: he bought a bigger shop, treated customers kindly and helped the poor people of his village.

mcqs.q: What lesson did the man in the model story learn?
options: Wealth earned with honesty and used wisely brings real happiness
Greed always makes a man richer
A man should never help the poor
mcqs.why: The man never became proud or greedy because he had learned that wealth earned with honesty and used wisely brings real happiness.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Make Groups of five students each for role play. Change your voice to act out the role. The rise and fall of your tone should indicate the emotions of shock, discomfort, hate, and anger.

  • Q: Role play: Change your voice to act out the role. The rise and fall of your tone should indicate the emotions of shock, discomfort, hate, and anger.
    Ans: Work in a group of five and act out each speech bubble, changing your voice and using the rise and fall of tone to show the emotion: Shock — "I am shocked to see the size of the telephone bill" — say it in a loud, surprised voice with wide eyes. Discomfort — "I have sharp pain in my stomach" — say it in a weak, pained voice, holding your stomach. Hate / dislike — "I don't want to eat fish. I don't like fish." — say it in a displeased voice, turning away from the plate. Anger — "Leave me alone, I don't want to talk to anyone." — say it in a loud, angry voice with arms crossed.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Can you name some female athletes of Pakistan?
    Ans: Naseem Hamid is a famous female athlete of Pakistan. She is a runner who became the fastest woman in South Asia by winning the 100 metres race at the 11th South Asian Federation (SAF) Games in 2010.
  • Q: Q2. Is it easy for a female to compete?
    Ans: No, it is not easy for a female to compete. Naseem Hamid belonged to a low-income family and faced many difficulties. At times she even ran barefoot because her family could not afford jogging shoes, yet she never became discouraged.
  • Q: Q3. Does it take strong determination to win a game?
    Ans: Yes, it takes strong determination to win a game. Naseem Hamid trained very hard, came home with aching legs and never gave up practising. Her determination helped her beat all odds and win the gold medal in Dhaka.

Glossary

  • Q: Give the meaning of: discouraged
    Ans: Feeling less confident or enthusiastic about doing something.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: aching
    Ans: To feel a continuous dull pain.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: barefoot
    Ans: Not wearing anything on your feet.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: determination
    Ans: The quality that makes you continue trying to do something even when this is difficult.

Exercise A — Answer the questions given below

  • Q: Q1. Why did Naseem's mother say that she has always been very brave?
    Ans: Naseem's mother said that Naseem has always been very brave because she has overcome lots of troubles but never lost heart even when she couldn't win races. Her mother said, "Naseem is like a son to me."
  • Q: Q2. Why could Naseem not participate in the 10th SAF Games?
    Ans: Naseem could not participate in the 10th South Asian Games in Colombo in 2006 because of an injury. She had to watch her colleagues run the 4x100-metre race and win the bronze medal.
  • Q: Q3. Describe the achievement of Naeem in the 11th SAF Games.
    Ans: In the 11th South Asian Games, 2010, Naseem Hamid ran to victory in the 100 metres in 11.81 seconds in Bangladesh. She beat two Sri Lankans and an Indian to win the gold medal, becoming Pakistan's first woman to win a gold medal and the fastest woman in South Asia.
  • Q: Q4. What is the theme of the lesson?
    Ans: The theme of the lesson is determination and hard work. It teaches us that a person who never loses faith and keeps trying can overcome poverty, hardships and all obstacles and can succeed in life, just as Naseem Hamid did.
  • Q: Q5. Write an incident from Naseem Hamid's life when she showed determination.
    Ans: Naseem Hamid belonged to a low-income family, so at times she ran barefoot because the family could not afford jogging shoes. She trained very hard and would come back home with aching legs and fall asleep at once, but she never gave up practising. This shows her great determination to succeed.

Exercise B — Find words in the passage which mean the same as

  • Q: Q1. a piece of ground with a special surface for racing.
    Ans: track
  • Q: Q2. a person who competes in sports.
    Ans: athlete
  • Q: Q3. seen and noticed.
    Ans: spotted
  • Q: Q4. hindrance.
    Ans: obstacle

Exercise C — Frame interrogatives for the following statements

  • Q: Q1. The 10th South Asian Federation Games were held in Colombo in 2006.
    Ans: Where were the 10th South Asian Federation Games held in 2006?
  • Q: Q2. Naseem said that her aim is to win more gold medals for her country.
    Ans: What did Naseem say her aim is?
  • Q: Q3. Naseem lives in the Korangi area in Karachi.
    Ans: Where does Naseem live?

mcqs.q: Who is Naseem Hamid?
options: A runner who became the fastest woman in South Asia
A gold medal judge at the SAF Games
mcqs.why: Naseem Hamid is a famous female athlete of Pakistan, a runner who became the fastest woman in South Asia by winning the 100 metres race at the 11th SAF Games in 2010.

mcqs.q: In how much time did Naseem Hamid win the 100 metres race at the 11th SAF Games?
mcqs.why: At the 11th South Asian Games in 2010, Naseem Hamid ran to victory in the 100 metres in 11.81 seconds and won the gold medal.

mcqs.q: Why could Naseem not participate in the 10th SAF Games in Colombo in 2006?
options: She was too young to compete
mcqs.why: Naseem could not participate in the 10th South Asian Games in Colombo in 2006 because of an injury, and she watched her colleagues win the bronze medal.

mcqs.q: Why did Naseem sometimes run barefoot?
options: Her family could not afford jogging shoes
The track was soft and sandy
Her coach advised her to do so
mcqs.why: Naseem belonged to a low-income family, so at times she ran barefoot because her family could not afford jogging shoes, yet she never gave up.

mcqs.q: What does 'determination' mean?
options: Feeling less confident about doing something
Not wearing anything on your feet
The quality that makes you continue trying even when something is difficult
mcqs.why: The glossary defines determination as the quality that makes you continue trying to do something even when this is difficult, which Naseem showed throughout her career.

mcqs.q: Which word in the passage means 'a piece of ground with a special surface for racing'?
mcqs.why: In Exercise B, the word for a piece of ground with a special surface for racing is 'track', the surface on which runners compete.

mcqs.q: Which word means the same as 'hindrance'?
mcqs.why: Exercise B gives 'obstacle' as the word meaning hindrance, something that blocks progress, and Naseem overcame many obstacles in life.

mcqs.q: What is the theme of the lesson 'Woman and Sports Field'?
options: Determination and hard work help a person overcome all obstacles
Only rich athletes can win medals
mcqs.why: The theme of the lesson is determination and hard work: a person who never loses faith and keeps trying can overcome poverty, hardships and all obstacles.

mcqs.q: Why did Naseem's mother say that Naseem has always been very brave?
options: She won every race she entered
She lived in the Korangi area of Karachi
She has overcome lots of troubles but never lost heart even when she couldn't win races
She watched the 4x100-metre race in Colombo
mcqs.why: Her mother said Naseem has always been very brave because she has overcome lots of troubles but never lost heart even when she couldn't win races.

mcqs.q: Where does Naseem live?
options: In the Korangi area in Karachi
mcqs.why: Exercise C is based on the statement that Naseem lives in the Korangi area in Karachi, and the interrogative formed is 'Where does Naseem live?'

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A — Split the sentences into subject, verb, indirect object and direct object

  • Q: Q1. He denied his visitor an appointment.
    Ans: Subject: He; Verb: denied; Indirect Object: his visitor; Direct Object: an appointment.
  • Q: Q2. Asma showed him the door.
    Ans: Subject: Asma; Verb: showed; Indirect Object: him; Direct Object: the door.
  • Q: Q3. Neha offered her sister a soft drink.
    Ans: Subject: Neha; Verb: offered; Indirect Object: her sister; Direct Object: a soft drink.
  • Q: Q4. The girl told her friend a secret.
    Ans: Subject: The girl; Verb: told; Indirect Object: her friend; Direct Object: a secret.
  • Q: Q5. The court refused him bail.
    Ans: Subject: The court; Verb: refused; Indirect Object: him; Direct Object: bail.
  • Q: Q6. The boy gave his sister a bar of chocolate.
    Ans: Subject: The boy; Verb: gave; Indirect Object: his sister; Direct Object: a bar of chocolate.
  • Q: Q7. The chief guest awarded him a gold medal.
    Ans: Subject: The chief guest; Verb: awarded; Indirect Object: him; Direct Object: a gold medal.

Vocabulary B — Fill in the blanks with suitable abstract nouns formed from the verbs / nouns in brackets

  • Q: ______ is the best chapter in the book of wisdom. (honest)
    Ans: Honesty
  • Q: He was saved from trouble by this friend's timely ______. (brave)
    Ans: bravery
  • Q: There are reports of many deaths from ______ in Somalia. (hungry)
    Ans: hunger
  • Q: He was known for his generosity and ______. (kind)
    Ans: kindness
  • Q: ______ is the best medicine. (laugh)
    Ans: Laughter
  • Q: "He that have ______ can have what he will". (patient)
    Ans: patience
  • Q: In today's world ______ is not a bliss. (ignore)
    Ans: ignorance

Vocabulary C — Choose the correct pronoun

  • Q: Q1. We / Me are going for picnic on Wednesday.
    Options: We / Me
    Ans: We
  • Q: Q2. This is the girl who/whose parents want to meet you.
    Options: who / whose
    Ans: whose
  • Q: Q3. You and I/me are invited to dinner this evening.
    Options: I / me
    Ans: I
  • Q: Q4. He is as good as I/me.
    Options: I / me
    Ans: I
  • Q: Q5. Nobody but he/him was present at that time.
    Options: he / him
    Ans: him

Grammar A — Say whether the verbs in the given sentences are in the active or passive voice

  • Q: Q1. The boys realized their mistake.
    Ans: Active voice.
  • Q: Q2. Garbage is collected in large bins.
    Ans: Passive voice.
  • Q: Q3. The birthday girl distributed sweets.
    Ans: Active voice.
  • Q: Q4. An important letter was posted.
    Ans: Passive voice.
  • Q: Q5. The court refused him bail.
    Ans: Active voice.
  • Q: Q6. Maha is singing a beautiful song.
    Ans: Active voice.
  • Q: Q7. Jamil cleaned his cupboard.
    Ans: Active voice.
  • Q: Q8. Aalia collects old clothes for the poor.
    Ans: Active voice.
  • Q: Q9. A letter was torn into pieces by Amjad.
    Ans: Passive voice.
  • Q: Q10. A stranger was seen by the neighbours.
    Ans: Passive voice.

Revision Unit 11-15 A — Choose the correct indirect sentence for the following direct sentences

  • Q: Q1. He says, "They will hurt you".
    Options: He says to me that they will hurt me. / He said to me that he would be hurt me. / He said to me that they would hurt me. / He said to me that they would hurt you.
    Ans: He says to me that they will hurt me.
  • Q: Q2. My father said to me, "You must work hard".
    Options: My father said to me that I must work hard. / My father said to me that you must work hard. / My father said to me that you have to work hard. / My father said to me that I had to work hard.
    Ans: My father said to me that I must work hard.
  • Q: Q3. She said, "My parents are going to Karachi".
    Options: She said that my parents were going to Karachi. / She said that my parents gone to Karachi. / She said that her parents were going to Karachi. / She said that her parents are going to Karachi.
    Ans: She said that her parents were going to Karachi.
  • Q: Q4. Mother said, "Where are you going?"
    Options: Mother said me where I am going. / Mother said to me where are you going. / Mother asked where I was going. / Mother asked me where I am going.
    Ans: Mother asked where I was going.
  • Q: Q5. "Did you come from Lahore?" said Sara to the boy.
    Options: Sara asked the boy if he had come from Lahore. / Sara asked the boy if he come from Lahore. / Sara asked the boy if he came from Lahore. / Sara said the boy did he come from Lahore.
    Ans: Sara asked the boy if he had come from Lahore.

Revision Unit 11-15 B — Complete the following sentences using an indirect object or a direct object, as required

  • Q: Q1. I bought ______ a present.
    Ans: I bought her a present. (Indirect object: her)
  • Q: Q2. He threw the beggar ______.
    Ans: He threw the beggar a coin. (Direct object: a coin)
  • Q: Q3. The British Council offered him ______.
    Ans: The British Council offered him a job. (Direct object: a job)
  • Q: Q4. The man sent ______ a message.
    Ans: The man sent her a message. (Indirect object: her)
  • Q: Q5. My friend hit the ______.
    Ans: My friend hit the ball. (Direct object: the ball)
  • Q: Q6. We ran to the ______.
    Ans: We ran to the park. (Model completion)
  • Q: Q7. My sister went to ______.
    Ans: My sister went to school. (Model completion)
  • Q: Q8. The earthquake shook ______.
    Ans: The earthquake shook the whole city. (Direct object: the whole city)
  • Q: Q9. The singer ______.
    Ans: The singer sang a beautiful song. (Direct object: a beautiful song)
  • Q: Q10. Will you buy me ______?
    Ans: Will you buy me a watch? (Direct object: a watch)

Revision Unit 11-15 C — Complete the following sentences using suitable analogies

  • Q: Bird is to fly as fish is to ______.
    Ans: swim
  • Q: Parrot is to feathers as bear is to ______.
    Ans: fur
  • Q: Zebra is to stripes as giraffe is to ______.
    Ans: spots
  • Q: Goose is to flock as fish is to ______.
    Ans: shoal
  • Q: Ant is to six legs as spider is to ______.
    Ans: eight

Revision Unit 11-15 D — Fill in the blanks with the correct punctuation mark (full stop, exclamation mark or question mark)

  • Q: I am so excited to see my family for Eid ______
    Ans: !
  • Q: What day of the week is your favourite ______
    Ans: ?
  • Q: You need to do your homework right after dinner ______
    Ans: .
  • Q: Please take out the trash when you get home ______
    Ans: .
  • Q: My favourite team won the game ______
    Ans: !
  • Q: What did you want to eat for lunch ______
    Ans: ?

Revision Unit 11-15 E — Choose the correct passive voice for the given active sentences

  • Q: Q1. Why do they take you on lunch?
    Options: Why are you taken by them on lunch? / Why do you taken by them on lunch? / Why is you taken by them on lunch. / Why do you taken by them on lunch?
    Ans: Why are you taken by them on lunch?
  • Q: Q2. Will she oppose them?
    Options: Will she oppose them? / Will they opposed by her? / Will they be opposed by her? / Will they been opposed by her?
    Ans: Will they be opposed by her?
  • Q: Q3. Will they attend meeting?
    Options: Will the meeting attended by them? / Will the meeting being attended by them? / Will the meeting be attended by them. / Would the meeting attend by them?
    Ans: Will the meeting be attended by them.
  • Q: Q4. Do you know how to swim?
    Options: Is it known by you how to swim? / Does it know by you how to swim? / It is being known by you how to swim? / Is it knows by you how to swim?
    Ans: Is it known by you how to swim?
  • Q: Q5. Why does he always blame others?
    Options: Why others always blamed by him? / Why do others always blamed by him? / Why are others always blamed by him? / Why is others always blamed by him.?
    Ans: Why are others always blamed by him?

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect sentence: He says, "They will hurt you".
options: He said to me that they would hurt me.
He says to me that they will hurt me.
He said to me that he would be hurt me.
He said to me that they would hurt you.
mcqs.why: The reporting verb 'says' is in the present tense, so the tense does not change and 'you' becomes 'me': 'He says to me that they will hurt me.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect sentence: My father said to me, "You must work hard".
options: My father said to me that you must work hard.
My father said to me that I had to work hard.
My father said to me that I must work hard.
My father said to me that you have to work hard.
mcqs.why: In indirect speech 'you' changes to 'I' for the listener, while 'must' stays unchanged: 'My father said to me that I must work hard.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect sentence: She said, "My parents are going to Karachi".
options: She said that my parents were going to Karachi.
She said that her parents are going to Karachi.
She said that my parents gone to Karachi.
She said that her parents were going to Karachi.
mcqs.why: 'My' changes to 'her' and present continuous 'are going' changes to past continuous 'were going', giving 'She said that her parents were going to Karachi.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect sentence: Mother said, "Where are you going?"
options: Mother asked where I was going.
Mother said me where I am going.
Mother said to me where are you going.
Mother asked me where I am going.
mcqs.why: A question in indirect speech uses 'asked', changes 'are' to 'was' and keeps statement order: 'Mother asked where I was going.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive voice: Why do they take you on lunch?
options: Why do you taken by them on lunch?
Why is you taken by them on lunch.
Why are you taken by them on lunch?
Why you are taken by them on lunch?
mcqs.why: In the passive voice the object 'you' becomes the subject with 'are' plus the past participle: 'Why are you taken by them on lunch?'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive voice: Will she oppose them?
options: Will they be opposed by her?
Will they been opposed by her?
mcqs.why: With 'will', the passive form is 'will be' plus the past participle, so the correct sentence is 'Will they be opposed by her?'

mcqs.q: In 'He denied his visitor an appointment', what is the indirect object?
mcqs.why: In this sentence 'He' is the subject and 'denied' is the verb; 'his visitor' receives the thing given, so it is the indirect object, while 'an appointment' is the direct object.

mcqs.q: In 'The boy gave his sister a bar of chocolate', what is the direct object?
mcqs.why: The thing given, 'a bar of chocolate', is the direct object, while 'his sister', the person who receives it, is the indirect object.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with the abstract noun formed from 'honest': ______ is the best chapter in the book of wisdom.
mcqs.why: The abstract noun formed from the adjective 'honest' is 'honesty', so the sentence reads 'Honesty is the best chapter in the book of wisdom.'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with the abstract noun formed from 'laugh': ______ is the best medicine.
mcqs.why: The abstract noun formed from the verb 'laugh' is 'laughter', completing the well-known saying 'Laughter is the best medicine.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct pronoun: ______ are going for picnic on Wednesday. (We / Me)
mcqs.why: The subject of the sentence must be the subject pronoun 'We', so the correct sentence is 'We are going for picnic on Wednesday.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct pronoun: This is the girl ______ parents want to meet you. (who / whose)
mcqs.why: 'Whose' shows possession and is used because the parents belong to the girl: 'This is the girl whose parents want to meet you.'

mcqs.q: Say whether the verb is in active or passive voice: Garbage is collected in large bins.
mcqs.why: 'Garbage is collected in large bins' is in the passive voice because the subject receives the action and the doer is not named.

mcqs.q: Say whether the verb is in active or passive voice: The boys realized their mistake.
mcqs.why: 'The boys realized their mistake' is in the active voice because the subject, the boys, performs the action of realizing.

mcqs.q: Complete the analogy: Bird is to fly as fish is to ______.
mcqs.why: A bird's movement is to fly, and a fish's movement is to swim, so 'swim' completes the analogy in the revision exercise.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Write a letter to your younger brother and tell him about the determination of the athlete Naseem Hamid

  • Q: Write a letter to your younger brother and tell him about the determination of the athlete Naseem Hamid.
    Ans: Korangi, Karachi. 12 February, 2026 Dear Brother, Assalam-o-Alaikum! I hope you are well and working hard at your studies. In this letter I want to tell you about a great Pakistani athlete, Naseem Hamid, whose determination is a lesson for all of us. Naseem Hamid became the fastest woman in South Asia when she won the 100 metres race in 11.81 seconds at the 11th South Asian Games in 2010. She was Pakistan's first woman to win a gold medal there. But her success was not easy. She belonged to a low-income family of Korangi, Karachi, and at times she ran barefoot because her family could not afford jogging shoes. She trained very hard and often came home with aching legs, yet she never gave up practising. In 2006 an injury stopped her from taking part in the 10th South Asian Games, but she did not lose heart. She says that failures have always given her heart to perform, and that we can beat all odds through determination. Dear brother, learn from her life. Whatever difficulties come in your way, never lose faith and keep working hard, and one day you will succeed. Your loving brother, Ahmed

mcqs.q: From where is the letter about Naseem Hamid written?
mcqs.why: The letter is headed 'Korangi, Karachi', which is the area of Karachi where Naseem Hamid and the letter writer live.

mcqs.q: What is the date written on the letter?
mcqs.why: The letter written to the younger brother is dated 12 February, 2026, below the address Korangi, Karachi.

mcqs.q: To whom is the letter written?
mcqs.why: The writing task is a letter to the writer's younger brother, telling him about the determination of the athlete Naseem Hamid.

mcqs.q: Who signs the letter at the end?
mcqs.why: The letter closes with 'Your loving brother, Ahmed', so Ahmed is the writer who signs the letter to his younger brother.

mcqs.q: According to the letter, in how much time did Naseem win the 100 metres race in 2010?
mcqs.why: The letter states that Naseem Hamid won the 100 metres race in 11.81 seconds at the 11th South Asian Games in 2010.

mcqs.q: What distinction does the letter give Naseem at the 11th South Asian Games?
options: She was the youngest runner there
She was Pakistan's first woman to win a gold medal there
She was the only barefoot runner there
She was the captain of the whole team
mcqs.why: The letter says she became the fastest woman in South Asia and was Pakistan's first woman to win a gold medal at those games.

mcqs.q: What stopped Naseem from taking part in the 10th South Asian Games in 2006, according to the letter?
mcqs.why: The letter explains that in 2006 an injury stopped her from taking part in the 10th South Asian Games, but she did not lose heart.

mcqs.q: According to the letter, what have failures always given Naseem?
options: A wish to change her country
mcqs.why: The letter quotes her view that failures have always given her heart to perform, and that we can beat all odds through determination.

mcqs.q: What advice does the writer give his brother at the end of the letter?
options: To train only when life is easy
To never lose faith and keep working hard
mcqs.why: The writer advises his brother that whatever difficulties come in his way, he should never lose faith and keep working hard, and one day he will succeed.

mcqs.q: Why did Naseem run barefoot at times, according to the letter?
options: Her shoes were lost in Colombo
She belonged to a low-income family that could not afford jogging shoes
Barefoot running was the rule of the games
She was recovering from an injury
mcqs.why: The letter says she belonged to a low-income family of Korangi, Karachi, and at times ran barefoot because her family could not afford jogging shoes.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Etiquettes for a telephonic conversation: Work in pairs and practice the conversation below in front of the class

  • Q: Practice the telephonic conversation given in the unit in pairs.
    Ans: Model conversation (as printed in the unit): Receiver: Hello! Good Morning. Caller: Hello! Good Morning. Receiver: May I ask who's calling please? Caller: This is Tahir, can I speak to Asim please? Receiver: Hold the line please. I'll just put you through. Caller: Okay! Thank you. Receiver: Sorry, he is out at the moment. Caller: Oh! Can I leave a message please? Receiver: Sure! Caller: Please ask him to call me back as soon as he is home. Thank you. Receiver: I will tell him. Anything else? Caller: No, thank you. Bye. Guide: Always make a polite introduction, ask who is calling, check the message, and take or leave a message politely, as Tahir and the receiver do in this conversation.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Look at the picture and predict what could be the lesson about.
    Ans: The picture shows two happy girls who are close friends. From the title "Sand and Stone" and the picture of the two friends, we can predict that the lesson is about friendship — about two friends, the wrong one does to the other, and the good one does in return, and about forgiving and remembering kindness.

Glossary

  • Q: Give the meaning of: interfaith
    Ans: Relating to activities involving members of different religions.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: harmony
    Ans: A situation in which people are peaceful and agree with each other, or when things seem right or suitable together.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: quarrelled
    Ans: An angry disagreement between two or more people or groups.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: slapped
    Ans: A quick hit with the flat part of the hand or other flat object.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: oasis
    Ans: A place in a desert where there is water and therefore plants and trees.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: rushed
    Ans: Done in a hurry, or feeling that you must do something quickly.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: blown
    Ans: To move and make currents of air, or to be moved or make something move on a current of air.
  • Q: Give the meaning of: cherish
    Ans: To keep hopes, memories, or ideas in your mind because they are important to you and bring you pleasure.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Why did the villagers decide to move to another place? Explain.
    Ans: Once a flood came in the village of Mary and Farida and all the crops were destroyed. So the villagers decided to move to another place. Mary's and Farida's parents also decided to move, and they went in search of a job and visited many places to earn some money.
  • Q: Q2. (No question is printed for number 2 in the book.)
    Ans: Question 2 is blank in the printed book — no question is printed against number 2 (checked in both available scans of the book), so no answer can be given for it.
  • Q: Q3. Why Mary and Farida had an argument in the desert?
    Ans: Mary and Farida had an argument in the desert over water. They had very little food and water. Mary said that they should save the food and water for later use, but Farida disagreed because she was very thirsty and wanted to drink water. They quarrelled with each other, and Mary slapped Farida.
  • Q: Q4. Is God willing to forgive us when we sin?
    Ans: Yes. The lesson tells us that God is ready and willing to forgive us when we come to Him and say we are sorry.
  • Q: Q5. Who saved Farida from drowning in the water? Give detail of the event.
    Ans: Mary saved Farida from drowning. When they reached an oasis, both girls were bathing and having fun in the water. Farida was a bit careless and began to drown. Mary rushed to her and saved her. Farida hugged her friend and thanked her.
  • Q: Q6. Is it hard to forgive someone over and over again? Why?
    Ans: Yes, it can be hard to forgive someone over and over again, because being unwilling to forgive makes us feel weighed down inside, as if we are carrying a heavy load. Still, the lesson teaches us to forget the bad things and cherish the good things done to us, and to forgive others just as God forgives us when we say we are sorry.

Comprehension B — State whether the following statements are true or false

  • Q: To allow our anger or hate to cause someone harm does not please God.
    Ans: True
  • Q: We should change our hate and anger into love and forgiveness.
    Ans: True
  • Q: When we forgive someone, it means what they did was right.
    Ans: False
  • Q: God forgives all of our sins and we need to readily forgive others too.
    Ans: True
  • Q: When someone hurts us, we should take revenge.
    Ans: False

mcqs.q: Why did the villagers decide to move to another place?
options: A flood came and all the crops were destroyed
They found gold in another village
They wanted to visit an oasis
mcqs.why: Once a flood came in the village of Mary and Farida and all the crops were destroyed, so the villagers decided to move to another place.

mcqs.q: Why did Mary and Farida have an argument in the desert?
options: Over water, because Farida was very thirsty and Mary wanted to save it for later
mcqs.why: They had very little food and water; Mary said they should save it for later, but Farida disagreed because she was very thirsty and wanted to drink water.

mcqs.q: What did Mary do to Farida during the quarrel?
mcqs.why: During the quarrel in the desert, Mary slapped Farida, and this wrong action is the hurt that the lesson teaches us to forgive and forget.

mcqs.q: What is an 'oasis'?
options: A quick hit with the flat part of the hand
A situation where people live in peace
A place in a desert where there is water and therefore plants and trees
mcqs.why: The glossary defines an oasis as a place in a desert where there is water and therefore plants and trees, and the girls later reached such an oasis.

mcqs.q: What does 'harmony' mean?
options: A situation in which people are peaceful and agree with each other
A place with water in a desert
mcqs.why: Harmony means a situation in which people are peaceful and agree with each other, or when things seem right or suitable together.

mcqs.q: What does 'cherish' mean?
options: To hit quickly with the hand
To move on a current of air
To keep hopes, memories or ideas in your mind because they are important to you
mcqs.why: To cherish means to keep hopes, memories or ideas in your mind because they are important to you and bring you pleasure, as we should cherish good deeds.

mcqs.q: Who saved Farida from drowning, and where?
options: Mary saved her at the oasis
The villagers saved her in the flood
mcqs.why: Mary saved Farida from drowning: at the oasis both girls were bathing, Farida began to drown, and Mary rushed to her and saved her.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, when is God willing to forgive us?
options: When we take revenge on others
When we come to Him and say we are sorry
mcqs.why: The lesson tells us that God is ready and willing to forgive us when we come to Him and say we are sorry for our sins.

mcqs.q: When we forgive someone, what does it mean?
options: It means what they did was right
It does not mean what they did was right
It means we must take revenge later
It means we should never speak to them
mcqs.why: The true/false exercise marks it false that forgiving means what the person did was right; forgiveness releases anger but does not make the wrong act right.

mcqs.q: What should we change our hate and anger into, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The lesson teaches that the statement is true: we should change our hate and anger into love and forgiveness, just as God forgives all of our sins.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary B — Use dictionary to find word definition, pronunciation, and syllable division of the following words

  • Q: secure
    Ans: Definition: safe and protected; not likely to be lost or stolen. Pronunciation: si-KYOOR. Syllable division: se-cure (2 syllables).
  • Q: small
    Ans: Definition: not large in size, amount or degree. Pronunciation: smawl. Syllable division: small (1 syllable).
  • Q: thick
    Ans: Definition: having a large distance between the two opposite sides; solid and dense. Pronunciation: thik. Syllable division: thick (1 syllable).
  • Q: quiet
    Ans: Definition: making very little noise; peaceful and calm. Pronunciation: KWY-ut. Syllable division: qui-et (2 syllables).
  • Q: free
    Ans: Definition: not controlled by anyone else; able to do what one wants; costing nothing. Pronunciation: free. Syllable division: free (1 syllable).
  • Q: lonely
    Ans: Definition: unhappy because one is alone and has no friends or company. Pronunciation: LOHN-lee. Syllable division: lone-ly (2 syllables).
  • Q: obedient
    Ans: Definition: ready and willing to do what a person in authority tells one to do. Pronunciation: uh-BEE-dee-unt. Syllable division: o-be-di-ent (4 syllables).
  • Q: attentive
    Ans: Definition: listening, watching or thinking carefully; paying close attention. Pronunciation: uh-TEN-tiv. Syllable division: at-ten-tive (3 syllables).

Grammar A — Form words with the given clusters in initial position

  • Q: Q1. Form words with the cluster 'scr' in initial position.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A — Develop a story using the following situation

  • Q: Develop a story using the following situation: "One student is playing a game, and he loses his temper when he doesn't win. He apologizes to the other students playing the game, and they forgive him."
    Ans: The Lost Temper Ali was playing a game of cricket with his classmates during the break. He was batting well, but at last he got out and his team lost the match. Ali became very angry. He threw his bat on the ground and shouted at his friends. He blamed the bowler and the fielders for the defeat. His friends felt hurt and walked away in silence. On his way home, Ali thought about his behaviour. He felt sorry and ashamed of what he had done. He knew that losing a game is a part of playing, and his anger had spoiled everyone's fun. The next day he went to his friends and said sorry to them from his heart. He promised that he would never lose his temper again. His friends smiled and forgave him at once. They said that everyone makes mistakes, and a true friend is one who accepts his mistake. Ali thanked them, and from that day he played every game with patience and good manners. He had learnt that forgiveness makes friendship stronger.

mcqs.q: What game was Ali playing with his classmates in the story 'The Lost Temper'?
mcqs.why: In the developed story, Ali was playing a game of cricket with his classmates during the break when he lost his temper.

mcqs.q: Why did Ali lose his temper?
options: His bat was broken by a friend
He got out and his team lost the match
His friends refused to play with him
The bowler arrived late for the game
mcqs.why: Ali was batting well, but at last he got out and his team lost the match, and this defeat made him become very angry.

mcqs.q: What did Ali do in his anger?
options: He thanked his friends and went home
He threw his bat on the ground and shouted at his friends
He quietly left the ground alone
He asked the teacher for help
mcqs.why: In anger Ali threw his bat on the ground and shouted at his friends, blaming the bowler and the fielders for the defeat.

mcqs.q: How did Ali's friends react when he shouted at them?
options: They shouted back at him loudly
They felt hurt and walked away in silence
They forgave him at once on the ground
mcqs.why: Ali's friends felt hurt by his behaviour and walked away in silence, which made Ali think about what he had done.

mcqs.q: How did Ali feel about his behaviour on his way home?
mcqs.why: On his way home Ali thought about his behaviour and felt sorry and ashamed, knowing that his anger had spoiled everyone's fun.

mcqs.q: What did Ali realise about losing a game?
options: Losing a game is a part of playing
Losing means friends are at fault
A player should never accept defeat
mcqs.why: Ali realised that losing a game is a part of playing, and that his anger, not the defeat itself, had spoiled everyone's fun.

mcqs.q: What did Ali do the next day?
options: He avoided his friends all day
He bought a new bat for himself
He went to his friends and said sorry to them from his heart
He blamed the fielders once again
mcqs.why: The next day Ali went to his friends and said sorry to them from his heart, promising that he would never lose his temper again.

mcqs.q: What promise did Ali make to his friends?
options: That he would win every match
That he would never lose his temper again
That he would stop playing cricket
That he would become the team captain
mcqs.why: While apologising, Ali promised his friends that he would never lose his temper again during a game.

mcqs.q: How did Ali's friends respond to his apology?
options: They smiled and forgave him at once
They walked away in silence again
They asked him to leave the team
mcqs.why: His friends smiled and forgave him at once, saying that everyone makes mistakes and a true friend is one who accepts his mistake.

mcqs.q: What lesson did Ali learn at the end of the story?
options: A lost game must always be replayed
mcqs.why: Ali thanked his friends and played with patience and good manners after learning that forgiveness makes friendship stronger.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Role play: Carry out a role play on the following situations

  • Q: Q1. Your friend accidentally broke your favourite toy.
    Ans: Model role play: Friend: Oh no! I have broken your favourite toy car. I am really sorry, it fell from my hands by accident. Me: It was my favourite toy, but I know you did not do it on purpose. It is all right, I forgive you. Friend: Thank you for understanding me.
  • Q: Q2. You did something you feel is very bad (forgiving yourself).
    Ans: Model role play: Me: I did a very bad thing today and I feel ashamed of myself. Friend: Everyone makes mistakes. What matters is that you feel sorry for it. Me: You are right. I will say sorry to the person I hurt, forgive myself, and try never to repeat it.
  • Q: Q3. Your brother takes something of yours without asking.
    Ans: Model role play: Me: Brother, you took my pen without asking me. You should have asked first. Brother: I am sorry, I needed it in a hurry and forgot to ask you. Me: It is okay this time, but please ask me before taking my things next time.
  • Q: Q4. Your friend got angry and said something unkind to you and then apologized.
    Ans: Model role play: Friend: I am sorry I spoke unkind words to you in anger. Please forgive me. Me: Your words hurt me, but I accept your apology. I forgive you, and I hope we shall remain good friends. Friend: Thank you. I promise to control my anger next time.
  • Q: Q5. Someone keeps doing something hurtful to you over and over without being sorry.
    Ans: Model role play: Me: You keep hurting me again and again and you are never sorry. I let go of my anger, but I must also protect myself. Friend: What do you mean? Me: I will stay away from you and will not give you another chance to hurt me. Respect for myself and justice are as important as forgiveness.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q. Examine the following set of pictures and say what is the common point between them.
    Ans: The common point between all the pictures is children. In every picture there are young children, and instead of enjoying a normal, carefree childhood and going to school, these deprived children are shown working or living in poverty. All the pictures point to the same problem: child labour.

Glossary

  • Q: Give the meaning of 'prevalent'.
    Ans: existing very commonly or happening often
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'deficiency'.
    Ans: a state of not having enough of something that is needed
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'conducted'.
    Ans: to organize and perform a particular activity
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'vocational'.
    Ans: relating to occupation / employment
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'accelerate'.
    Ans: increase in rate, amount or extent
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'UNESCO'.
    Ans: abbreviation for United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'menace'.
    Ans: something that is likely to cause harm
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'eliminating'.
    Ans: to remove or take away someone or something

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. How do you know that many people are insensitive to the problem of child labour?
    Ans: We know this from the passage itself: child labour is prevalent throughout Pakistan and children are openly used in the Textile Industry and the Sports Goods Industry, yet the practice has continued and even increased since 1960. Factory owners keep employing children to lower labour costs, and millions of deprived children have never known a normal, carefree childhood. If people were truly sensitive to the problem, child labour could not go on increasing in this way.
  • Q: Q2. What does the government do to help child labourers? What happens to those schemes?
    Ans: The passage does not describe any government scheme for child labourers. The only remedy it names is 'Right to Education', which can accelerate eliminating the menace of child labour and can ensure that every child achieves his full potential. The passage says the Education System in Pakistan is deficient and the educational facilities in small cities are so poor and insufficient that parents have no motivation to send their children to schools.
  • Q: Q3. Name the fields that employ child labourer?
    Ans: The fields named in the passage are the Textile Industry and the Sports Goods Industry of Pakistan. The worst cases of child labour occur in the carpet industry and the soccer ball industry. In Sialkot, children engage in football stitching, and children as young as seven years of age spend days stitching footballs and boxing and cricket gloves for export.
  • Q: Q4. Childhood is bitter phase for these children. Why?
    Ans: Childhood is a bitter phase for these children because they have never known a normal, carefree childhood. Child labour damages, spoils and destroys their future. Instead of going to school, they are sent to work in factories in harmful conditions so that they can add to the family income, and in this way the age of play and learning is spent in hard labour.
  • Q: Q5. What steps have to be taken to eliminate the problem?
    Ans: According to the passage, 'Right to Education' can accelerate eliminating the menace of child labour and can ensure that every child achieves his full potential. For this, the deficiency of the Education System in Pakistan must be removed and proper educational facilities must be provided, especially in small cities, so that parents are motivated to send their children to schools instead of sending them to work in the factories.
  • Q: Q6. What is the link between poverty and child labour?
    Ans: Poverty is by far the most important reason for the use of child labour in Pakistan's manufacturing industry. The majority of the families in Pakistan lie below the poverty line, which leaves them with no option but to send their children to work so that they can add to the family income. In this way poverty directly pushes children into labour.
  • Q: Q7. What are the advantages for the child's family when he or she works?
    Ans: When the child works, he or she adds to the family income, which helps the poor family that lies below the poverty line. In Sialkot, children engaged in football stitching also learn vocational skills that help them earn a living, so the family sees work as a more viable option than acquiring education.

Comprehension — B. Use the following phrases in sentences of your own

  • Q: Use 'heart-rending' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: It was a heart-rending sight to see a seven-year-old child stitching footballs instead of going to school.
  • Q: Use 'amidst much' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Amidst much noise and dust, the little boy went on working in the carpet factory.
  • Q: Use 'much publicized' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: The much publicized campaign against child labour has not yet ended this menace.
  • Q: Use 'desired results' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Unless the laws are strictly enforced, the campaign against child labour will not give the desired results.
  • Q: Use 'eliminate the menace' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Free and compulsory education is the surest way to eliminate the menace of child labour from our country.
  • Q: Use 'achieve one's full potential' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Every child should get a proper education so that he can achieve his full potential.
  • Q: Use 'to strike at the roots of' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: To end child labour, we must strike at the roots of poverty and illiteracy.

Comprehension — C. Find the words in the passage that mean the same as the following

  • Q: Q1. points at which flow is constricted
    Ans: No word with this meaning occurs in the printed passage on pages 165–166. (This question appears to belong to a longer original version of the passage.)
  • Q: Q2. having skill in handling things
    Ans: No word with this meaning occurs in the printed passage on pages 165–166. (This question appears to belong to a longer original version of the passage.)
  • Q: Q3. risky
    Ans: No word with this meaning occurs in the printed passage on pages 165–166. The passage only describes the work as being done in harmful conditions. (This question appears to belong to a longer original version of the passage.)
  • Q: Q4. move faster
    Ans: accelerate — 'Right to Education' can accelerate eliminating the menace of child labour.

Comprehension — D. Use the following determiners and fill in the blanks

  • Q: ______ childhood is spent in terrible conditions.
    Ans: Their
  • Q: ______ of children work in harmful conditions.
    Ans: Thousands
  • Q: It is ______ a torture for them.
    Ans: quite
  • Q: They work in ______ bad conditions.
    Ans: such
  • Q: There is ______ change in living condition of child labourers.
    Ans: little
  • Q: Is there ______ hope of ______ bright future for them?
    Ans: any / a
  • Q: ______ responsibility is it?
    Ans: Whose
  • Q: There are ______ of child labourers in ______ world.
    Ans: many / the

mcqs.q: What is the common point between the pictures shown before the lesson?
options: Young children enjoying games at school
Young children working or living in poverty instead of enjoying a carefree childhood and going to school
Farmers sowing seeds in their fields
Scouts camping in a green valley

mcqs.q: What does the word 'prevalent' mean?
options: Very rare and hard to find
Existing very commonly or happening often
mcqs.why: The glossary gives 'prevalent' as existing very commonly or happening often, which fits the passage saying child labour is prevalent throughout Pakistan.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'deficiency' mean?
options: A state of not having enough of something that is needed
A plan made by the government
mcqs.why: The glossary defines 'deficiency' as a state of not having enough of something that is needed, and the passage uses it for the deficient education system in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Which two industries are named in the passage as using child labour in Pakistan?
options: The steel industry and the railway industry
The airline industry and the ship industry
The oil industry and the coal industry
The Textile Industry and the Sports Goods Industry
mcqs.why: The passage says child labour is prevalent throughout Pakistan and children are openly used in the Textile Industry and the Sports Goods Industry.

mcqs.q: Where do the worst cases of child labour occur, according to the passage?
options: In the carpet industry and the soccer ball industry
mcqs.why: The notes state that the worst cases of child labour occur in the carpet industry and the soccer ball industry, with children in Sialkot stitching footballs.

mcqs.q: How old are some of the children who stitch footballs in Sialkot?
options: As young as seven years of age

options: Poverty, because most families lie below the poverty line
